title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
思而得固天不為限量而縱之將為生知之聖焉勉
而中者若天限量之也夫子則不勉而中實天不為
限量而縱之將為安行之聖焉天既縱夫聖德故凡
事之大者洞達小者亦罔不達而自兼乎多能也事
之精者貫通粗者亦無不通而自該乎多能也子貢
之答如此蓋謂聖不止於多能由本而該末也吁以
子貢之知猶謙若不敢知而曰將聖彼大宰者曷足
以知之哉大抵德為本也才為末也夫子才德兼全
本末具備多能豈足以語其聖邪及夫子聞之曰君
===
子多乎哉不多也其意亦因可見矣若子貢誠可謂
知足以知聖人者歟
子庶民則百姓勸來百工則財用足柔遠人則
四方歸之懷諸侯則天下畏之
廖𤣱
同考試官教諭謝批此題本是常道施於國與天
下之效場中作者泛泛不切此
作文典古而理明白表出為宜
考試官教諭陳批辭不繁而意自足非老筆不能到
punctuated:
思而得，固天不為限量而縱之，將為生知之聖焉；勉而中者，若天限量之也，夫子則不勉而中，實天不為限量而縱之，將為安行之聖焉。天既縱夫聖德，故凡事之大者洞達，小者亦罔不達，而自兼乎多能也；事之精者貫通，粗者亦無不通，而自該乎多能也。子貢之答如此，蓋謂聖不止於多能，由本而該末也。吁！以子貢之知，猶謙若不敢知，而曰「將聖」，彼大宰者，曷足以知之哉？大抵德為本也，才為末也。夫子才德兼全，本末具備，多能豈足以語其聖邪？及夫子聞之，曰：「君子多乎哉？不多也。」其意亦因可見矣。若子貢，誠可謂知足以知聖人者歟！

「子庶民則百姓勸，來百工則財用足，柔遠人則四方歸之，懷諸侯則天下畏之。」
廖𤣱
同考試官教諭謝批：此題本是常道施於國與天下之效，場中作者泛泛不切，此作文典古而理明白，表出為宜。
考試官教諭陳批：辭不繁而意自足，非老筆不能到。
translation_en:
… thinking before attaining it, whereas for the Master, he attains it without thinking; indeed, Heaven has set no limit upon him and has given him free rein to be a sage born with knowledge. Those who hit the mark only through effort are as though limited by Heaven, whereas for the Master, he hits the mark without effort; truly, Heaven has set no limit upon him and has given him free rein to be a sage who practices with ease. Since Heaven has given free rein to his sagely virtue, in all affairs he thoroughly comprehends the great and fails to comprehend nothing of the small, thus naturally combining many abilities; in all affairs he penetrates the subtle and fails to master nothing of the coarse, thus naturally encompassing many abilities. Such was Zigong's reply, meaning that sagehood does not stop at having many abilities, but proceeds from the fundamental to encompass the incidental. Ah! Even with Zigong's wisdom, he remained humble as though not daring to claim full knowledge, saying "almost a sage"—how could that Grand宰 (Taizai) be capable of understanding him? In general, virtue is the root, and talent is the branch. The Master was complete in both talent and virtue, fully equipped in both root and branch; how could having many abilities suffice to describe his sagehood? When the Master heard of it, he said, "Does the gentleman have many abilities? No, he does not have many." From this, his meaning can also be seen. As for Zigong, can he not truly be called one whose wisdom was sufficient to know a sage!

"Treat the common people as one's children, and the hundred surnames will be encouraged; attract the hundred artisans, and wealth and resources will be sufficient; be gracious to men from afar, and the four quarters will turn to him; cherish the feudal lords, and all under Heaven will hold him in awe."
By Liao Xuan 廖𤣱.
Associate Examiner Instructor Xie comments: This topic is fundamentally about the effects of applying the constant Way to the state and to all under Heaven. The candidates in the examination hall wrote vaguely and missed the point, whereas this essay is classical in style and clear in principle; it is fitting to set it forth as a model.
Examiner Instructor Chen comments: The words are not prolix, yet the meaning is naturally complete; none but a seasoned brush could achieve this.

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭張批粹乎理而瑩乎文讀之無不
快意者
常道施於國者有其效常道施於天下者亦有其效
夫治國平天下必有不易之常道也然常道既盡於
上則其效豈不以類而應哉中庸二十章子思引夫
子答哀公之問政若曰人君為國必有常道焉是故
於庶民也愛之如子而時其徭役薄其稅斂則人皆
尊君親上趨事赴工而百姓勸矣於百工也加意招
徠而日省月試既稟稱事則人皆通工易事農末相
===
資而財用足矣此則常道施於國者之效也由國以
及天下而治之亦必有常道焉是故於遠人也則為
之授節以送往豐其委積以迎來善者嘉之而不能
者矜之是則寬以柔之者至矣由是天下之旅皆悅
而願出於其塗四方有不歸乎於諸侯也則繼絕舉
廢而治亂持危朝聘以時而厚往薄來是則恩以懷
之者厚矣由是德之所施者博威之所制者廣天下
有不畏乎此又常道施於天下者之效也大抵哀公
問政而夫子告之以九經則為治之道盡矣然有九
punctuated:
考試官教諭張批：粹乎理而瑩乎文，讀之無不快意者。

常道施於國者有其效，常道施於天下者亦有其效。夫治國平天下，必有不易之常道也。然常道既盡於上，則其效豈不以類而應哉？《中庸》二十章，子思引夫子答哀公之問政，若曰：人君為國，必有常道焉。是故於庶民也，愛之如子，而時其徭役，薄其稅斂，則人皆尊君親上，趨事赴工，而百姓勸矣；於百工也，加意招徠，而日省月試，既稟稱事，則人皆通工易事，農末相資，而財用足矣。此則常道施於國者之效也。由國以及天下而治之，亦必有常道焉。是故於遠人也，則為之授節以送往，豐其委積以迎來，善者嘉之而不能者矜之，是則寬以柔之者至矣，由是天下之旅皆悅而願出於其塗，四方有不歸乎？於諸侯也，則繼絕舉廢而治亂持危，朝聘以時而厚往薄來，是則恩以懷之者厚矣，由是德之所施者博，威之所制者廣，天下有不畏乎？此又常道施於天下者之效也。大抵哀公問政，而夫子告之以九經，則為治之道盡矣。然有九
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Zhang 張 comments: Pure in principle and lustrous in style; no one who reads it can fail to be delighted.

When the constant Way is applied to the state, it has its effect; when the constant Way is applied to all under Heaven, it likewise has its effect. Now in governing the state and bringing peace to all under Heaven, there must be an unchanging, constant Way. Yet once the constant Way is fully realized above, how could its effects fail to respond each according to its kind? In the twentieth chapter of the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong), Zisi 子思 cites the Master's reply to Duke Ai's 哀公 question about governance, as if to say: When a ruler governs a state, there must be a constant Way. Therefore, with regard to the common people, if he loves them like children, employs their corvée labor only at the proper seasons, and makes their taxes and levies light, then everyone will honor the ruler and feel affection for their superiors, hastening to their tasks and works, and the hundred surnames will be encouraged. With regard to the hundred artisans, if he takes care to attract them, examining them daily and testing them monthly, with rations proportionate to their work, then everyone will exchange the products of their labor and trade services, agriculture and crafts will mutually support one another, and wealth and resources will be sufficient. This, then, is the effect of the constant Way as applied to the state. In extending governance from the state to all under Heaven, there must likewise be a constant Way. Therefore, with regard to people from afar, if he grants them tallies to escort them on their departure and makes abundant their provisions to welcome them on their arrival, commending the good and showing compassion for the incapable, then his leniency ingentling them is complete. Consequently, all travelers under Heaven will be pleased and wish to travel upon his roads—will the four quarters not turn to him in allegiance? With regard to the feudal lords, if he restores broken lineages and revives abolished states, brings order to chaos and supports those in peril, receives court visits and missions at the proper times, and sends them off with generous gifts while requiring only meager tribute on their arrival, then his grace in cherishing them is profound. Consequently, the reach of the virtue he bestows is broad, and the scope of the awe he commands is vast—will all under Heaven not stand in awe of him? This, in turn, is the effect of the constant Way as applied to all under Heaven. On the whole, when Duke Ai asked about governance and the Master instructed him with the Nine Standard Rules (jiujing 九經), the Way of governing was exhausted therein. Yet among the Nine…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
經之序有九經之事而此則九經之效也且治道固
不外乎九經而九經則皆本於脩身約而言之則又
本乎誠而已矣中庸引之以繼大舜文武周公之緒
明其所傳之一致舉而措之亦猶是爾吁旨哉
易義
進得位往有功也進以正可以正邦也
韓章
同考試官訓導周批〔作此題者有以卦體言有以君臣言紛紛不一晚得是篇發〕
===
〔明夫子以卦變釋利貞之意殆無餘蘊是宜錄出〕
考試官教諭陳批〔深得潔靜精微之旨可羨可羨〕
考試官教諭張批〔詞贍理明佳作也〕
唯剛進得位之正故所往獲效之大夫陽剛之進固
在得乎位尤在以其正惟漸之時而進得乎位之正
宜乎獲效之大也聖人即卦變而釋利貞之意厥旨
微矣且夫漸之為卦合艮巽而成體文王既繫以利
貞之辭矣至吾夫子傳彖又從而釋其辭蓋謂是卦
punctuated:
經之序，有九經之事，而此則九經之效也。且治道固不外乎九經，而九經則皆本於脩身，約而言之，則又本乎誠而已矣。《中庸》引之，以繼大舜、文、武、周公之緒，明其所傳之一致，舉而措之，亦猶是爾。吁！旨哉！

易義

「進得位，往有功也；進以正，可以正邦也。」
韓章
同考試官訓導周批：〔作此題者，有以卦體言，有以君臣言，紛紛不一。晚得是篇，發〕〔明夫子以卦變釋「利貞」之意，殆無餘蘊，是宜錄出。〕
考試官教諭陳批：〔深得潔靜精微之旨，可羨可羨！〕
考試官教諭張批：〔詞贍理明，佳作也。〕

唯剛進得位之正，故所往獲效之大。夫陽剛之進，固在得乎位，尤在以其正。惟漸之時，而進得乎位之正，宜乎獲效之大也。聖人即卦變而釋「利貞」之意，厥旨微矣。且夫漸之為卦，合艮、巽而成體，文王既繫以「利貞」之辭矣。至吾夫子傳《彖》，又從而釋其辭，蓋謂是卦
translation_en:
… the sequence of the Nine Standard Rules, and there are the affairs of the Nine Standard Rules, whereas this is the efficacy of the Nine Standard Rules. Moreover, the way of governance certainly does not lie outside the Nine Standard Rules, and the Nine Standard Rules are all rooted in cultivating the person; speaking of it concisely, it is in turn rooted in nothing more than sincerity. The Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) cites this to continue the heritage of the Great Shun, King Wen, King Wu, and the Duke of Zhou, making clear the unity of what was transmitted; to take it up and put it into practice is just like this. Ah, how profound in meaning!

Expositions on the Book of Changes

"Advancing and attaining position, going forth brings merit; advancing with correctness, one can rectify the state."

By Han Zhang 韓章.

Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Zhou 周: [Among those who wrote on this topic, some spoke in terms of the constituent trigrams of the hexagram, and some spoke in terms of ruler and minister, all varied and inconsistent. Late in the grading I obtained this essay, which elucidates the Master's intent in explaining "advantageous to be correct and firm" through hexagram alteration, leaving almost nothing unexpressed. It is fitting to record and publish it.]
Comment by Examiner Instructor Chen 陳: [It deeply grasps the purport of purity, stillness, and subtle refinement—admirable, admirable!]
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zhang 張: [Rich in diction and clear in principle; a fine work.]

Only when the strong advances and attains the correctness of position does its going forth achieve great efficacy. Now, the advance of yang strength certainly lies in attaining position, and even more so in doing so with correctness. Only at the time of Gradual Development (Jian), when advancing to attain the correctness of position, is it fitting that the efficacy achieved is great. When the Sage examined the hexagram alteration to explain the meaning of "advantageous to be correct and firm," his purport was subtle indeed. Moreover, as a hexagram, Gradual Development combines the trigrams Gen and Xun to form its structure, and King Wen had already appended to it the words "advantageous to be correct and firm." When our Master wrote the Commentary on the Judgments (Tuanzhuan), he went on to explain those words, saying in effect that the …

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之變自渙而來者九本居二則陽居乎陰位未得其
宜也今則進居于艮體之三是進得其位矣然進不
徒進進必有功所謂其行次且者何有焉自旅而來
者九本居四則剛處乎柔位未得其當也今則進居
于巽體之五是往得其位矣然往不徒往往則有尚
所謂困于臲卼者无有焉然人但知三與五之進得
乎位而有功而不知三之進也以陽居陽所進者正
而无一行之偏詖于焉以之脩政而政无不舉以之
立事而事无不成其與當位貞吉以正邦者同一揆
===
矣五之進也以剛履剛所往者正而无一事之邪僻
于焉以之正百官而百官无不正以之正萬民而萬
民无不服其與說而巽孚乃化邦者无二致矣愚故
曰唯剛進得位之正故所往獲效之大者以此抑觀
文王繫漸之辭以利貞者本言女之歸也利於正而
夫子傳彖又推言君子之進也亦以正蓋女之歸君
子之進同一理也女歸不以正則見金夫不有躬矣
君子之進不以正則枉道徇人徒為失巳矣然則聖
人於漸其以敦風化乎
punctuated: 之變，自渙而來者，九本居二，則陽居乎陰，位未得其宜也；今則進居于艮體之三，是進得其位矣。然進不徒進，進必有功，所謂「其行次且」者，何有焉？自旅而來者，九本居四，則剛處乎柔，位未得其當也；今則進居于巽體之五，是往得其位矣。然往不徒往，往則有尚，所謂「困于臲卼」者，无有焉。然人但知三與五之進得乎位而有功，而不知三之進也，以陽居陽，所進者正，而无一行之偏詖；于焉以之脩政而政无不舉，以之立事而事无不成，其與「當位貞吉，以正邦」者同一揆矣。五之進也，以剛履剛，所往者正，而无一事之邪僻；于焉以之正百官而百官无不正，以之正萬民而萬民无不服，其與「說而巽，孚乃化邦」者无二致矣。愚故曰：「唯剛進得位之正，故所往獲效之大」者，以此。抑觀文王繫漸之辭以「利貞」者，本言女之歸也利於正；而夫子傳《彖》，又推言君子之進也亦以正。蓋女之歸、君子之進，同一理也。女歸不以正，則「見金夫，不有躬」矣；君子之進不以正，則枉道徇人，徒為失巳矣。然則聖人於漸，其以敦風化乎！
translation_en: … transformation: where it comes from the Huan (Dispersion) hexagram, the yang line originally resided in the second place, meaning that yang occupied a yin position and the place had not yet attained its appropriateness; now, however, it advances to reside in the third place of the lower trigram Gen (Keeping Still), which is "advancing and attaining its proper place." Yet its advance is not a mere advance—advancing, it will surely achieve merit; what is there of the so-called "walking haltingly"? Where it comes from the Lü (Wanderer) hexagram, the yang line originally resided in the fourth place, meaning that the firm occupied a yielding position and the place had not yet attained its fitness; now, however, it advances to reside in the fifth place of the upper trigram Xun (Gentle), which is "going forward and attaining its proper place." Yet its going forward is not a mere going forward—going forward, it has merit; there is nothing of the so-called "distress on a perilous height." Still, people only know that the third and fifth lines advance to attain their proper places and achieve merit, without knowing that in the advance of the third line, yang occupies a yang position, so what advances is upright and without a single biased or perverse action. Thereby, when one uses it to cultivate governance, no aspect of governance fails to be raised up; when one uses it to establish affairs, no affair fails to be accomplished—it follows the very same principle as "being in the proper place, correct and auspicious, so as to rectify the state." And in the advance of the fifth line, the firm treads upon a firm position, so its going forward is upright and without a single depraved or perverse affair. Thereby, when one uses it to rectify the hundred officials, none of the hundred officials fails to be rectified; when one uses it to rectify the myriad people, none of the myriad people fails to submit—it is no different in effect from "joyous and gentle, sincere and thus transforming the state." This is why I say: "Only because the firm advances and attains the correctness of its position does its going forward reap great efficacy." Moreover, looking at King Wen's attaching the phrase "advantageous to be correct and firm" to the Jian (Gradual Development) hexagram, he originally spoke of how a woman's marriage finds advantage in correctness; yet when the Master [Confucius] wrote the Commentary on the Judgments (Tuanzhuan), he extended the meaning to say that the advance of the noble man is likewise through correctness. Indeed, the marriage of a woman and the advance of a noble man share the exact same principle. If a woman marries without correctness, then "she sees a man with money and loses possession of herself"; if a noble man advances without correctness, he bends the Way to accommodate others and merely loses himself in vain. If that is so, then in the Jian hexagram, did the sages not intend to thicken moral customs and transformation!

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
動萬物者莫疾乎雷撓萬物者莫疾乎風燥萬
物者莫熯乎火說萬物者莫說乎澤潤萬
物者莫潤乎水終萬物始萬物者莫盛乎
艮故水火相逮雷風不相悖山澤通氣
梁建中
同考試官訓導周批說出先天後天之體用親切簡
當非熟於易者不能宜為多士
之冠
考試官教諭陳批辭旨俱贍超於眾作宜表多士
===
考試官教諭張批理趣精到宜冠本經
聖人論後天造化流行之用必原先天造化對待之
體蓋對待者造化流行之本體流行者造化對待之
妙用孰謂後天之造化而不原於先天之造化也歟
試以後天造化言之震居東方其象為雷而時乎春
故鼓動萬物者莫疾乎雷焉巽居東南其象為風而
當春夏之交故撓亂萬物者莫疾乎風焉象為火而
居南者離也而時乎夏故晅燥萬物者莫有熯於火
也象為澤而居西者兌也而時乎秋故說遂萬物者
punctuated:
動萬物者莫疾乎雷，撓萬物者莫疾乎風，燥萬物者莫熯乎火，說萬物者莫說乎澤，潤萬物者莫潤乎水，終萬物始萬物者莫盛乎艮。故水火相逮，雷風不相悖，山澤通氣。
梁建中
同考試官訓導周批：說出先天後天之體用，親切簡當，非熟於《易》者不能，宜為多士之冠。
考試官教諭陳批：辭旨俱贍，超於眾作，宜表多士。
考試官教諭張批：理趣精到，宜冠本經。
聖人論後天造化流行之用，必原先天造化對待之體。蓋對待者，造化流行之本體；流行者，造化對待之妙用。孰謂後天之造化而不原於先天之造化也歟？試以後天造化言之：震居東方，其象為雷，而時乎春，故鼓動萬物者莫疾乎雷焉。巽居東南，其象為風，而當春夏之交，故撓亂萬物者莫疾乎風焉。象為火而居南者，離也，而時乎夏，故晅燥萬物者莫有熯於火也。象為澤而居西者，兌也，而時乎秋，故說遂萬物者
translation_en:
"Nothing stirs up the myriad things more rapidly than thunder; nothing bends the myriad things more rapidly than wind; nothing parches the myriad things more fiercely than fire; nothing gladdens the myriad things more delightfully than the marsh; nothing moistens the myriad things more thoroughly than water; nothing brings the myriad things to an end and gives them a new beginning more flourishingly than Gen [keeping still / the mountain]. Therefore, water and fire reach each other, thunder and wind do not conflict with each other, and mountain and marsh communicate their vital breaths."

Liang Jianzhong 梁建中

Comment by Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Zhou 周: He articulates the substance and function of the Prior-to-Heaven and Posterior-to-Heaven arrangements in a way that is intimate, concise, and apt. None who is not thoroughly versed in the Book of Changes (Yi 易) could have achieved this; he deserves to be placed at the head of the many scholars.

Comment by Examiner, Instructor Chen 陳: Both diction and purport are rich and abundant, surpassing the compositions of the crowd; it deserves to stand as a model for the many scholars.

Comment by Examiner, Instructor Zhang 張: Its grasp of principle and import is refined and thorough; it deserves to stand first in this Classic.

When the Sage discusses the flowing function of creation's transformations in the Posterior-to-Heaven (houtian 後天) order, he necessarily traces it back to the paired substance of creation's transformations in the Prior-to-Heaven (xiantian 先天) order. For pairing in opposition is the fundamental substance of creation's flowing movement, while flowing movement is the wondrous function of creation's pairing in opposition. Who could say that the transformations of the Posterior-to-Heaven order do not originate in the transformations of the Prior-to-Heaven order?

Let us try to speak of it in terms of the transformations of the Posterior-to-Heaven order: Zhen 震 resides in the east; its image is thunder, and its season is spring; therefore, in stirring and rousing the myriad things, nothing is more rapid than thunder. Xun 巽 resides in the southeast; its image is wind, and it corresponds to the juncture of spring and summer; therefore, in bending and agitating the myriad things, nothing is more rapid than wind. That whose image is fire and which resides in the south is Li 離, and its season is summer; therefore, in warming and parching the myriad things, nothing is more fiercely drying than fire. That whose image is the marsh and which resides in the west is Dui 兌, and its season is autumn; therefore, in gladdening and fulfilling the myriad things, …

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
孰有說於澤也至於坎居北方而時乎冬故滋潤萬
物者孰有潤於坎水乎艮居東北而當冬春之交故
終始萬物者孰有盛於艮止乎後天造化流行之用
如此豈不原於先天造化對待之體乎是故以先天
卦位觀之坎爲水而居西離爲火而居東坎離相對
得其偶則水火不相射而暵潤之功成矣震爲雷而
居東北巽爲風而居西南震巽相對得其偶則雷風
不相悖而動撓之功成矣至於艮居西北而爲山兌
居東南而爲澤所以成終成始而說萬物者豈不由
===
於艮兌相對之得其偶而山澤之通氣乎說卦聖人
由後天之易而原夫先天之易者可見其體用一原
莫非神之所爲也抑考前章論六子則兼乾坤而言
之此不言乾坤而專言六子者豈非乾坤其始任六
子以成功及其終也六子成其功以歸於乾坤乾坤
則有不與者乎此又學易者所當知
書義
天工人其代之天叙有典勅我五典五惇哉天
秩有禮自我五禮有庸哉同寅協恭和衷哉
punctuated:
孰有說於澤也？至於坎居北方而時乎冬，故滋潤萬物者，孰有潤於坎水乎？艮居東北而當冬春之交，故終始萬物者，孰有盛於艮止乎？後天造化流行之用如此，豈不原於先天造化對待之體乎？是故以先天卦位觀之：坎爲水而居西，離爲火而居東，坎離相對得其偶，則水火不相射，而暵潤之功成矣；震爲雷而居東北，巽爲風而居西南，震巽相對得其偶，則雷風不相悖，而動撓之功成矣；至於艮居西北而爲山，兌居東南而爲澤，所以成終成始而說萬物者，豈不由於艮兌相對之得其偶，而山澤之通氣乎？《說卦》聖人由後天之《易》而原夫先天之《易》者，可見其體用一原，莫非神之所爲也。抑考前章論六子，則兼乾坤而言之；此不言乾坤而專言六子者，豈非乾坤其始任六子以成功，及其終也，六子成其功以歸於乾坤，乾坤則有不與者乎？此又學《易》者所當知。

書義
天工人其代之。天叙有典，勅我五典五惇哉！天秩有禮，自我五禮有庸哉！同寅協恭，和衷哉！
translation_en:
…what brings them greater joy than the marsh? As for Kan, it occupies the north and corresponds in season to winter; therefore, in nourishing and moistening the myriad things, what is more moistening than the water of Kan? Gen occupies the northeast and corresponds to the transition between winter and spring; therefore, in bringing the myriad things to an end and to a new beginning, what is more flourishing than the stopping of Gen? Since the functioning of the post-heavenly (Houtian) creative transformations in their seasonal flow is such as this, how could it not originate in the substance of the pre-heavenly (Xiantian) creative transformations in their paired opposition? Therefore, if we examine it in terms of the pre-heavenly positions of the trigrams: Kan is water and occupies the west, while Li is fire and occupies the east; Kan and Li stand opposite each other and obtain their pairing, so that water and fire do not combat each other, and the work of drying and moistening is accomplished. Zhen is thunder and occupies the northeast, while Xun is wind and occupies the southwest; Zhen and Xun stand opposite each other and obtain their pairing, so that thunder and wind do not run counter to each other, and the work of stirring and bending is accomplished. As for Gen occupying the northwest as mountain, and Dui occupying the southeast as marsh, how could that by which they bring things to completion and to a new beginning and give joy to the myriad things not result from Gen and Dui standing opposite each other to obtain their pairing, and mountain and marsh communicating their vital breaths? That the sage in the Explanation of the Trigrams (Shuogua) traced the post-heavenly Changes back to the pre-heavenly Changes shows clearly that substance and function share a single origin, and that none of this is anything other than the work of the unfathomable Spirit. Moreover, if we examine the preceding chapter where the six children [trigrams] are discussed, they are spoken of together with Qian and Kun. That here it does not mention Qian and Kun, speaking exclusively of the six children—is it not because in the beginning Qian and Kun entrust the six children with accomplishing the work, and in the end the six children accomplish their work and return the credit to Qian and Kun, while Qian and Kun themselves take no part in the toil? This too is what students of the Book of Changes ought to know.

Exposition on the Book of Documents (Shuyi)
"The work is Heaven's; it is men who must act for it. Heaven has arranged the social relationships with their invariable principles; let us set right our five invariable relationships, that all five may be generously observed! Heaven has ordained the rites in their degrees; from our five rites let there be constant practice! Together be reverent and united in respect, so as to harmonize the moral nature!…"

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天命有德五服五章哉天討有罪五刑五用
哉政事懋哉懋哉天聰明自我民聰明天明
畏自我民明威達于上下敬哉有土
廖垣
同考試官教諭謝批〔此題本長難於包括而學者往〕
〔蹈襲陳言失之太繁此作筆力遒〕
〔勁行文簡古真佳作也〕
同考試官教諭鄭批〔場中作此者不失之泛即失之畧〕
〔惟此作詞理簡當可取〕
===
考試官教諭陳批〔說出天工人代之理貫串一篇非〕
〔精於書者不能也〕
考試官教諭張批〔詞約理備非熟於本領者不〕
〔能宜錄出之〕
大臣論理天事在乎人既言政教出於天而當立本
以盡其責復言天人同一理而當主敬以臨乎民盖
代天理物者固在於人也然政教雖出於天而非君
臣之敬勉則無以盡其責天人雖同一理而非君心
之主敬又何以合而一之哉在昔皐陶陳謨於帝舜之
punctuated:
天命有德，五服五章哉！天討有罪，五刑五用哉！政事懋哉懋哉！天聰明，自我民聰明；天明畏，自我民明威。達于上下，敬哉有土！
廖垣
同考試官教諭謝批：〔此題本長，難於包括，而學者往蹈襲陳言，失之太繁。此作筆力遒勁，行文簡古，真佳作也。〕
同考試官教諭鄭批：〔場中作此者，不失之泛，即失之畧。惟此作詞理簡當，可取。〕
考試官教諭陳批：〔說出天工人代之理，貫串一篇，非精於《書》者不能也。〕
考試官教諭張批：〔詞約理備，非熟於本領者不能，宜錄出之。〕
大臣論理天事在乎人，既言政教出於天而當立本以盡其責，復言天人同一理而當主敬以臨乎民。盖代天理物者，固在於人也。然政教雖出於天，而非君臣之敬勉，則無以盡其責；天人雖同一理，而非君心之主敬，又何以合而一之哉？在昔皐陶陳謨於帝舜之
translation_en:
… "Heaven graciously distinguishes the virtuous; are there not the five habiliments, fivefold brightly distinguished? Heaven punishes the guilty; are there not the five punishments, to be fivefoldly applied? Political affairs—be strenuous, be strenuous! Heaven hears and sees as our people hear and see; Heaven brightly approves and displays its terrors as our people brightly approve and would awe. Such connection is there between the upper and lower worlds. Be reverent, O you who possess the land!"

Liao Yuan 廖垣

Associate Examiner and Instructor Xie 謝 comments: 〔This topic is inherently long and difficult to encompass, and scholars often follow clichés, erring on the side of excessive verbosity. This composition has vigorous brushwork and concise, ancient prose—truly a fine piece.〕

Associate Examiner and Instructor Zheng 鄭 comments: 〔Among those writing on this topic in the examination hall, if they do not err by being too vague, they err by being too brief. Only this composition is concise and appropriate in both wording and principle; it is worthy of selection.〕

Examiner and Instructor Chen 陳 comments: 〔It articulates the principle of men acting in the stead of Heaven's work, threading it throughout the entire piece. None but one well-versed in the Book of Documents (Shu) could accomplish this.〕

Examiner and Instructor Zhang 張 comments: 〔Concise in wording and complete in principle, none who has not mastered the fundamentals could achieve this. It ought to be transcribed and published.〕

When the great minister discusses how managing the affairs of Heaven rests with man, he first states that governance and instruction originate from Heaven and that one must establish the foundation so as to fulfill one's responsibility; he then states that Heaven and man share a single principle and that one must maintain reverence in presiding over the people. For indeed, governing things on behalf of Heaven rests with man. Yet although governance and instruction originate from Heaven, without the reverent exertion of ruler and ministers, there is no way to fulfill that responsibility; and although Heaven and man share a single principle, without the ruler's mind maintaining reverence, how could they be united as one? In antiquity, when Gao Yao 皐陶 set forth his counsels before Emperor Shun 舜…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
前若曰天下之事無一不統於君人君之事無一不
出於天天不能有為而付之君君不能獨治而任之
臣君臣所治之事雖不一無非代天而為之也是故
五典天之所叙也在我則當正之使倫叙而益厚五
禮天之所秩也在我則當用之使品秩而有常然惇
典庸禮乃人君之教化君臣當同其寅畏協其恭敬
使民彞物則各得其正則民之衷無不和矣若夫全
是衷而有德者天之所命也則制為五等之服以彰
顯之戾是衷而有罪者天之所討也則制為五等之
===
刑以懲戒之然爵賞刑罰乃人君之政事君主之臣
用之當孜孜汲汲勉力不怠則政之施無不當矣雖
然君臣敬勉固為立政敷教之本而君心主敬又豈
不可合天人而一之乎是故天之聰明未甞見其傾
耳而聽之下目而視之也因民之視聽以為聰明焉
天之明畏亦未甞見其何為而彰善何為而癉惡也
因民之好惡以為明威焉夫天人雖有上下之分理
則通達而無二天人雖有彼此之殊理則貫徹而無
間民心之所存即天理之所在人君之有天下其可
punctuated: 前，若曰：「天下之事，無一不統於君；人君之事，無一不出於天。天不能有為而付之君，君不能獨治而任之臣。君臣所治之事雖不一，無非代天而為之也。是故五典，天之所叙也，在我則當正之，使倫叙而益厚；五禮，天之所秩也，在我則當用之，使品秩而有常。然惇典庸禮，乃人君之教化，君臣當同其寅畏，協其恭敬，使民彞物則各得其正，則民之衷無不和矣。若夫全是衷而有德者，天之所命也，則制為五等之服以彰顯之；戾是衷而有罪者，天之所討也，則制為五等之刑以懲戒之。然爵賞刑罰，乃人君之政事，君主之，臣用之，當孜孜汲汲，勉力不怠，則政之施無不當矣。」雖然，君臣敬勉，固為立政敷教之本，而君心主敬，又豈不可合天人而一之乎？是故天之聰明，未甞見其傾耳而聽之、下目而視之也，因民之視聽以為聰明焉；天之明畏，亦未甞見其何為而彰善、何為而癉惡也，因民之好惡以為明威焉。夫天人雖有上下之分，理則通達而無二；天人雖有彼此之殊，理則貫徹而無間。民心之所存，即天理之所在，人君之有天下，其可
translation_en: … presence, as if to say: "Among the affairs of the world, there is not one that is not governed by the ruler; among the affairs of the ruler, there is not one that does not originate from Heaven. Because Heaven cannot take direct action, it entrusts them to the ruler; because the ruler cannot govern alone, he delegates them to his ministers. Although the affairs governed by ruler and ministers are diverse, there is none that is not carried out on behalf of Heaven. Therefore, the Five Relationships are what Heaven has arranged; it rests with us to rectify them so that the human relationships are ordered and made ever deeper. The Five Rites are what Heaven has ordained; it rests with us to employ them so that the grades and ranks remain constant. Yet giving weight to the relationships and employing the rites constitute the transformative teaching of the ruler. Ruler and ministers must share in reverent awe and unite in respectful deference, ensuring that the constant norms of the people and the rules of things each attain their proper rectitude; then the moral nature of the people will never fail to be harmonious. As for those who preserve this moral nature intact and possess virtue, they are the ones whom Heaven charges with office, and so robes of the five ranks are instituted to distinguish and honor them. As for those who violate this moral nature and commit offenses, they are the ones whom Heaven punishes, and so punishments of the five degrees are instituted to chastise and warn them. Yet conferring ranks and rewards and meting out penalties and punishments constitute the governance of the ruler. The ruler presides over them and the ministers implement them; they must be assiduous and untiring, exerting themselves without laxity, and then the administration of governance will never fail to be fitting." Even so, while the reverence and diligence of ruler and ministers are indeed the foundation for establishing governance and spreading instruction, can the ruler's mind holding fast to reverence not also unite Heaven and man into one? Therefore, as for Heaven's hearing and sight, one has never seen it incline its ear to listen or cast down its eyes to look; rather, it takes the seeing and hearing of the people as its own hearing and sight. As for Heaven'ssplendor and awe, one has likewise never seen by what act it distinguishes the good or by what act it afflicts the evil; rather, it takes the likes and dislikes of the people as its own splendor and majesty. Although Heaven and man have the distinction of above and below, their principle penetrates through both without duality; although Heaven and man have the difference of that and this, their principle runs through all without gap. Where the minds of the people abide is precisely where Heavenly principle resides. When a ruler possesses the Empire, how could he…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不知所以敬之哉苟能敬以臨其民則下可以得民
心而不忽乎民上可以得天心而不忽乎天矣是則
吾心之敬又所以合天人而一之者歟抑攷皐陶
之謨以知人安民爲一篇之體要自天叙有典而下
所以發明天工人代之意自天聰明以下所以申明
典禮命討之意於知人之餘則戒以去逸欲崇兢業
於安民之餘則戒以懋政事敬有土盖以人君一心
又知人安民之根柢此皐陶所以爲善於告君也
其不能誠于小民今休王不敢後用顧畏于民
===
嵒王來紹上帝自服于土中旦曰其作大邑
其自時配皇天毖祀于上下其自時中乂王
厥有成命治民今休
陳文
同考試官敎諭謝批此題本平易而場中作者多分
截不明且不知敬德爲和民之本
而王厥有成命治民今休爲召公之
言此作發明親切辭理兼到誠劈
經之翹楚者也一薦何忝
punctuated:
不知所以敬之哉？苟能敬以臨其民，則下可以得民心而不忽乎民，上可以得天心而不忽乎天矣。是則吾心之敬，又所以合天人而一之者歟！抑攷《皐陶之謨》，以知人、安民爲一篇之體要。自「天叙有典」而下，所以發明「天工人代」之意；自「天聰明」以下，所以申明「典禮命討」之意。於知人之餘，則戒以去逸欲、崇兢業；於安民之餘，則戒以懋政事、敬有土。盖以人君一心，又知人、安民之根柢，此皐陶所以爲善於告君也。

「其不能誠于小民，今休。王不敢後，用顧畏于民嵒。王來紹上帝，自服于土中。旦曰：『其作大邑，其自時配皇天，毖祀于上下，其自時中乂。』王厥有成命，治民今休。」

陳文
同考試官敎諭謝批：此題本平易，而場中作者多分截不明，且不知敬德爲和民之本，而「王厥有成命，治民今休」爲召公之言。此作發明親切，辭理兼到，誠劈經之翹楚者也。一薦何忝！
translation_en:
… fail to know how to revere them? If he is able to approach his people with reverence, then below he can win the hearts of the people and not neglect the people, and above he can win the heart of Heaven and not neglect Heaven. Thus, the reverence of one's own mind is what unites Heaven and humanity into one! Furthermore, if we examine the "Counsels of Gao Yao" (Gao Yao mo), it takes knowing men and bringing peace to the people as the essential substance of the entire chapter. From "Heavenly arrangements have their five social relationships" onward, it elucidates the meaning of "Heaven's work is carried out by human representatives"; from "Heaven's hearing and seeing" onward, it reiterates the meaning of "regulating the rites, conferring charges, and punishing the wicked." In addition to knowing men, he admonishes the ruler to cast aside idleness and desires and to exalt cautiousness and diligence; in addition to bringing peace to the people, he admonishes him to exert himself in affairs of government and to show reverence in possessing the territory. For the single mind of the ruler is in turn the root and foundation of knowing men and bringing peace to the people—this is why Gao Yao was so skilled at counseling his sovereign.

"Pray that the king may bring harmony to the common people, so that there be present blessing. The king must not delay, but take heed and stand in awe of the perilousness of the people. May the king come and succeed to the work of the Supreme Lord, and personally govern in the center of the land. I, Dan, say: 'Having built this great city, from here he shall be the counterpart of August Heaven, carefully sacrificing to the spirits above and below, and from here centrally govern.' Thus the king may fulfill the determinate Mandate, and in governing the people enjoy present blessing."

Chen Wen 陳文
Comment (pi) by Associate Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Xie 謝: This topic is inherently straightforward, yet most writers in the examination hall failed to divide the sections clearly; moreover, they did not realize that revering virtue is the foundation of harmonizing the people, and that the lines "Thus the king may fulfill the determinate Mandate, and in governing the people enjoy present blessing" are the words of the Duke of Shao (Shao Gong 召公). This essay elucidates the meaning intimately, achieving perfection in both diction and principle. Truly, he is an outstanding leader among those specializing in this Classic. What shame could there be in recommending it for first place!

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭鄭批場中作此題多分截不明惟此篇
明於分截且寫出周召告君忠愛
之意宛然見於言辭之表
考試官教諭陳批深明召公告成王之意宜表出之
考試官教諭張批詞理俱優
大臣既勉君致和民之美必欲疾敬其德以畏乎民
復勉君盡天人之責必述同列之言以期其效夫敬
德者誠和小民之本也然大臣勉君盡天人之責而
不引同列之言以實之又何以見其效之可必哉昔
===
召公作書以告成王若曰王當馴擾調娛期夫大能
和裕小民而爲今日盛治之休可也游息化養期夫
大能和保小民而爲今日太和之美可也然和民之
道惟在於敬德而已王必兢兢焉敬德不敢後于以
顧乎民心之𢇲險不可以其至微而忽之焉業業焉
敬德不敢緩于以畏乎民心之難保不可以其至賤
而慢之焉雖然小民之誠和固本於敬德而敬德畏
民豈可舎此洛邑以圖治乎吾王來此洛邑繼天出
治當自服行政教於土中而達之天下也代天理物
punctuated:
同考試官教諭鄭批：場中作此題，多分截不明，惟此篇明於分截，且寫出周、召告君忠愛之意，宛然見於言辭之表。
考試官教諭陳批：深明召公告成王之意，宜表出之。
考試官教諭張批：詞理俱優。
大臣既勉君致和民之美，必欲疾敬其德以畏乎民；復勉君盡天人之責，必述同列之言以期其效。夫敬德者，誠和小民之本也；然大臣勉君盡天人之責，而不引同列之言以實之，又何以見其效之可必哉？昔召公作書以告成王，若曰：「王當馴擾調娛，期夫大能和裕小民，而爲今日盛治之休可也；游息化養，期夫大能和保小民，而爲今日太和之美可也。然和民之道，惟在於敬德而已。王必兢兢焉敬德不敢後，于以顧乎民心之𢇲險，不可以其至微而忽之焉；業業焉敬德不敢緩，于以畏乎民心之難保，不可以其至賤而慢之焉。雖然，小民之誠和固本於敬德，而敬德畏民，豈可舎此洛邑以圖治乎？吾王來此洛邑，繼天出治，當自服行政教於土中，而達之天下也；代天理物，
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Instructor Zheng's comment: Among the candidates writing on this topic in the examination compound, most were unclear in dividing the passage into sections. Only this essay is clear in its section divisions; moreover, it brings out the loyal and affectionate spirit with which the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao admonished their sovereign, making it vividly apparent beyond the mere words.
Examiner Instructor Chen's comment: It deeply grasps the meaning of the Duke of Shao's admonition to King Cheng; it deserves to be singled out for praise.
Examiner Instructor Zhang's comment: Both the diction and the reasoning are excellent.

When a great minister has exhorted his sovereign to achieve the beauty of harmonizing the people, he must wish him to urgently revere his virtue so as to stand in awe of the people; and when he further exhorts his sovereign to fulfill his responsibilities toward Heaven and man, he must cite the words of his colleague in order to anticipate the efficacy of doing so. Now, revering virtue is the root of bringing genuine harmony to the common people; yet if a great minister exhorts his sovereign to fulfill his responsibilities toward Heaven and man without citing the words of his colleague to substantiate them, how then could one see that such efficacy can be assured?

Of old, the Duke of Shao composed a document to admonish King Cheng, as if to say: "Your Majesty ought to gently guide and harmoniously gladden them, hoping to be greatly able to bring harmony and abundance to the common people, and thus make this the blessing of today's flourishing governance; you ought to give them rest, transform, and nourish them, hoping to be greatly able to harmonize and protect the common people, and thus make this the beauty of today's supreme harmony. Yet the Way of harmonizing the people lies solely in revering virtue and nothing more. Your Majesty must cautiously revere virtue without daring to lag behind, thereby paying heed to the perilousness of the people's hearts, not neglecting them because they are most lowly; and you must warily revere virtue without daring to slacken, thereby standing in awe of the difficulty of preserving the people's hearts, not slighting them because they are most humble. Even so, while bringing genuine harmony to the common people is indeed rooted in revering virtue, in revering virtue and standing in awe of the people, how could one set aside this city of Luo in planning for governance? When our King comes to this city of Luo to succeed Heaven in issuing governance, he ought personally to carry out governmental ordinances and instruction in the center of the land and extend them throughout all under Heaven; acting on behalf of Heaven to order all things, …

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
當自躬行德化於洛邑而施之四方也然召公既告
之以此而尤恐其未信故又引周公之言以實之若
曰其作大邑豈徒然哉自是可以對越上帝而仰無
愧於天可以饗答神祇而幽無愧於神可以宅中圖
治而俯無愧於人此即紹上帝服土中之謂也王能
如是將見眷命用懋申命用休庶幾天有成命矣兹
非紹上帝之效乎百姓昭明黎民於變庶幾治民今
即休美矣兹非服土中之效乎然則敬德以和小民
事天以圖治效成王宅洛可不知所務哉抑考洛邑
===
既成成王始政召公因周公之歸作書致告達之於
王究其歸則以誠小民為祈天永命之本以疾敬德
為誠小民之本既曰王不敢後又曰王其疾敬德既
曰誠于小民又曰欲王以小民受天永命一篇之中
累致意焉此蓋老臣事幼主惓惓之心也異時成王
為守文之令主而周家歷年遠過於夏商謂非召公
告戒之力而誰歟
詩義
受天之祜四方來賀
punctuated:
當自躬行德化於洛邑，而施之四方也。然召公既告之以此，而尤恐其未信，故又引周公之言以實之，若曰：其作大邑，豈徒然哉？自是可以對越上帝，而仰無愧於天；可以饗答神祇，而幽無愧於神；可以宅中圖治，而俯無愧於人。此即「紹上帝、服土中」之謂也。王能如是，將見眷命用懋，申命用休，庶幾天有成命矣，兹非紹上帝之效乎？百姓昭明，黎民於變，庶幾治民今即休美矣，兹非服土中之效乎？然則敬德以和小民，事天以圖治效，成王宅洛，可不知所務哉？抑考洛邑既成，成王始政，召公因周公之歸，作書致告，達之於王。究其歸，則以誠小民為祈天永命之本，以疾敬德為誠小民之本。既曰「王不敢後」，又曰「王其疾敬德」；既曰「誠于小民」，又曰「欲王以小民受天永命」，一篇之中，累致意焉，此蓋老臣事幼主惓惓之心也。異時成王為守文之令主，而周家歷年遠過於夏、商，謂非召公告戒之力而誰歟？

詩義
受天之祜，四方來賀。
translation_en:
…ought personally to practice moral transformation at the settlement of Luo (Luoyi 洛邑) and extend it to the four quarters. Yet after the Duke of Shao (Shao Gong 召公) had told him this, he still feared that the King might not believe it; therefore he further cited the words of the Duke of Zhou (Zhou Gong 周公) to substantiate it, as if to say: In building this great settlement, how could it have been in vain? From this place one can respond to the Supreme Lord (Shangdi 上帝) and looking up have no shame before Heaven; one can offer sacrifices in answer to the spirits of Heaven and Earth and in the unseen realm have no shame before the spirits; one can dwell at the center to plan for good governance and looking down have no shame before men. This is precisely what is meant by "continuing the work of the Supreme Lord and governing yourself in the center of the land." If the King is able to do this, one will see Heaven's favoring mandate thereby invigorated and its renewed mandate thereby made auspicious, so that Heaven's determinate mandate may nearly be secured—is this not the effect of continuing the work of the Supreme Lord? The hundred surnames will become bright and clear, and the black-haired people will be transformed, so that the governance of the people may now immediately attain auspicious perfection—is this not the effect of governing oneself in the center of the land? This being so, revering virtue in order to harmonize the common people, and serving Heaven in order to seek the results of good governance—as King Cheng (Cheng Wang 成王) takes up residence in Luo, how could he not know what he must devote himself to?

Moreover, if we examine the matter: after the settlement of Luo was completed and King Cheng assumed personal rule, the Duke of Shao took the occasion of the Duke of Zhou's return to compose this document of admonition and convey it to the King. If we trace its ultimate point, it takes bringing誠 (sincere harmony) to the common people as the foundation for praying to Heaven for a lasting mandate, and takes urgently revering virtue as the foundation for bringing sincere harmony to the common people. Having said "the King must not dare to be remiss," he says again "may the King urgently revere virtue"; having said "let there be sincere harmony among the common people," he says again "I wish the King, through the common people, to receive Heaven's lasting mandate." Throughout the single chapter, he repeatedly expresses this intention—this was truly the earnest heart of an old minister serving a young sovereign. In later times, that King Cheng became an admirable ruler who preserved the civil order, and that the years of the House of Zhou far surpassed those of Xia and Shang—if one were to say this was not due to the strength of the Duke of Shao's admonitions, then to whom could it be attributed?

Exposition on the Book of Odes (Shiyi 詩義)
"He receives the blessing of Heaven, and from the four quarters they come to offer congratulations."

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
林會
同考試官教諭鄭批此詩美武王而及後嗣學者往
往於講貫處多忽武王唯此篇
敷衍詳明深合經旨
考試官教諭陳批理明詞贍非精於詩者未易
及此
考試官教諭張批辭理通暢
既膺天心之眷必得人心之歸此詩人頌聖君之後
也夫天之所眷人之所歸也後王既有以膺上天之
===
眷豈不足以得天下人心之歸哉是詩美武王而作
五章既言武王之来世能繼武王之昭明則久荷天
祿而不替矣至此復言其得天得人焉盖皇天無私
惟德是輔武王之後人而能繼其德則必荷天之休
百祿是遒衍不易之駿命於無窮無忝武王之為天
子矣皇天無親惟善是與武王之後世而能嗣其善
則必荷天之寵百祿是總綿不拔之王業於悠久無
異武王之居天位矣天且福之人將焉往殆見天下
之大侯伯子男非一爵莫不執圭捧璧以来朝四海
punctuated:
林會
同考試官教諭鄭批：此詩美武王而及後嗣，學者往往於講貫處多忽武王。唯此篇敷衍詳明，深合經旨。
考試官教諭陳批：理明詞贍，非精於《詩》者未易及此。
考試官教諭張批：辭理通暢。
既膺天心之眷，必得人心之歸，此詩人頌聖君之後也。夫天之所眷，人之所歸也。後王既有以膺上天之眷，豈不足以得天下人心之歸哉？是詩美武王而作。五章既言武王之来世能繼武王之昭明，則久荷天祿而不替矣。至此，復言其得天得人焉。盖皇天無私，惟德是輔。武王之後人而能繼其德，則必荷天之休，百祿是遒，衍不易之駿命於無窮，無忝武王之為天子矣。皇天無親，惟善是與。武王之後世而能嗣其善，則必荷天之寵，百祿是總，綿不拔之王業於悠久，無異武王之居天位矣。天且福之，人將焉往？殆見天下之大，侯、伯、子、男非一爵，莫不執圭捧璧以来朝；四海…
translation_en:
Lin Hui

Associate Examiner, County Director of Studies Zheng comments: This ode praises King Wu and extends to his descendants; scholars in their explanations and analyses often overlook King Wu. Only this essay elaborates with clarity and detail, deeply according with the purport of the Classic.
Examiner, County Director of Studies Chen comments: The reasoning is clear and the diction rich; one who is not well-versed in the Book of Odes (Shi) could not easily attain this.
Examiner, County Director of Studies Zhang comments: The expression and reasoning are fluent and coherent.

Having received the favor of Heaven's mind, one will surely win the allegiance of people's hearts; in this the poet eulogizes the descendants of the sage ruler. Now, him whom Heaven favors is him to whom men turn in allegiance. Since the successor kings have what it takes to receive the favor of High Heaven, how could that not suffice to win the allegiance of the hearts of the people throughout the realm? This ode was composed in praise of King Wu. The fifth stanza having stated that King Wu's coming generations would be able to continue King Wu's illustriousness and thus long bear Heaven's blessings without decline, at this point it further speaks of their winning both Heaven and man. For August Heaven has no partiality, assisting only virtue. If King Wu's descendants are able to continue his virtue, they will surely bear the grace of Heaven, gathering all blessings, extending the unchanging great Mandate into infinity, and bringing no shame to King Wu's having been the Son of Heaven. August Heaven has no favorites, granting its aid only to goodness. If King Wu's posterity are able to succeed to his goodness, they will surely bear the favor of Heaven, uniting all blessings, prolonging the unshakable royal enterprise into perpetuity, no different from King Wu's occupying the heavenly throne. Since Heaven itself blesses them, where else would men go? One will surely see that throughout the vastness of the realm, the marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons—not of a single rank of nobility—will none of them fail to hold their jade tablets and present their jade disks to come to court; and across the breadth of the Four Seas…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之廣綏甸要荒非一國莫不獻琛效贄而來賀爵雖
有崇卑而趨向之心與四方攸同皇王維辟者同一
致焉職雖有大小而歸往之志與媚茲一人應侯順
德者同一揆焉天福之如此其隆人歸之如此其衆
自非後王能繼武王之道亦何以臻此哉抑考是詩
凡六章美武王繼三后於已往開後嗣於方来惟以
求世德永孝思而上合天理下孚人心者為之本耳
下武詩人其亦善於形容者歟
皇皇后帝皇祖后稷享以騂犧是饗是宜降福
===
既多周公皇祖亦其福女秋而載嘗夏而楅
衡白牡騂剛犧尊將將毛炰胾羹籩豆大房
萬舞洋洋孝孫有慶
蕭澳

得此篇辭理明順特表出之
考試官教諭陳批詩義此篇條暢宜冠本經
考試官教諭張批此篇獨優衆作宜置前列
敬郊廟而獲福隆敬宗廟而獲福盛此詩人頌禱魯
punctuated:
之廣，綏甸要荒非一國，莫不獻琛效贄而來賀。爵雖有崇卑，而趨向之心，與「四方攸同，皇王維辟」者同一致焉；職雖有大小，而歸往之志，與「媚茲一人，應侯順德」者同一揆焉。天福之如此其隆，人歸之如此其衆，自非後王能繼武王之道，亦何以臻此哉？抑考是詩凡六章，美武王繼三后於已往，開後嗣於方来，惟以求世德、永孝思，而上合天理、下孚人心者為之本耳。《下武》詩人，其亦善於形容者歟！

皇皇后帝，皇祖后稷。享以騂犧，是饗是宜。降福既多，周公皇祖，亦其福女。秋而載嘗，夏而楅衡。白牡騂剛，犧尊將將。毛炰胾羹，籩豆大房。萬舞洋洋，孝孫有慶。
蕭澳

敬郊廟而獲福隆，敬宗廟而獲福盛，此詩人頌禱魯
translation_en:
… across the breadth [of the Four Seas], the Pacified, Royal, Constraint, and Wild Domains are not of a single state, yet none fails to offer treasures and present gifts in coming to offer congratulations. Though their ranks of nobility differ in being high or low, their hearts in turning toward him are identical with "the four quarters uniting in the same allegiance, the august king being their sovereign." Though their offices differ in being great or small, their resolve in giving allegiance to him follows the same measure as "loving this one man, responding with docile virtue." With Heaven blessing them so abundantly and the people turning to them in such multitudes, had the later kings not been able to continue the Way of King Wu, how could they have attained this? Furthermore, if we examine this ode in all its six stanzas, it praises King Wu for succeeding the Three Rulers in the past and opening the way for his descendants in the future, taking nothing other than seeking the hereditary virtue and perpetuating filial thoughts—thereby conforming to Heavenly Principle above and winning the trust of human hearts below—as its foundation. How skilled indeed at depiction was the poet of "Xiawu" (Following the Footsteps of Wu)!

"Most august is the Sovereign Emperor, and the august ancestor Hou Ji. He offers to them red victims; they enjoy them, they approve them. They send down blessings in abundance; the Duke of Zhou, the august ancestor, also blesses you. In autumn he performs the chang sacrifice, and in summer applies the cross-bars to the horns of the victims; the white bull and the red one, the bull-figured goblets so grand; the singed pig, the sliced meat, the broth, the bamboo and wooden vessels, and the great stand; the wan dance so expansive—the filial descendant shall have felicity."
By Xiao Ao 蕭澳.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Zheng 鄭: This topic has quite a few threads and is difficult to lay out in order. Late in the reading I came upon this essay; its diction and reasoning are clear and smooth, so I specially single it out.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Chen 陳: Among the essays on the Classic of Poetry (Shijing), this piece is well-structured and fluent; it deserves to head the essays in this classic.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zhang 張: This piece alone excels above all the other compositions and should be placed at the forefront.

Being reverent in the suburban and ancestral sacrifices and thus obtaining abundant blessings, and being reverent in the ancestral temple and thus obtaining flourishing blessings—this is the poet praising and praying for the [Duke] of Lu…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
公也夫敬者事神獲福之本今魯公郊廟宗廟之祭
既無一而不致其敬矣則其獲福之盛也豈不宜哉
是詩蓋僖公脩閟宮詩人咏歌其事以為頌禱之詞
至此歌之若曰莫高匪天而皇皇后帝至難格也莫
幽匪神而皇祖后稷至難感也惟僖公之郊祀上帝
配以后稷竭始終之誠敬獻肥腯之騂犧后帝是饗
而后稷亦是饗焉后帝是宜而后稷亦是宜焉夫以
郊廟之頃誠敬交格如此由是上帝也皇祖也則必
降之百福而眉壽保魯矣周公也羣公也亦必綏以
===
多福而黃髮兒齒矣郊廟致敬既獲乎福則宗廟致
敬又豈不獲乎福哉是故牲不可以不夙戒也秋而
將行甞祭夏而福衡其牛則既夙戒矣色不可以不
有辨也祀周公以白牡祀魯公以騂剛則既有辨矣
當是之時以言其器則畫牛於腹而謂之犧尊將將
而列以言其味則炰豚切肉而太羹鉶羹苾苾而芳
籩豆以盛殽核者有焉大房以載牲體者具焉至於
作樂以祭則執籥秉翟而文舞之是陳朱干玉戚而
武舞之並作宗廟之祭誠敬感孚如此由是俾熾而
punctuated: 公也。夫敬者，事神獲福之本。今魯公郊廟、宗廟之祭，既無一而不致其敬矣，則其獲福之盛也，豈不宜哉？是詩蓋僖公脩閟宮，詩人咏歌其事以為頌禱之詞。至此歌之若曰：莫高匪天，而皇皇后帝至難格也；莫幽匪神，而皇祖后稷至難感也。惟僖公之郊祀上帝，配以后稷，竭始終之誠敬，獻肥腯之騂犧，后帝是饗，而后稷亦是饗焉；后帝是宜，而后稷亦是宜焉。夫以郊廟之頃，誠敬交格如此，由是上帝也、皇祖也，則必降之百福，而眉壽保魯矣；周公也、羣公也，亦必綏以多福，而黃髮兒齒矣。郊廟致敬既獲乎福，則宗廟致敬又豈不獲乎福哉？是故牲不可以不夙戒也，秋而將行甞祭，夏而福衡其牛，則既夙戒矣；色不可以不有辨也，祀周公以白牡，祀魯公以騂剛，則既有辨矣。當是之時，以言其器，則畫牛於腹而謂之犧尊，將將而列；以言其味，則炰豚、切肉，而太羹、鉶羹苾苾而芳；籩豆以盛殽核者有焉，大房以載牲體者具焉。至於作樂以祭，則執籥秉翟而文舞之是陳，朱干玉戚而武舞之並作。宗廟之祭，誠敬感孚如此，由是俾熾而
translation_en:
… the Duke [of Lu]. Now, reverence is the root of serving the spirits and obtaining blessings. Since in the Duke of Lu's sacrifices at the suburban altar and the ancestral temple there was not a single aspect in which he failed to exercise the utmost reverence, how could it not be fitting that he obtained such abundant blessings?

This ode was composed when Duke Xi repaired the Solemn Temple (Bi Gong), and the poet sang of this affair in words of praise and prayer. At this point in the song, it is as if he says: Nothing is higher than Heaven, and the august Sovereign on High is most difficult to reach; nothing is more inscrutable than the spirits, and the august ancestor Hou Ji is most difficult to move. Yet when Duke Xi performed the suburban sacrifice to the Lord on High, matching him with Hou Ji, he exhausted his sincerity and reverence from beginning to end and offered up fat and sleek red sacrificial victims. The Sovereign on High enjoyed them, and Hou Ji likewise enjoyed them; the Sovereign on High approved of them, and Hou Ji likewise approved of them. Because during the suburban sacrifice his sincerity and reverence reached both of them like this, consequently the Lord on High and the august ancestor will surely send down a hundred blessings, granting him longevity with bushy eyebrows to preserve Lu; the Duke of Zhou and the succession of dukes will also surely comfort him with manifold blessings, granting him yellow hair and renewed teeth.

Since expressing the utmost reverence in the suburban sacrifice already obtained blessings, how then could expressing the utmost reverence in the ancestral temple not also obtain blessings? Therefore, the sacrificial victims could not but be prepared early: when the autumnal sacrifice (chang) was to be performed in autumn, the crossbars were attached to the horns of the oxen in summer, so they were already prepared early. Their colors could not but be distinguished: sacrificing to the Duke of Zhou with a white bull and sacrificing to the Duke of Lu [Boqin] with a stiff-horned red bull, they were already distinguished. At this time, to speak of the vessels, there were the victim-goblets (xizun) with oxen painted on their bellies, arrayed in grand order; to speak of the flavors, there were roasted suckling pig, sliced meat, the unseasoned great broth, and the seasoned vessel-broth, all fragrant and sweet-smelling; there were bamboo and wooden dishes to hold the meats and fruits, and the great stand (dafang) to bear the limbs of the sacrificial victims was provided. As for performing music to offer sacrifice, the civil dancers holding flutes and pheasant plumes were arrayed, while the martial dancers with vermilion shields and jade-handled axes performed alongside them. In the sacrifice at the ancestral temple, his sincerity and reverence moved and inspired confidence like this, and consequently they made him prosperous and…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
昌俾壽而臧而孝孫有慶矣保彼東方魯邦是常而
孝孫獲福矣是皆國人稱頌之如此也抑考是詩推
本后稷之生而下及於僖公一詩之中頭其上為神
明之所福內為國人之所安外為鄰國之所懷而脩
舊起廢治其寢廟以順萬民之所望稱頌之意至矣
噫非僖公之賢何以致此哉
春秋義
九月丁卯子同生〔桓公六年〕甲午衛侯衎復歸于
衛〔襄公二十六年〕吳子使札来聘〔襄公二十九年〕取鄫
===
〔昭公四年〕
林球

punctuated:
昌，俾壽而臧，而孝孫有慶矣；保彼東方，魯邦是常，而孝孫獲福矣。是皆國人稱頌之如此也。抑考是詩，推本后稷之生，而下及於僖公，一詩之中，頭其上為神明之所福，內為國人之所安，外為鄰國之所懷，而脩舊起廢，治其寢廟，以順萬民之所望，稱頌之意至矣。噫！非僖公之賢，何以致此哉？

春秋義
九月丁卯，子同生。〔桓公六年〕甲午，衛侯衎復歸于衛。〔襄公二十六年〕吳子使札来聘。〔襄公二十九年〕取鄫。〔昭公四年〕

論聖經之㫖，既有以兼帝王之道，復有以叅文質之
translation_en:
… and prosperous, making him long-lived and good—thus the filial descendant has blessings! Protecting that eastern region, keeping the state of Lu enduring—thus the filial descendant receives good fortune! All of this is how the people of the state praised and eulogized him. Moreover, if we examine this ode, it traces the origin back to the birth of Hou Ji and extends down to Duke Xi. Within a single ode, it praises [? 頭 for 頌] how above he was blessed by the gods and spirits, within he brought peace to the people of the state, and abroad he was cherished by neighboring states, while he repaired the old and revived what had fallen into disuse, putting his ancestral temple in order so as to fulfill the hopes of the myriad people—the spirit of praise and eulogy reaches the utmost! Alas! Without the worthiness of Duke Xi, how could this have been brought about?

Expositions on the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
中蓋夫子作春秋所以示萬世也得不兼帝王參文
質而立法以垂訓乎且唐虞以賢而相禪三代以子
而相繼此帝王傳授之義也春秋何以兼帝王之道
乎其意蓋曰賢可與則以天下為公而不拘於世及
之禮子可繼則以天下為家而不必於讓國之義故
子同始生即書于策以明立嫡之重義即所謂夏后
殷周繼者也季札來聘不稱公子以貶辭國之非義
即所謂唐虞禪者也或禪或繼非兼帝王之道而何
虞史書名而不諱周人以諱而易名此文質因革之
===
宜也春秋又何以參文質之中乎其旨蓋曰義不可
諱則直紀其事以示信史之實禮所當諱則特婉其
詞以伸臣子之情故襄公名午即書甲午而不諱其
名義即所以從虞史之質也昭公滅鄫乃書取鄫而
特諱其惡義即所以倣周道之文也或諱或不諱非
參文質之中而何凡此類皆所謂酌古今而貫乎書
之事者也吁非聖人其孰能脩之大抵魯生夫子萬
世而一人也夫子作春秋萬世而一時也故其制作
之義廣大悉備不但如是而已如公好惡則發乎詩
punctuated: 中。蓋夫子作《春秋》，所以示萬世也，得不兼帝王、參文質而立法以垂訓乎？且唐、虞以賢而相禪，三代以子而相繼，此帝王傳授之義也。《春秋》何以兼帝王之道乎？其意蓋曰：賢可與，則以天下為公，而不拘於世及之禮；子可繼，則以天下為家，而不必於讓國之義。故子同始生，即書于策，以明立嫡之重，義即所謂「夏后、殷、周繼」者也；季札來聘，不稱公子，以貶辭國之非，義即所謂「唐、虞禪」者也。或禪或繼，非兼帝王之道而何？虞史書名而不諱，周人以諱而易名，此文質因革之宜也。《春秋》又何以參文質之中乎？其旨蓋曰：義不可諱，則直紀其事，以示信史之實；禮所當諱，則特婉其詞，以伸臣子之情。故襄公名午，即書「甲午」而不諱其名，義即所以從虞史之質也；昭公滅鄫，乃書「取鄫」而特諱其惡，義即所以倣周道之文也。或諱或不諱，非參文質之中而何？凡此類，皆所謂酌古今而貫乎《書》之事者也。吁！非聖人，其孰能脩之？大抵魯生夫子，萬世而一人也；夫子作《春秋》，萬世而一時也。故其制作之義，廣大悉備，不但如是而已。如公好惡則發乎《詩》
translation_en:
… mean between cultural refinement and unadorned substance. For when the Master composed the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), it was in order to instruct ten thousand generations; how could he not combine the ways of the Five Emperors and Three Kings and blend refinement and substance in establishing laws to hand down as teachings? 

Moreover, Yao and Shun yielded the throne to the worthy in succession, whereas the Three Dynasties passed the throne to their sons by hereditary succession; such are the principles of transmission of the Emperors and Kings. How does the Spring and Autumn Annals combine the ways of the Emperors and Kings? Its meaning is roughly this: when there is a worthy man to whom the realm may be given, one takes All-under-Heaven as a public trust and is not bound by the rites of hereditary succession; when there is a son who can succeed, one takes All-under-Heaven as a family possession and need not insist on the principle of yielding the state. Thus, when Zi Tong was first born, it was immediately recorded in the tablets to make clear the importance of establishing the legitimate heir—a principle that corresponds to what is called "the hereditary succession of Xia, Yin, and Zhou." When Ji Zha came on a mission of friendly inquiry, he was not styled "Ducal Son" (gongzi), in order to censure the impropriety of his declining the state—a principle that corresponds to what is called "the abdication of Yao and Shun." Whether by abdication or by hereditary succession, what is this if not combining the ways of the Emperors and Kings?

The scribes of Yu recorded personal names without taboo, whereas the men of Zhou replaced names on account of taboos; such is the appropriateness of continuity and change in refinement and substance. And how does the Spring and Autumn Annals blend the mean between refinement and substance? Its purport is roughly this: where righteousness does not permit tabooing, it directly records the matter to show the reality of a trustworthy history; where ritual propriety requires tabooing, it specially softens the phrasing to give expression to the feelings of subjects and sons. Thus, although Duke Xiang's personal name was Wu, it directly wrote "jiawu" without tabooing his name—a principle whereby it followed the unadorned substance of the scribes of Yu. When Duke Zhao destroyed Zeng, it wrote "seized Zeng" to specially taboo his evil—a principle whereby it imitated the cultural refinement of the way of Zhou. Whether tabooing or not tabooing, what is this if not blending the mean between refinement and substance? All cases of this sort are what is meant by weighing antiquity and the present and threading together the affairs of the Book of Documents (Shu). 

Ah! Were he not a sage, who could have compiled it? In general, Lu's giving birth to the Master was a matter of one man in ten thousand generations; the Master's composing the Spring and Autumn Annals was a matter of one moment in ten thousand generations. Therefore, the principles of its creation are vast and fully complete, and not merely limited to this. For instance, in making likes and dislikes impartial, it gives expression to the sentiments of the Book of Odes (Shi)…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之情興常典則體乎禮之經本忠恕則導乎樂之和
著權制則盡乎易之變或貴王而賤伯或內夏而外
夷或有功而抑有罪而宥或功未就而予罪未著而
奪或顯而微或幽而闡信非聖人莫能脩也吁游夏
不能贊一辭其以是歟林珝
臧孫辰告糴于齊〔莊公二十八年〕歸粟于蔡〔定公五年〕
同考試官訓導華批〔此篇理有定見文善發明佳作也宜表之〕
===
考試官教諭陳批〔體認真切傑出衆作〕
考試官教諭張批〔得謹嚴之旨〕
治名而忘實者可譏舍大而務小者可責此臧孫行
糴于齊晉定輸粟于蔡春秋得不書之以示意哉且
國有饑饉卿出告糴古之制也而臧孫辰糴于齊何
以為治名而不治實邪盖當國任事大臣之職而徇
名忘實君子所耻今辰徒以急病讓夷為名而不知
務農重穀於民未告急之日徒以居上恤下為名而
不能徹彼桑土於天未陰雨之際至於穀一不登仰
punctuated:
之情，興常典則體乎禮之經，本忠恕則導乎樂之和，著權制則盡乎《易》之變。或貴王而賤伯，或內夏而外夷，或有功而抑、有罪而宥，或功未就而予、罪未著而奪，或顯而微，或幽而闡，信非聖人莫能脩也。吁！游、夏不能贊一辭，其以是歟！

林珝
臧孫辰告糴于齊〔莊公二十八年〕歸粟于蔡〔定公五年〕
同考試官訓導華批：〔此篇理有定見，文善發明，佳作也，宜表之。〕
考試官教諭陳批：〔體認真切，傑出衆作。〕
考試官教諭張批：〔得謹嚴之旨。〕

治名而忘實者可譏，舍大而務小者可責。此臧孫行糴于齊、晉定輸粟于蔡，《春秋》得不書之以示意哉？且國有饑饉，卿出告糴，古之制也；而臧孫辰糴于齊，何以為治名而不治實邪？盖當國任事，大臣之職；而徇名忘實，君子所耻。今辰徒以急病讓夷為名，而不知務農重穀於民未告急之日；徒以居上恤下為名，而不能徹彼桑土於天未陰雨之際。至於穀一不登，仰
translation_en:
… sentiments of the Odes (Shi); in reviving regular canons, it embodies the constant principles of the Rites (Li); in taking loyalty and reciprocity as its foundation, it guides toward the harmony of the Music (Yue); and in manifesting expedient regulation, it exhausts the transformations of the Changes (Yi). At times it honors the true King and disparages the hegemons; at times it treats the Chinese states as inner and the barbarians as outer; at times it suppresses those who have merit and pardons those who have guilt; at times it praises before merit is accomplished and censures before guilt is manifest; at times what is prominent is made subtle, and at times what is obscure is elucidated. Truly, none but a sage could have compiled it! Alas, that Ziyou and Zixia could not add a single word—was it not because of this?

Lin Xu 林珝
"Zang Sunchen requested to purchase grain in Qi" 〔28th year of Duke Zhuang〕; "Sent a gift of grain to Cai" 〔5th year of Duke Ding〕
Comment by Associate Examiner Hua, Assistant Instructor: 〔This essay holds a firm view of principle, and the writing is skillful in its elucidation. It is an excellent piece and ought to be highlighted.〕
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: 〔Its comprehension of the truth is genuine and earnest, standing out among all the compositions.〕
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: 〔It grasps the purport of strictness and rigor.〕

Those who pursue reputation while forgetting reality deserve ridicule; those who abandon the great to attend to the small deserve reproach. Given Zang Sun's going to purchase grain in Qi and Duke Ding of Jin's transporting grain to Cai, how could the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) not record them in order to show its intent? Moreover, when a state suffers famine, for a minister to go abroad to request the purchase of grain is an ancient institution; why then is Zang Sunchen's purchasing grain in Qi considered pursuing reputation while not attending to reality? Because taking charge of the state and bearing responsibility for its affairs is the duty of a great minister, whereas chasing after reputation and forgetting reality is what a gentleman is ashamed of. Now Chen merely used "relieving distress and yielding to equals" as a pretext, yet did not know to promote agriculture and value grain on the days before the people reported an emergency; he merely used "occupying a superior position and showing compassion for inferiors" as a pretext, yet was unable to "gather that mulberry-root bark" before the sky grew dark with rain. When it came to a single harvest failing, the state looked up to…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
給四鄰縱百圭罄如失政何故春秋不曰于齊告糴
而曰告糴于齊者所以譏大臣治名而不治實之蔽
也若夫小國飢乏鄰國歸粟亦禮之正也而晋定歸
粟于蔡又何以為舍大而務小乎盖賙窮恤匱固仁
人之心而攘夷安夏實伯者之畧今晋定徒務輸粟
於蔡圍既解之餘而楚人滔天之罪則置而不問徒
施小恩於蔡人焚溺之後而蠻荆燎原之烈則置而
不恤至於伯舉戰勝聊爾輸粟區區小惠奚補於事
故春秋特書歸粟于蔡而不書諸侯者所以罪伯國
===
忘大義而事小惠也吁以告糴為名者辰也而君子
必責其實以歸粟為恩者晋定也而君子必責其大
聖人之意何如哉大抵臧孫務名而忘實固不足錄
使齊桓不仗義以恤魯則東蒙之民亦云殆矣晋定
務小而忘大固無足齒使吳子不伸義以援蔡則叔
度之廟幾不祀矣噫此葵丘之禁齊桓可謂能踐其
言而伯舉之役吳人所以進而書子也歟
禮記義
考禮正刑一德以尊于天子
punctuated:
給四鄰，縱百圭罄，如失政何？故《春秋》不曰「于齊告糴」，而曰「告糴于齊」者，所以譏大臣治名而不治實之蔽也。若夫小國飢乏，鄰國歸粟，亦禮之正也。而晋定歸粟于蔡，又何以為舍大而務小乎？盖賙窮恤匱，固仁人之心，而攘夷安夏，實伯者之畧。今晋定徒務輸粟於蔡圍既解之餘，而楚人滔天之罪則置而不問；徒施小恩於蔡人焚溺之後，而蠻荆燎原之烈則置而不恤。至於伯舉戰勝，聊爾輸粟，區區小惠，奚補於事？故《春秋》特書「歸粟于蔡」，而不書諸侯者，所以罪伯國忘大義而事小惠也。吁！以告糴為名者，辰也，而君子必責其實；以歸粟為恩者，晋定也，而君子必責其大。聖人之意何如哉！大抵臧孫務名而忘實，固不足錄；使齊桓不仗義以恤魯，則東蒙之民亦云殆矣。晋定務小而忘大，固無足齒；使吳子不伸義以援蔡，則叔度之廟幾不祀矣。噫！此葵丘之禁，齊桓可謂能踐其言，而伯舉之役，吳人所以進而書「子」也歟！
禮記義
考禮正刑，一德以尊于天子。
translation_en:
…depend on supplies from the neighboring states on all four sides; even if a hundred jade tablets were exhausted in soliciting grain, what would that avail against the failure of governance? Therefore, that the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) does not say "in Qi, requested to buy grain," but rather says "requested to buy grain in Qi," is the means by which it criticizes the blind fault of a great minister attending to reputation while failing to attend to reality.

As for when a small state suffers famine and want, for neighboring states to send grain to it is also the proper norm of ritual. Yet why is Duke Ding of Jin's (Jin Ding) sending grain to Cai considered abandoning the great to pursue the small? For relieving the destitute and aiding the needy is indeed the heart of a benevolent man, whereas repelling the barbarians and pacifying the Chinese states is truly the grand strategy of a hegemon (bo). Now Duke Ding of Jin merely busied himself with transporting grain after the siege of Cai had already been lifted, while leaving the heaven-flooding crimes of the people of Chu uninvestigated; he merely bestowed a petty favor after the people of Cai had suffered burning and drowning, while leaving the prairie-scorching ferocity of the Man-Jing barbarians unheeded. Coming after the victory in battle at Boju, casually transporting grain as a trifling, petty kindness—what help was that to the affair? Therefore, that the Spring and Autumn Annals specially records "sent grain to Cai" without recording the feudal lords is the means by which it condemns the hegemon's state for forgetting great righteousness and engaging in petty favors.

Alas! He who used requesting to buy grain to make a name was Chen [Zang Sunchen], yet the gentleman necessarily holds him accountable for the reality; he who used sending grain to show grace was Duke Ding of Jin, yet the gentleman necessarily holds him accountable for the great duty. What, then, was the intention of the Sage? On the whole, Zang Sun pursued reputation and forgot reality, which is certainly not worth recording with approval; had Duke Huan of Qi (Qi Huan) not upheld righteousness to take pity on Lu, the people of Dongmeng [in Lu] would indeed have been in peril! Duke Ding of Jin pursued the small and forgot the great, which is certainly not worth mentioning among peers; had the Viscount of Wu (Wu zi) not extended righteousness to rescue Cai, the ancestral temple of Shudu [the founder of Cai] would nearly have ceased its sacrifices! Ah! In the prohibitions at the covenant of Kuiqiu, Duke Huan of Qi may be said to have been able to fulfill his word, and in the campaign of Boju, was this not why the people of Wu were advanced in status and recorded as "Viscount"?

Expositions on the Record of Rites (Liji)

"To examine the rites and rectify the punishments, unifying virtue in order to honor the Son of Heaven."

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
王惟節
同考試官訓導郁批此題本平易場中作者類能
言之而考禮正刑處多不知以下
文作講求其識此而且行文簡勁
不陳腐者僅見此篇是用録出
考試官教諭陳批詞理通貫可取
考試官教諭張批遣辭析理無不精當
人臣謹其法以同其心皆所以尊其君也盖臣道莫
大於尊君也苟欲尊君而不知考禮正刑一德焉其
===
可乎哉是宜記禮者言此以示人也且夫諸侯之朝
于天子也豈徒然哉誠以禮有五天子所制也考天
子之禮而行之使豐殺多寡悉惟其稱可也如鬯為
禮之至而圭瓚酌鬯酒之噐也為諸侯者必賜圭瓚
而後為鬯其或未賜則資於天子而已其可縱私違
僭如我魯行郊禘於諸侯之庭乎刑有五天子所定
也正天子之刑而用之使征伐殺戮舉出於公可也
如征殺所以致天討而弓矢鈇鉞皆致天討之噐也
為諸侯者必賜弓矢鈇鉞而後征殺其或未賜則守
punctuated:
王惟節
同考試官訓導郁批：此題本平易，場中作者類能言之，而「考禮正刑」處多不知以下文作講。求其識此，而且行文簡勁、不陳腐者，僅見此篇，是用録出。
考試官教諭陳批：詞理通貫，可取。
考試官教諭張批：遣辭析理，無不精當。

人臣謹其法以同其心，皆所以尊其君也。盖臣道莫大於尊君也，苟欲尊君而不知考禮、正刑、一德焉，其可乎哉？是宜記禮者言此以示人也。且夫諸侯之朝于天子也，豈徒然哉？誠以禮有五，天子所制也；考天子之禮而行之，使豐殺多寡悉惟其稱，可也。如鬯為禮之至，而圭瓚酌鬯酒之噐也；為諸侯者，必賜圭瓚而後為鬯，其或未賜，則資於天子而已，其可縱私違僭，如我魯行郊禘於諸侯之庭乎？刑有五，天子所定也；正天子之刑而用之，使征伐殺戮舉出於公，可也。如征殺所以致天討，而弓矢鈇鉞皆致天討之噐也；為諸侯者，必賜弓矢鈇鉞而後征殺，其或未賜，則守
translation_en:
Wang Weijie 王惟節
Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Yu 郁 comments: This topic is inherently plain and easy, and writers in the examination hall are generally able to discuss it; yet at the passage on "examining the rites and rectifying the punishments," most do not know to explicate it by drawing on the text that follows below. Seeking one who understands this and whose prose is moreover concise, vigorous, and free of clichés, I found only this essay, and therefore selected it for inclusion.
Examiner Instructor Chen 陳 comments: The diction and reasoning are coherent throughout; it is worthy of selection.
Examiner Instructor Zhang 張 comments: In the choice of words and analysis of principles, nothing fails to be precise and fitting.

When a minister carefully observes the laws so as to unify his heart with others, all of this is the means by which he honors his ruler. Indeed, in the way of a minister, nothing is greater than honoring the ruler. If one wishes to honor the ruler without knowing to examine the rites, rectify the punishments, and unify virtue, how could that be acceptable? It is fitting, therefore, that the recorder of the Rites spoke thus to instruct people. Moreover, when the feudal lords attend court before the Son of Heaven, how could it be for nothing? Truly it is because the five categories of rites are instituted by the Son of Heaven; one should examine the rites of the Son of Heaven and put them into practice, ensuring that abundance and reduction, much and little, all correspond to what is proper. For example, aromatic sacrificial wine (chang 鬯) is the culmination of ritual, and the jade-handled libation ladle (guizan 圭瓚) is the vessel for ladling aromatic wine; a feudal lord must first be bestowed the jade-handled libation ladle before he may prepare the aromatic wine, and if it has not yet been bestowed, he simply obtains the wine from the Son of Heaven—how could he indulge private desires and commit usurping transgressions, as our state of Lu 魯 did in performing the suburban and ancestral sacrifices (jiao di 郊禘) in the courtyard of a feudal lord? The five categories of punishments are established by the Son of Heaven; one should rectify the punishments of the Son of Heaven and apply them, ensuring that punitive expeditions and executions all proceed from impartiality. For example, punitive expeditions and executions are the means to carry out Heaven's punishment, and bows and arrows, battle-axes and halberds (fuyue 鈇鉞) are all instruments for carrying out Heaven's punishment; a feudal lord must first be bestowed bows and arrows, battle-axes and halberds before he may undertake punitive expeditions and executions, and if they have not yet been bestowed, he simply abides by…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其常法而已其可率意偏枉如桓文專征殺而不用
天子之命乎考禮如此正刑又如此由是一德一心
罔敢二三也同寅恊恭罔有異慮也是蓋以君為元
首為腹心而相視為一體矣惟其考禮則禮樂自天
子出矣謹其禮即尊其君也奚必奔走承順而後為尊
邪惟其正刑則征伐自天子出矣守其法即尊其上
也奚必擎拳曲跽而後為尊邪一德則不貳其君矣
何莫而非尊之哉雖然此特言諸侯朝于天子之事
也若夫天子之適諸侯則祀神養老觀民風察天道
===
脩人事無往而不致其謹焉噫古者天子之巡狩諸
侯之述職皆無有無事而空行者此所以成雍熙泰
和之治也
親者屬也自仁率親等而上之至於祖自義率
祖順而下之至於禰是故人道親親也
王惟節
同考試官訓導郁批作此題者多不知本制服立說惟
此篇體認集說之意最為切當
且文氣舂容敻出衆作宜取以
punctuated:
其常法而已。其可率意偏枉，如桓、文專征殺而不用天子之命乎？考禮如此，正刑又如此，由是一德一心，罔敢二三也；同寅恊恭，罔有異慮也。是蓋以君為元首、為腹心，而相視為一體矣。惟其考禮，則禮樂自天子出矣；謹其禮即尊其君也，奚必奔走承順而後為尊邪？惟其正刑，則征伐自天子出矣；守其法即尊其上也，奚必擎拳曲跽而後為尊邪？一德則不貳其君矣，何莫而非尊之哉！雖然，此特言諸侯朝于天子之事也。若夫天子之適諸侯，則祀神、養老、觀民風、察天道、脩人事，無往而不致其謹焉。噫！古者天子之巡狩、諸侯之述職，皆無有無事而空行者，此所以成雍熙泰和之治也。

親者屬也。自仁率親，等而上之至於祖；自義率祖，順而下之至於禰。是故人道親親也。
王惟節
同考試官訓導郁批：作此題者，多不知本制服立說，惟此篇體認《集說》之意最為切當，且文氣舂容，敻出衆作，宜取以
translation_en:
… the established laws and nothing more. How could they act willfully and perversely, like Dukes Huan and Wen, who monopolized punitive expeditions and executions without awaiting the command of the Son of Heaven? By examining the rites in this way, and rectifying punishments in that way, they consequently shared a single virtue and a single mind, never daring to be duplicitous or divided; they joined in reverent harmony and mutual respect, harboring no divergent intentions. This is because they regarded the ruler as the head and the heart, viewing themselves and him as a single body. Precisely because they examined the rites, rites and music proceeded from the Son of Heaven; being careful with his rites was itself honoring their ruler—why must one scurry about in obsequious compliance before it counts as honoring him? Precisely because they rectified punishments, punitive expeditions proceeded from the Son of Heaven; upholding his laws was itself honoring their superior—why must one clasp hands and kneel in a crouch before it counts as honoring him? Sharing a single virtue meant never being disloyal to their ruler—what part of this was not honoring him! Even so, this speaks only of the feudal lords' court visits to the Son of Heaven. As for the Son of Heaven going to the feudal lords, in sacrificing to the spirits, nourishing the aged, observing the customs of the people, examining the way of Heaven, and cultivating human affairs, there was nowhere that he did not exercise the utmost care. Alas! In antiquity, whether in the tours of inspection by the Son of Heaven or the reporting of official duties by the feudal lords, neither ever traveled in vain without purpose; this is how the governance of harmonious peace and supreme concord was achieved.

"Kinship means connection. Proceeding from benevolence to follow affection for kin, one ascends by degrees up to the distant ancestor; proceeding from righteousness to follow the ancestor, one descends in order down to the deceased father. Therefore, the way of humanity lies in loving one's kin."
Wang Weijie 王惟節

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
冠本房
考試官教諭陳批文理暢達宜居前列
考試官教諭張批辭理簡當宜冠本經
制服以有親而因其屬故用理以治親有其等此人
道莫大於親親也盖服以表其親屬而已苟不用仁
義以治之其何以知親屬之重輕哉此親親為人道
之大也有以夫昔記禮者謂人之有親則有服也彼
服有重者非徒重也以親而重之爾服有輕者非徒
輕也以親而輕之爾制服以有親豈有他哉盖親有
===
聯屬也如卑者幼者則以屬於尊與長者而服之親
有繫屬也如庶者旁者則以屬於適與正者而服之
夫親者屬也如此其可不用仁義以治親耶是故仁
主恩也用夫仁之恩愛依循於親節級而上至於祖
焉仁則父母重而祖輕也如至親以期斷而父母三
年不為仁重乎義主斷也用夫義之斷割依循於祖
順而下之至於禰焉義則祖重而父母輕也如高曾
應緦麻而進以齊衰不為義重乎夫以親屬而制服
用仁義以治親何莫而非親親哉故追王祭祀皆人
punctuated:
冠本房。

考試官教諭張批：辭理簡當，宜冠本經。
制服以有親，而因其屬；故用理以治親，有其等。此人道莫大於親親也。盖服以表其親屬而已，苟不用仁義以治之，其何以知親屬之重輕哉？此親親為人道之大也，有以夫！昔記禮者，謂人之有親則有服也。彼服有重者，非徒重也，以親而重之爾；服有輕者，非徒輕也，以親而輕之爾。制服以有親，豈有他哉？盖親有聯屬也，如卑者、幼者，則以屬於尊與長者而服之；親有繫屬也，如庶者、旁者，則以屬於適與正者而服之。夫「親者屬也」如此，其可不用仁義以治親耶？是故仁主恩也，用夫仁之恩愛，依循於親，節級而上至於祖焉。仁則父母重而祖輕也，如至親以期斷，而父母三年，不為仁重乎？義主斷也，用夫義之斷割，依循於祖，順而下之至於禰焉。義則祖重而父母輕也，如高、曾應緦麻，而進以齊衰，不為義重乎？夫以親屬而制服，用仁義以治親，何莫而非親親哉？故追王、祭祀，皆人
