punctuated: 驟則理不究，其言之不行也，固也。」此又進諫之有其時也。夫君子之進諫，亦惟盡其道與□□時之何如爾。盖嘗求之古人矣：有風力愈勁，若目曰「擊鶻」，則王素其人也；有廷争不回，若稱為「殿虎」，則劉安世其人也。以其風采晫立，雖鼎鑊不避者，謂非直諫可乎？因詩章而含規諷，歐陽脩之辭何婉耶？因身疾而喻朝政，吕獻可之章何誠耶？以其旁入曲喻，雖風雅不過者，謂非諷諫得乎？之數君子者，發乎愛君之誠，合乎告君之道，而又皆近者、親者、久任者，此所以上信其心，下服其識，天下後世知其忠，夫何有佞與激之譏耶？然君聖則臣直。洪惟我聖天子嗣登大寶，首開言路，其論治體而裨國事者，多見采納，真億萬載太平之主也。然其間有未信其心而行其所言者，豈有他哉？其即東萊所謂遠者、踈者與驟者，時不至焉者也。雖然，此但言其時與勢爾，以理言之，則□□愛
translation_en: … If one is abrupt, the underlying principles are not thoroughly examined. That one's words are not put into practice is only natural." This shows that remonstrating also has its proper timing. When a gentleman presents remonstrance, he simply fulfills the proper way and [considers?] what the timing is like. Indeed, I have sought examples among the ancients: there was one whose force of character grew ever more vigorous, looked upon as a "striking falcon"—such a man was Wang Su 王素; there was one who argued at court without yielding, acclaimed as the "Tiger of the Hall"—such a man was Liu Anshi 劉安世. With their bearing standing out brilliantly, not shrinking even from the cauldron and executioner's block, could one say this was not direct remonstrance? Imbuing poetic verses with admonition, how gentle were the words of Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩! Using physical ailments as a metaphor for court administration, how sincere were the memorials of Lü Xianke 吕獻可 (Lü誨)! Approaching indirectly and using subtle metaphors, unsurpassed even by the Airs and Odes of the Book of Odes, could one fail to call this remonstrance by indirection? These several gentlemen proceeded from the sincerity of loving their ruler and conformed to the proper way of advising their ruler; moreover, they were all close to the throne, trusted, and long in office. This is why the ruler above trusted their intentions, those below admired their insight, and the world and posterity knew their loyalty—how could there be any criticism of flattery or of being overly drastic? Yet when the ruler is sagely, the ministers are forthright. Humbly considering how our Sacred Son of Heaven succeeded to the Great Treasure, he first opened the avenues of speech; those who discuss the principles of governance and benefit state affairs have largely seen their advice adopted—truly the Lord of Great Peace for a myriad ages! Yet if among them there are some whose intentions are not yet trusted and whose words are not yet put into practice, how could there be any other reason? It is simply what Donglai 東萊 (Lü Zuqian 吕祖謙) called being distant, estranged, or abrupt, the timing not yet having arrived. Even so, this speaks only of timing and circumstance; speaking in terms of principle, then […][?] love…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄後序
天道至公而已矣
聖人法天立道亦至公而已矣
天道
聖德莫罄名言而皆不外乎一公下此
而中外臣鄰所以奉若
天道祗承
聖德者亦不外夫公焉爾公以治事則
===
事集公以治民則民安公以求賢
則賢才進然求賢最重進士一科
而是科之制置條格既周且備一
有不公弊將不可勝言矣成化戊
子之秋適賓興賢能之期先是提
督兩廣軍務左副都御史韓雍削
平羣盜愛民養士蓋公心也繼而
巡撫右副都御史陳濂拊循瘡痍
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄後序

天道至公而已矣，聖人法天立道，亦至公而已矣。天道、聖德，莫罄名言，而皆不外乎一公。下此而中外臣鄰所以奉若天道、祗承聖德者，亦不外夫公焉爾。公以治事則事集，公以治民則民安，公以求賢則賢才進。然求賢最重進士一科，而是科之制置條格，既周且備；一有不公，弊將不可勝言矣。

成化戊子之秋，適賓興賢能之期。先是，提督兩廣軍務左副都御史韓雍，削平羣盜，愛民養士，蓋公心也。繼而，巡撫右副都御史陳濂，拊循瘡痍，
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

The Way of Heaven is nothing other than utmost impartiality; the Sage models himself on Heaven to establish the Way, and that too is nothing other than utmost impartiality. The Way of Heaven and the virtue of the Sage cannot be exhausted in words, yet neither goes beyond this single principle of impartiality. Below them, the means by which officials and ministers at court and in the provinces conform to the Way of Heaven and reverently uphold the virtue of the Sage likewise do not go beyond impartiality. When one governs affairs with impartiality, affairs are accomplished; when one governs the people with impartiality, the people are at peace; when one seeks out the worthy with impartiality, worthy talents advance. Yet in seeking out the worthy, the greatest weight is placed upon the metropolitan graduate (jinshi) examination stream, and the regulations and statutes established for this stream are both comprehensive and complete. Should there be the slightest impartiality, the abuses would be beyond description.

In the autumn of the wuzi year of the Chenghua era [1468], it was the appointed time for summoning and promoting the worthy and capable. Prior to this, the Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and Supreme Commander of Military Affairs in Liangguang, Han Yong 韓雍, had suppressed the bands of bandits, cherished the people, and nurtured the scholars—all out of an impartial heart. Subsequently, the Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator, Chen Lian 陳濂, comforted and cared for the war-scarred populace, …

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
文地之文聖人之文實出一揆而
文之所在道之所在也亦心之所
在也學者文焉而推致之則心純
道純而文無不純用以經體賛元
康時酬物樹大名建丕烈一求給
於文而不窮矣是以
列聖相承咸崇科目而人材之盛政教
之隆媲美成周有不知孰前而孰
punctuated: 文、地之文、聖人之文，實出一揆。而文之所在，道之所在也，亦心之所在也。學者文焉而推致之，則心純、道純而文無不純。用以經體賛元，康時酬物，樹大名，建丕烈，一求給於文而不窮矣。是以列聖相承，咸崇科目，而人材之盛、政教之隆，媲美成周，有不知孰前而孰
translation_en: …of heaven], the patterns of earth, and the writings of the sages truly issue from a single principle. Where writing resides is where the Way resides, and also where the mind resides. When scholars engage with literary learning and extend it to the utmost, their minds become pure, their grasp of the Way becomes pure, and their writing is in every respect pure. Used to order the body politic and assist the primal governance, to bring peace to the times and respond to all affairs, to establish a great name and achieve vast meritorious deeds—all these may be sought and supplied entirely from literary learning without ever being exhausted. Therefore, as the successive sacred emperors have inherited the throne one after another, all have revered the examination system; the flourishing of talented men and the prosperity of governance and instruction rival the beauty of the glorious Zhou dynasty, to the point that one cannot tell which came before and which…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
後也猗歟休哉成化戊子歲當大
比廣東藩臬重臣禮聘儒碩以典
文衡至期合十郡士餘千人而三
試之得其文之弗畔於道者七十
有五人遵解額也小錄既成僉謂
克廉宜有一言序之惟東廣實古
綏服之外自入
聖朝沐浴清化人材儒術始埒甸侯而
數十年間西冦剽掠以東滋久滋
熾由是米鹽戎馬之事紛紛起矣
凡郡邑之當其衝者絃誦為之絕
響自餘亦皆弊於供億轉輸士習
不能不少間焉乙酉之秋
聖神天子不忍邊氓之顛越也爰
命太監陳瑄等率師征伐而今奉
勅提督兩廣軍務左副都御史姑蘇韓
punctuated: 後也。猗歟休哉！成化戊子歲當大比，廣東藩臬重臣禮聘儒碩，以典文衡。至期，合十郡士餘千人而三試之，得其文之弗畔於道者七十有五人，遵解額也。小錄既成，僉謂克廉宜有一言序之。惟東廣實古綏服之外，自入聖朝，沐浴清化，人材儒術，始埒甸侯。而數十年間，西冦剽掠以東，滋久滋熾，由是米鹽戎馬之事紛紛起矣。凡郡邑之當其衝者，絃誦為之絕響；自餘亦皆弊於供億轉輸，士習不能不少間焉。乙酉之秋，聖神天子不忍邊氓之顛越也，爰命太監陳瑄等率師征伐，而今奉勅提督兩廣軍務、左副都御史姑蘇韓…
translation_en:
…and which came after. Oh, how magnificent!

In the wuzi year of the Chenghua reign (1468), the year of the triennial examination, the senior officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions of Guangdong respectfully invited eminent Confucian scholars to take charge of evaluating the compositions. When the appointed time arrived, more than a thousand scholars from the ten prefectures were gathered and tested in three sessions. Seventy-five men whose essays did not depart from the Way were selected, in compliance with the provincial quota. Once the examination record was completed, everyone said that I, Kelian, ought to write a few words as a preface to it.

Eastern Guang (Guangdong) truly lies beyond the ancient "Pacified Zone" (suifu). Since entering our Sacred Dynasty and bathing in its pure transformative influence, its men of talent and Confucian learning have for the first time come to equal those of the royal domain and the inner feudatories. Yet over the past several decades, bandits from the west have plundered eastward, growing ever more rampant the longer they persisted, and because of this, the affairs of grain, salt, and military horses arose in great confusion. In all the prefectures and counties that lay in the path of their assaults, the sound of stringed instruments and chanting of classics fell silent; the remaining areas were likewise exhausted by provisioning and transport, so that the scholarly ethos could not avoid suffering some interruption.

In the autumn of the yiyou year (1465), the sagely and divine Son of Heaven, unable to bear the ruin and displacement of the frontier people, commanded the Grand Eunuch Chen Xuan 陳瑄 and others to lead an army on a punitive expedition, while the Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and Imperial Commissioner Supreme Commander of Military Affairs in Liangguang, Han [Yong] 韓[雍] of Gusu…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
雍實總制之遠謨雄畧功成再造
民安於廬士奮於學繼而奉
勅巡撫右副都御史四明陳濂加意作
新文教用興而左布政使江浦張
瑄右布政使天台夏塤左參政孝
感張瓚桂林鄧義右參政安成劉
鉞左參議吉水劉諭右參議三山
王英副使山陰唐彬餘姚徐海僉
===
事姑蘇戈立顧儼華亭張祚王祐
施謙鬱林陶魯莆田陳貴亦皆同
心符德安養不懈故前諸科士之
集試者大率不過七百而今實倍
之至於臨事提調監試以至克廉
等內外執事罔不精白一心綱維
防範鑑別取舍惟公惟慎可以質
諸鬼神而無愧矣用是所得之文
punctuated: 雍實總制之。遠謨雄畧，功成再造，民安於廬，士奮於學。繼而奉勅巡撫右副都御史四明陳濂加意作新，文教用興；而左布政使江浦張瑄、右布政使天台夏塤、左參政孝感張瓚、桂林鄧義、右參政安成劉鉞、左參議吉水劉諭、右參議三山王英、副使山陰唐彬、餘姚徐海、僉事姑蘇戈立、顧儼、華亭張祚、王祐、施謙、鬱林陶魯、莆田陳貴，亦皆同心符德，安養不懈。故前諸科士之集試者，大率不過七百，而今實倍之。至於臨事提調、監試，以至克廉等內外執事，罔不精白一心。綱維防範，鑑別取舍，惟公惟慎，可以質諸鬼神而無愧矣。用是所得之文，
translation_en: …Yong 韓雍 assumed overall command of the campaign. Through his far-reaching counsel and heroic strategy, he achieved the feat of reconstructing the region, so that the common people rested peacefully in their homes and the scholars exerted themselves in learning. Subsequently, the Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Chen Lian 陳濂 of Siming 四明, who served as Grand Coordinator by imperial command, paid special attention to renewal and invigoration, whereby literary and moral education flourished. Furthermore, Left Administration Commissioner Zhang Xuan 張瑄 of Jiangpu 江浦; Right Administration Commissioner Xia Xun 夏塤 of Tiantai 天台; Left Administration Vice Commissioners Zhang Zan 張瓚 of Xiaogan 孝感 and Deng Yi 鄧義 of Guilin 桂林; Right Administration Vice Commissioner Liu Yue 劉鉞 of Ancheng 安成; Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Liu Yu 劉諭 of Jishui 吉水; Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Wang Ying 王英 of Sanshan 三山; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Tang Bin 唐彬 of Shanyin 山陰 and Xu Hai 徐海 of Yuyao 餘姚; and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Ge Li 戈立 and Gu Yan 顧儼 of Gusu 姑蘇, Zhang Zuo 張祚, Wang You 王祐, and Shi Qian 施謙 of Huating 華亭, Tao Lu 陶魯 of Yulin 鬱林, and Chen Gui 陳貴 of Putian 莆田—all likewise shared the same mind and matched in virtue, tirelessly pacifying and nurturing the people. Therefore, whereas in previous examinations the scholars who gathered to be tested generally numbered no more than seven hundred, today the number has in fact doubled. When it came to the actual proceedings, from the Proctors and Censors-in-Surveillance down to Kelian 克廉 and the other inner and outer functionaries, there was none who did not maintain pure and untarnished devotion with a single mind. In maintaining order and taking precautions, as well as in evaluating, distinguishing, selecting, and rejecting, they were solely impartial and cautious, such that they could stand before ghosts and spirits without shame. For this reason, the essays obtained…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
皆氣充辭正而一純夫道即弗純
者不與焉諸士子登名薦書固華
矣繼自今偕海內之士角捷禮闈
對揚
大廷而皆有所授焉夫所授有小大
一自吾所業之文推而行之所謂
經體賛元康時酬務樹名建烈者
要皆與成周之吉人多士聯休共
===
美於無窮斯為科目增重而無忝
也萬有一焉曲學以阿世舍己以
從人所以負於古負於今負於
上負於下而負於克廉等亦多矣諸士
子勉旃
福建福州府懷安縣儒學教諭張克廉
謹序
punctuated:
皆氣充辭正，而一純夫道，即弗純者不與焉。諸士子登名薦書，固華矣。繼自今，偕海內之士角捷禮闈，對揚大廷，而皆有所授焉。夫所授有小大，一自吾所業之文推而行之，所謂經體賛元、康時酬務、樹名建烈者，要皆與成周之吉人多士聯休共美於無窮，斯為科目增重而無忝也。萬有一焉，曲學以阿世，舍己以從人，所以負於古、負於今、負於上、負於下，而負於克廉等亦多矣。諸士子勉旃！
福建福州府懷安縣儒學教諭張克廉謹序。
translation_en:
… are all vigorous in spirit and upright in expression, and uniformly pure in the Way; any that were not pure were not included. For all of you scholars to have your names entered on the list of recommended candidates is indeed glorious. From this point onward, you will join the scholars of the entire realm to compete for victory in the Metropolitan Examination, respond to the Emperor's inquiries in the Great Court, and all receive official appointments. Now, appointments may be minor or major, but if you simply extend and put into practice the learning of the essays you have studied—what is meant by ordering the state structure and assisting the primal harmony, bringing peace to the times and meeting the demands of affairs, establishing a reputation and achieving illustrious deeds—in sum, you will all join the worthy men and numerous officers of the flourishing Zhou in sharing splendor and beauty without end. Thus you will add weight to the examination system and bring no disgrace to it. Should there be even one in ten thousand who distorts his learning to flatter the age, or abandons his own principles to follow others, how greatly he would fail antiquity, fail the present, fail the Sovereign above, fail the people below, and fail Kelian and his colleagues as well! May all you scholars strive therein!
Respectfully prefaced by Zhang Kelian 張克廉, Instructor of the Confucian School of Huai'an County in Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian.

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
成化四年廣東鄉試
提調官
廣東等處承宣布政使司右布政使夏壎〔宗成浙江天台縣人辛未進士〕
廣東等處承宣布政使司左參政張瓚〔宗器湖廣孝感縣人戊辰進士〕
監試官
廣東等處提刑按察司僉事戈立〔允中直隸吳縣人監生〕
廣東等處提刑按察司僉事張祚〔永錫直隸華亭縣人甲戌進士〕
考試官
===
福建福州府懷安縣儒學教諭張克廉〔以清直隸上海縣人丙子貢士〕
河南開封府洧川縣儒學教諭陳信〔彥實直隸山陽縣人庚午貢士〕
同考試官
浙江紹興府蕭山縣儒學教諭鄭遷善〔遷善福建莆田縣人甲子貢士〕
直隸蘇州府常熟縣儒學教諭謝紘〔維冕江西樂安縣人庚午貢士〕
江西廣信府儒學訓導華黼〔廷章浙江餘姚縣人己卯貢士〕
浙江金華府義烏縣儒學訓導郁珎〔君聘應天府江浦縣人丙子貢士〕
直隸安慶府太湖縣儒學訓導周邦熈〔堯佐江西安福縣人癸酉貢士〕
punctuated:
成化四年廣東鄉試

提調官：
廣東等處承宣布政使司右布政使夏壎〔宗成，浙江天台縣人，辛未進士〕。
廣東等處承宣布政使司左參政張瓚〔宗器，湖廣孝感縣人，戊辰進士〕。

監試官：
廣東等處提刑按察司僉事戈立〔允中，直隸吳縣人，監生〕。
廣東等處提刑按察司僉事張祚〔永錫，直隸華亭縣人，甲戌進士〕。

考試官：
福建福州府懷安縣儒學教諭張克廉〔以清，直隸上海縣人，丙子貢士〕。
河南開封府洧川縣儒學教諭陳信〔彥實，直隸山陽縣人，庚午貢士〕。

同考試官：
浙江紹興府蕭山縣儒學教諭鄭遷善〔遷善，福建莆田縣人，甲子貢士〕。
直隸蘇州府常熟縣儒學教諭謝紘〔維冕，江西樂安縣人，庚午貢士〕。
江西廣信府儒學訓導華黼〔廷章，浙江餘姚縣人，己卯貢士〕。
浙江金華府義烏縣儒學訓導郁珎〔君聘，應天府江浦縣人，丙子貢士〕。
直隸安慶府太湖縣儒學訓導周邦熈〔堯佐，江西安福縣人，癸酉貢士〕。
translation_en:
Guangdong Provincial Examination of the Fourth Year of the Chenghua Era (1468)

Proctors:
Xia Xun 夏壎, Right Administration Commissioner of the Guangdong Provincial Administration Commission (courtesy name Zongcheng 宗成, a native of Tiantai County, Zhejiang, and a metropolitan graduate of the xinwei year [1451]).
Zhang Zan 張瓚, Left Administration Vice Commissioner of the Guangdong Provincial Administration Commission (courtesy name Zongqi 宗器, a native of Xiaogan County, Huguang, and a metropolitan graduate of the wuchen year [1448]).

Monitoring Officials:
Ge Li 戈立, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of the Guangdong Provincial Surveillance Commission (courtesy name Yunzhong 允中, a native of Wu County, Zhili, and a National University Student).
Zhang Zuo 張祚, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of the Guangdong Provincial Surveillance Commission (courtesy name Yongxi 永錫, a native of Huating County, Zhili, and a metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year [1454]).

Examiners:
Zhang Kelian 張克廉, Instructor in the Confucian School of Huai'an County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian (courtesy name Yiqing 以清, a native of Shanghai County, Zhili, and a tribute scholar [provincial graduate] of the bingzi year [1456]).
Chen Xin 陳信, Instructor in the Confucian School of Weichuan County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan (courtesy name Yanshi 彥實, a native of Shanyang County, Zhili, and a tribute scholar [provincial graduate] of the gengwu year [1450]).

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第一場
四書
大宰問於子貢曰夫子聖者與何其多
能也子貢曰固天縱之將聖又多能
也
子庶民則百姓勸来百工則財用足柔
遠人則四方歸之懷諸侯則天下畏
之
===
孔子登東山而小魯登太山而小天下
故觀於海者難為水遊於聖人之門
者難為言
易
九二之孚有喜也
進得位往有功也進以正可以正邦也
初六藉用白茅无咎子曰苟錯諸地而
可矣藉之用茅何咎之有慎之至也
punctuated:
第一場

四書
大宰問於子貢曰：「夫子聖者與？何其多能也！」子貢曰：「固天縱之將聖，又多能也。」
子庶民，則百姓勸；来百工，則財用足；柔遠人，則四方歸之；懷諸侯，則天下畏之。
孔子登東山而小魯，登太山而小天下。故觀於海者難為水，遊於聖人之門者難為言。

易
九二之孚，有喜也。進得位，往有功也；進以正，可以正邦也。
「初六，藉用白茅，无咎。」子曰：「苟錯諸地而可矣，藉之用茅，何咎之有？慎之至也。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
1. A Great Officer asked Zigong (子貢), "Is the Master a sage? How is it that he has so many abilities?" Zigong replied, "Certainly Heaven has endowed him so widely that he is a great sage, and moreover he has many abilities." (Analects 9.6)
2. By treating the common people as one's children, the hundred surnames are encouraged; by attracting the various artisans, wealth and resources are made sufficient; by showing tenderness to men from afar, people from all four quarters will turn to him; by cherishing the feudal lords, the whole world will hold him in awe. (Doctrine of the Mean 20)
3. Confucius ascended the Eastern Mountain (Dongshan 東山) and Lu (魯) seemed small to him; he ascended Mount Tai (Taishan 太山) and all under Heaven seemed small to him. Therefore, to one who has gazed upon the sea, it is difficult for other waters to seem anything; to one who has roamed within the gate of the sage, it is difficult for other words to seem anything. (Mencius 7A.24)

Book of Changes (Yi 易)
1. "The sincerity of the Nine in the second place": there is joy. Advancing and attaining its proper position, going forward brings merit. Advancing with correctness, one can rectify the state. (Hexagram 20, Guan 觀, "Commentary on the Line Statements" [Xiaoxiang 小象], and Hexagram 53, Jian 漸, "Commentary on the Judgments" [Tuanzhuan 彖傳])
2. "'Six at the beginning: For placing things underneath, one uses white cogon grass; there is no blame.' The Master said: 'If one simply places them on the ground, that would be acceptable. When one places white cogon grass underneath them, what blame could there be? It is the utmost caution. …'" (Hexagram 28, Daguo 大過, and "Commentary on the Appended Phrases," Part I [Xici shang 繫辭上] 8)

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
夫茅之為物薄而用可重也慎斯術
也以往其无所失矣
動萬物者莫疾乎雷撓萬物者莫疾乎
風燥萬物者莫熯乎火說萬物者莫
說乎澤潤萬物者莫潤乎水終萬物
始萬物者莫盛乎艮故水火相逮雷
風不相悖山澤通氣
書
===
天工人其代之天叙有典勅我五典五
惇哉天秩有禮自我五禮有庸哉同
寅恊恭和衷哉天命有德五服五章
哉天討有罪五刑五用哉政事懋哉
懋哉天聰明自我民聰明天明畏自
我民明威達于上下敬哉有土
其不能誠于小民今休王不敢後用顧
畏于民碞王来紹上帝自服于土中
punctuated:
夫茅之為物薄，而用可重也。慎斯術也以往，其无所失矣。」
「動萬物者莫疾乎雷，撓萬物者莫疾乎風，燥萬物者莫熯乎火，說萬物者莫說乎澤，潤萬物者莫潤乎水，終萬物始萬物者莫盛乎艮。故水火相逮，雷風不相悖，山澤通氣。」

《書》
「天工人其代之。天叙有典，勅我五典五惇哉！天秩有禮，自我五禮有庸哉！同寅恊恭和衷哉！天命有德，五服五章哉！天討有罪，五刑五用哉！政事懋哉懋哉！天聰明，自我民聰明；天明畏，自我民明威。達于上下，敬哉有土！」
「其不能誠于小民，今休。王不敢後，用顧畏于民碞。王来紹上帝，自服于土中。
translation_en:
…Now, white grass as a thing is trivial, yet the use to which it can be put is weighty. If one goes forward practicing this art of caution, he will suffer no loss.”
“In stirring the myriad things, nothing is swifter than thunder; in bending the myriad things, nothing is swifter than wind; in drying the myriad things, nothing is more parching than fire; in gladdening the myriad things, nothing is more gladdening than the marsh; in moistening the myriad things, nothing is more moistening than water; in bringing the myriad things to an end and bringing the myriad things to a new beginning, nothing is more flourishing than Gen [Keeping Still / the Mountain]. Therefore water and fire complement each other, thunder and wind do not conflict with each other, and mountain and marsh communicate their vital breaths.”

Book of Documents (Shu):
“It is Heaven’s work that man acts on behalf of. Heaven has set forth the invariable relationships; let us set in order our five relationships and see that all five are generously observed! Heaven has ordained the rites; let our five rites be constantly practiced! Let us share in reverent harmony and concord of heart! Heaven bestows charges upon the virtuous—there are the five grades of ceremonial dress with their five emblems of distinction! Heaven punishes the guilty—there are the five punishments with their five applications! In affairs of governance, be diligent, be diligent! Heaven’s hearing and seeing proceed from our people’s hearing and seeing; Heaven’s discerning of theawesome and dreadful proceeds from our people’s discerning of majesty. This reaches above and below—be reverent, O possessor of the land!”
“Whether he can or cannot achieve sincerity toward the common people, the present offers an auspicious opportunity. May the King not dare to lag behind, being mindful and fearful of the perilousness of the people. May the King come to succeed to the work of the Lord on High, and personally undertake his duties in the center of the land. …

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
旦曰其作大邑其自時配皇天毖祀
于上下其自時中乂王厥有成命治
民今休
自作不和爾惟和哉爾室不睦爾惟和
哉爾邑克明爾惟克勤乃事爾尚不
忌于凶德亦則以穆穆在乃位克閱
于乃邑謀介
惟察惟法其審克之
===
詩
顯允方叔征伐玁狁蠻荆来威
受天之祜四方来賀
何求為我以戾庶正
皇皇后帝皇祖后稷享以騂犧是饗是
宜降福既多周公皇祖亦其福女秋
而載嘗夏而楅衡白牡騂剛犧尊將
將毛炰胾羹籩豆大房萬舞洋洋孝
punctuated:
旦曰：「其作大邑，其自時配皇天，毖祀于上下，其自時中乂。王厥有成命，治民今休。」
「自作不和，爾惟和哉；爾室不睦，爾惟和哉。爾邑克明，爾惟克勤乃事。爾尚不忌于凶德，亦則以穆穆在乃位，克閱于乃邑謀介。」
「惟察惟法，其審克之。」
詩
「顯允方叔，征伐玁狁，蠻荆来威。」
「受天之祜，四方来賀。」
「何求為我，以戾庶正。」
「皇皇后帝，皇祖后稷。享以騂犧，是饗是宜。降福既多，周公皇祖，亦其福女。秋而載嘗，夏而楅衡。白牡騂剛，犧尊將將。毛炰胾羹，籩豆大房。萬舞洋洋，孝
translation_en:
… Dan [the Duke of Zhou] said: "Having built this great city, he shall from here be a counterpart to August Heaven; he shall carefully offer sacrifices to the spirits above and below, and from this center he shall govern. The king, having fulfilled the mandate, will govern the people, and now there will be prosperity."

"When unrest arises of itself, do you bring harmony! When your household is not at peace, do you bring harmony! When your cities are able to be clear-sighted, you will have been diligent in your affairs. If you do not shun on account of evil dispositions, and thus remain reverently in your positions, you will be able to inspect your cities and take counsel for assistance."

"Be discerning, be lawful, and examine into them carefully to attain the truth."

Book of Odes (Shi):

"Illustrious and true is Fang Shu, who went to punish the Xianyun, and the Man of Jing came in awe."

"He receives the blessing of Heaven, and from the four quarters they come to offer congratulations."

"What can it do for us, so as to settle the heads of the departments?"

"Most august is the Sovereign on High, and our august ancestor Hou Ji! We offer the red sacrificial victim; they enjoy it, they approve it, and send down abundant blessings. The Duke of Zhou, our august ancestor, will also bless you. In autumn we perform the chang sacrifice, and in summer we fasten the crossbars to the horns of the victims: the white bull and the red one; the victim-shaped goblets in grand array; the singed pig, the sliced meat, the broth; the bamboo and wooden vessels, and the great stand; the wan dance in all its grandeur. text:
孫有慶
春秋
宋人伐鄭圍長葛〔隱公五年〕冬宋人取長
葛〔隱公六年〕
九月丁卯子同生〔桓公六年〕甲午衛侯衎復
歸于衛〔襄公二十六年〕吳子使札来聘〔襄公二〕
〔十九年〕取鄫〔昭公四年〕

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考禮正刑一德以尊于天子
親者屬也自仁率親等而上之至于祖
自義率祖順而下之至于禰是故人
道親親也
不興其藝不能樂學故君子之於學也
藏焉脩焉息焉遊焉夫然故安其學
而親其師樂其友而信其道
仁有三與仁同功而異情與仁同功其
===
仁未可知也與仁同過然後其仁可
知也仁者安仁知者利仁畏罪者強
仁
第二場
論
聖人教人有定本
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢文帝親率羣臣勸農賜民今年田
punctuated:
考禮、正刑、一德，以尊于天子。
親者，屬也。自仁率親，等而上之至于祖；自義率祖，順而下之至于禰。是故人道親親也。
不興其藝，不能樂學。故君子之於學也，藏焉，脩焉，息焉，遊焉。夫然，故安其學而親其師，樂其友而信其道。
仁有三，與仁同功而異情。與仁同功，其仁未可知也；與仁同過，然後其仁可知也。仁者安仁，知者利仁，畏罪者強仁。

第二場
論
聖人教人有定本
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢文帝親率羣臣勸農賜民今年田
translation_en:
"To examine the rites, rectify the punishments, and unify morality, so as to honor the Son of Heaven."
"Kinship means connection. Proceeding from benevolence to follow the principle of kinship, one ascends by degrees up to the distant ancestor; proceeding from righteousness to follow the ancestor, one descends in order down to the deceased father. Therefore, the way of humanity is to feel affection for one's kin."
"If one does not take delight in the subsidiary arts, one cannot find joy in learning. Therefore, in his pursuit of learning, the gentleman stores it up, cultivates it, rests in it, and wanders in it. Being thus, he rests content in his learning and feels affection for his teacher, takes joy in his friends and has faith in his Way."
"There are three kinds of benevolence, which share the same achievements as benevolence yet differ in motivation. When people share the same achievements as the benevolent, their benevolence cannot yet be known; when they share the same faults as the benevolent, only then can their benevolence be known. The benevolent rest in benevolence, the wise find advantage in benevolence, and those who fear punishment force themselves to practice benevolence."

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天明命
列聖繼作文治大興薄海内外聲教遠暨而
人倫無不明矣伏遇
宣宗章皇帝體道謙冲游心典籍又於萬幾
之暇采古今之嘉言善行有關於倫
理者萃以成編名曰五倫書而
頒布天下以示勸其立教垂訓之意盖與
列聖同一心也欽誦所載君道之目五十而
===
以聖德聖學為之冠以聖德言之有
如天如神如日如雲者矣其視克寬
克仁克明克忠者為孰優有臨下以
簡御衆以寬者矣其視不泄邇不忘
遠者為孰賢以聖學言之有受丹書
訪洪範者矣與開學館而銳情經術
者孰與耶有舊學甘盤克邁乃訓者
矣與在軍旅而手不釋卷者孰勤耶
punctuated: 天明命，列聖繼作，文治大興，薄海内外，聲教遠暨，而人倫無不明矣。伏遇宣宗章皇帝體道謙冲，游心典籍，又於萬幾之暇，采古今之嘉言善行有關於倫理者，萃以成編，名曰《五倫書》，而頒布天下，以示勸。其立教垂訓之意，盖與列聖同一心也。欽誦所載君道之目五十，而以聖德、聖學為之冠。以聖德言之，有如天、如神、如日、如雲者矣，其視克寬、克仁、克明、克忠者為孰優？有臨下以簡、御衆以寬者矣，其視不泄邇、不忘遠者為孰賢？以聖學言之，有受《丹書》、訪《洪範》者矣，與開學館而銳情經術者孰與耶？有舊學甘盤、克邁乃訓者矣，與在軍旅而手不釋卷者孰勤耶？
translation_en:
… the bright Mandate of Heaven, the successive sacred emperors arose one after another, and civil governance greatly flourished. Within and beyond the cuatro seas, royal prestige and moral instruction reached afar, and there were none among the human relationships that were not made clear. We have humbly encountered the Emperor Xuanzong Zhang (宣宗章皇帝, the Xuande Emperor), who embodied the Way in modest humility and let his mind roam among the canonical classics. Furthermore, in his leisure from the myriad affairs of state, he gathered admirable words and good deeds from antiquity and the present that relate to moral principles, compiling them into a work titled the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu 五倫書), and promulgated it throughout the empire in order to offer encouragement. His intention in establishing teaching and handing down instruction was indeed of one mind with the successive sacred emperors.

Reverently reciting what is recorded therein: under the Way of the Ruler there are fifty headings, headed by "Sacred Virtue" and "Sacred Learning." Speaking with respect to Sacred Virtue: there was one whose virtue was like heaven, like a spirit, like the sun, and like the clouds [Emperor Yao]—how does he compare in excellence to the one who was capable of generosity, benevolence, clarity, and loyalty [King Tang]? There was one who oversaw his subordinates with simplicity and governed the multitude with generosity [Emperor Shun]—how does he compare in worthiness to the one who did not treat familiarly those who were near and did not forget those who were distant [King Wu]? Speaking with respect to Sacred Learning: there was one who received the Cinnabar Writing (Danshu 丹書) and inquired into the Great Plan (Hongfan 洪範) [King Wu]—how does he compare to the one who opened an academy of learning and devoted his passion keenly to the arts of the Classics [Emperor Taizong of Tang]? There was one who formerly studied with Gan Pan (甘盤) and was able to advance in his teachings [King Gaozong of Shang / Wu Ding]—who was more diligent, he or the one who even amidst military campaigns never put down a scroll from his hand [Emperor Guangwu of Han]? …

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
臣道之目四十有八而以輔德經國
為之首以輔德言之無怠無荒四夷
来王謨訓切矣其視作書賦詩以戒
王者為何如脩德脩刑動天以誠規
戒深矣其視手疏八事以諫帝者又
何如以經國言之决九川弼五服厥
功茂矣方之經營四方而告成于王
者又孰愈耶辨方正位體國經野其
===
績偉矣較之出納王命而為王喉舌
者又孰勝耶三十七字以詔後人父
道善矣視以田十頃桑千株遺子孫
者同歟異歟清朝履霜援琴而歌子
道盡矣視畊歷山號旻天而終身怨
慕者是歟非歟寧忤帝旨不以貴戚
易陋妻夫道之善也婦能却金璧之
聘辭夫人之位而守節不渝者心豈
punctuated: 臣道之目四十有八，而以輔德、經國為之首。以輔德言之，「無怠無荒，四夷来王」，謨訓切矣，其視作書賦詩以戒王者為何如？脩德脩刑，動天以誠，規戒深矣，其視手疏八事以諫帝者又何如？以經國言之，决九川，弼五服，厥功茂矣，方之經營四方而告成于王者又孰愈耶？辨方正位，體國經野，其績偉矣，較之出納王命而為王喉舌者又孰勝耶？三十七字以詔後人，父道善矣，視以田十頃、桑千株遺子孫者同歟異歟？清朝履霜，援琴而歌，子道盡矣，視畊歷山、號旻天而終身怨慕者是歟非歟？寧忤帝旨，不以貴戚易陋妻，夫道之善也；婦能却金璧之聘，辭夫人之位，而守節不渝者，心豈…
translation_en: The headings under the Way of the Minister are forty-eight in number, and assisting in virtue and ordering the state stand at their head. Speaking in terms of assisting in virtue: "Do not be idle, do not be negligent, and the four barbarous tribes will come to acknowledge the sovereign's rule"—how earnest was this counsel and instruction! How does it compare with composing books and presenting poems in order to admonish the king? Cultivating virtue and regulating punishments to move Heaven through sincerity—how profound was this admonition! And how does it compare with writing out a memorial in one's own hand on eight matters to remonstrate with the emperor? Speaking in terms of ordering the state: dredging the nine rivers and establishing the five domains—how abundant was this achievement! Compared with planning and managing the four quarters and reporting completion to the king, which is superior? Determining the directions and fixing the positions, laying out the capital and dividing the countryside—how magnificent was this accomplishment! Compared with issuing and receiving the royal commands and serving as the king's throat and tongue, which excels? Leaving a testament of thirty-seven characters to instruct descendants shows excellence in the Way of the Father; compared with bequeathing ten qing of fields and a thousand mulberry trees to one's sons and grandsons, are they the same or different? Treading on the morning frost and taking up the zither to sing fulfills the Way of the Son to the utmost; compared with plowing on Mount Li, crying out to compassionate Heaven, and harboring lifelong yearning and remorse, is it right or wrong? Preferring to defy an imperial decree rather than exchange a humble wife for an imperial relative exemplifies excellence in the Way of the Husband; as for a wife who was able to reject betrothal gifts of gold and jade, decline the rank of noble lady, and preserve her chastity without wavering, how could her heart…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
異乎寧違父命不以寵祿傷天倫弟
道之善也兄能輕千乘之國效泰伯
之讓而秉德不回者心何厚乎至若
朋友之倫有同舉孝廉而自許以膠
漆者有同游太學而相托以死生者
有念及其親以柳易播而不計其利害
者有三仕三逐三戰三北而不以其
為柔怯者是又友道之善而凡學者
皆不可以不知也諸士子游學庠序
欽服
聖訓有日矣其詳言之毋諉曰請俟更僕
問六經四書之所載微辭奧義廣大悉
備未可以一二究其涯涘姑舉其槩
評之可乎故法象莫大於天地而有
陰陽剛柔之妙陰陽莫妙於鬼神而
不無費隱小大之別上天所賦之謂
punctuated:
異乎？寧違父命，不以寵祿傷天倫，弟道之善也；兄能輕千乘之國，效泰伯之讓，而秉德不回者，心何厚乎？至若朋友之倫，有同舉孝廉而自許以膠漆者，有同游太學而相托以死生者，有念及其親，以柳易播，而不計其利害者，有三仕三逐、三戰三北，而不以其為柔怯者，是又友道之善，而凡學者皆不可以不知也。諸士子游學庠序，欽服聖訓有日矣，其詳言之，毋諉曰「請俟更僕」。

問：六經、四書之所載，微辭奧義，廣大悉備，未可以一二究其涯涘，姑舉其槩評之，可乎？故法象莫大於天地，而有陰陽剛柔之妙；陰陽莫妙於鬼神，而不無費隱小大之別。上天所賦之謂…
translation_en:
…different? Rather disobeying a father's command so as not to harm the natural bond of kinship for the sake of favor and emolument—this is the excellence of the way of a younger brother; and when an elder brother is able to treat lightly a state of a thousand chariots, emulating the yielding of Taibo 泰伯 and holding fast to virtue without wavering, how generous is his heart! As for the human relationship of friends: there were those who were jointly recommended as Filial and Incorrupt (xiaolian) and regarded their bond as like glue and lacquer; those who studied together at the National University (Taixue) and entrusted life and death to one another; one who, thinking of his friend's parent, offered to exchange Liuzhou 柳州 for Bozhou 播州 without calculating personal advantage or harm; and one who knew a friend who took office three times and was dismissed three times, fought in three battles and fled three times, without considering him weak or cowardly. These, in turn, exemplify the excellence of the way of friendship, of which no scholar can afford to be ignorant. You gentlemen have studied in the local schools and have reverently submitted to the Sacred Instructions for many days now. Expound upon these matters in detail, and do not excuse yourselves by saying, "Please allow a change of attendants before I finish."

Question: That which is recorded in the Six Classics (Liujing) and the Four Books (Sishu) contains subtle words and profound meanings, vast and complete in every respect, such that one cannot exhaust their bounds through one or two points; yet may we tentatively raise their general outlines to appraise them? Now, among visible models and images there is nothing greater than Heaven and Earth, which possess the subtle wonder of yin and yang, the firm and the yielding; within yin and yang there is nothing more wondrous than ghosts and spirits (guishen), which are not without distinctions of wide-reaching and hidden, small and great. What High Heaven confers is called…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
命何以有正不正之分人物所受之
謂性何以有謂不謂之異性率於已
之謂道而一二五之目何所指耶道
得於心之謂德而三六九之類何所
在耶人道莫大於仁義而何以見其
有健順分錯之妙制作莫大於禮樂
而何以見其有本末偏全之論誠乃
眞實無妄之理何以有天道人道之
===
分忠恕盡已推已之謂何以有以天
以人之別君臣人道之大倫而皇帝
王伯之殊號公卿大夫士之殊名與
其所各當盡之道又何所辨而何所
在耶父子天屬之至親而嫡繼慈養
之異等大宗小宗之異禰與其所當
為之服又何所別而何所處耶凡若
此者皆天理人道之大端而凡學者
punctuated: 命，何以有正不正之分？人物所受之謂性，何以有謂不謂之異？性率於已之謂道，而一二五之目何所指耶？道得於心之謂德，而三六九之類何所在耶？人道莫大於仁義，而何以見其有健順分錯之妙？制作莫大於禮樂，而何以見其有本末偏全之論？誠乃眞實無妄之理，何以有天道人道之分？忠恕盡已推已之謂，何以有以天以人之別？君臣，人道之大倫，而皇、帝、王、伯之殊號，公、卿、大夫、士之殊名，與其所各當盡之道，又何所辨而何所在耶？父子，天屬之至親，而嫡、繼、慈、養之異等，大宗、小宗之異禰，與其所當為之服，又何所別而何所處耶？凡若此者，皆天理人道之大端，而凡學者
translation_en: … decree; why is there a distinction between what is regular and what is irregular? What human beings and things receive is called nature; why is there a difference between what is called nature and what is not called nature? Following nature in oneself is called the Way; what do the headings of one, two, and five refer to? The Way attained in the mind is called virtue; where are the categories of the three, the six, and the nine to be found? Nothing in the Way of Man is greater than benevolence and righteousness; how can we see the subtlety of their robustness and docility, their division and alternation? Nothing in human institutions is greater than rites and music; how can we see the discussions of their roots and branches, their partiality and completeness? Sincerity is the principle of truth and freedom from falsehood; why is there a division between the Way of Heaven and the Way of Man? Conscientiousness and altruism mean exhausting oneself and extending from oneself; why is there a distinction between acting by Heaven and acting by Man? Ruler and minister are a great human relationship; as for the differing titles of August One, Emperor, King, and Hegemon, the differing designations of Duke, Minister, Grand Master, and Servitor, and the Way that each ought to fulfill, how are they distinguished and wherein do they reside? Father and son are the closest of natural kin; as for the differing grades of principal,継 [step-], compassionate, and adoptive mothers, the differing ancestral shrines of the great lineage and lesser lineages, and the mourning garments that ought to be worn for them, how are they differentiated and how are they managed? All such matters are the great essentials of Heavenly Principle and the Way of Man, which all scholars…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不可以不講也其詳言之
問考論古人行事之跡不越乎載籍而
載籍之辭未可盡信也同時而仕同
堂而語十人書之其事各異盖聞見
有詳畧文辭有工拙意向有高下坐
是失其真者亦多矣况於數百年或
千餘歳之相遠耳不聞其言目不睹
其事意揣心搆以補其所不足而増
===
其所未備則其失真不既多矣乎甞
觀載籍與儒先君子之論未甞不衆
難填胸羣疑滿腹也姑舉其一二顯
明而易斷者以商確焉燕昭王築臺
招賢而樂毅自魏國来未幾至上将
軍并護趙楚韓魏之兵以伐齊連下
七十餘城而即墨與莒不拔昔人謂
其庶幾湯武又謂其行王道之過漢
punctuated:
不可以不講也。其詳言之。

問：考論古人行事之跡，不越乎載籍，而載籍之辭未可盡信也。同時而仕，同堂而語，十人書之，其事各異。盖聞見有詳畧，文辭有工拙，意向有高下，坐是失其真者亦多矣。况於數百年或千餘歳之相遠，耳不聞其言，目不睹其事，意揣心搆，以補其所不足，而増其所未備，則其失真不既多矣乎？甞觀載籍與儒先君子之論，未甞不衆難填胸、羣疑滿腹也。姑舉其一二顯明而易斷者以商確焉。燕昭王築臺招賢，而樂毅自魏國来，未幾至上将軍，并護趙、楚、韓、魏之兵以伐齊，連下七十餘城，而即墨與莒不拔。昔人謂其庶幾湯、武，又謂其行王道之過。漢
translation_en:
… cannot leave unexamined. Discuss this in detail.

Question: When investigating and discussing the deeds of the ancients, one cannot go beyond written records, yet the words of written records cannot be entirely believed. When men serve in office at the same time and speak together in the same hall, if ten people write down an account, the events in each will differ. This is because what they heard and saw varies in detail or brevity, their literary expression varies in skill or clumsiness, and their intentions vary in elevation or baseness; for these reasons, there are many cases in which the truth is lost. How much more so when separated by several hundred or over a thousand years, when one's ears have not heard their words and one's eyes have not witnessed their deeds, and writers conjecture and fabricate in their minds to supply what is lacking and add what is incomplete—are not the losses of truth then already abundant indeed? Whenever I have examined the written records and the discussions of former Confucian gentlemen, my breast has never failed to be stuffed with numerous difficulties and my belly filled with a multitude of doubts. Let us tentatively raise one or two clear and easily judged cases to deliberate upon them. King Zhao of Yan 燕昭王 built a terrace to summon worthy men, and Yue Yi 樂毅 came from the state of Wei 魏. Before long he rose to the rank of Upper General (shang jiangjun), and jointly commanded the troops of Zhao 趙, Chu 楚, Han 韓, and Wei 魏 to attack Qi 齊. He successively captured more than seventy cities, yet Jimo 即墨 and Ju 莒 were not taken. Men of the past said that he came close to Tang 湯 and Wu 武, and also said that his fault lay in practicing the Kingly Way. When the Han …

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
昭烈三顧草廬諸葛亮以布衣起未
幾身都將相欲竭股肱忠正之節以
興漢壽止五十四歲而興復大業不
就昔人謂其亞匹管蕭又謂其非將
畧之長夫湯武與管蕭三尺之童亦
知其懸絶王道與將畧一藝之士亦
識其小大借使樂毅與孔明有優劣
高下優而幾湯武劣而亞管蕭相去
===
何遠歟高而行王道下而短將畧相
遠何甚歟雖然孔明養高隆中之日
嘗自比管仲樂毅而時人莫之許也
則是孔明自附太高而所謂不及樂
毅之言已出於當時而非獨後世矣
諸生博古待問於二人行跡熟之久
矣必舉其立論之人與所論之當否
而折衷以對毋徒諉曰知人其難
punctuated: 昭烈三顧草廬，諸葛亮以布衣起，未幾身都將相，欲竭股肱忠正之節以興漢，壽止五十四歲而興復大業不就。昔人謂其「亞匹管、蕭」，又謂其「非將畧之長」。夫湯、武與管、蕭，三尺之童亦知其懸絶；王道與將畧，一藝之士亦識其小大。借使樂毅與孔明有優劣高下，優而幾湯、武，劣而亞管、蕭，相去何遠歟！高而行王道，下而短將畧，相遠何甚歟！雖然，孔明養高隆中之日，嘗自比管仲、樂毅，而時人莫之許也，則是孔明自附太高，而所謂不及樂毅之言，已出於當時，而非獨後世矣。諸生博古待問，於二人行跡熟之久矣，必舉其立論之人與所論之當否，而折衷以對，毋徒諉曰「知人其難」！
translation_en:
… Emperor Zhaolie (Liu Bei 劉備) visited the thatched cottage three times, and Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮 rose from the status of a commoner. Before long, he personally held the offices of both general and chief minister, wishing to exhaust the loyal and upright integrity of a right-hand man in order to restore the Han; yet his lifespan reached only fifty-four sui, and the great enterprise of restoration was not accomplished. Commentators of the past have said that he was "a close match for Guan [Zhong 管仲] and Xiao [He 蕭何]," while others have said that "military strategy as a commander was not his strong suit."

Now, as for the disparity between Tang 湯 and Wu 武 on the one hand, and Guan Zhong and Xiao He on the other, even a child three feet tall knows how vast the gap is; and as for the difference in magnitude between the Kingly Way and military strategy, even a scholar of a single skill recognizes which is great and which is small. Supposing that Yue Yi 樂毅 and Kongming 孔明 (Zhuge Liang) did differ in superiority and inferiority, or in loftiness and lowness: if the superior one nearly matched Tang and Wu while the inferior one was merely second to Guan Zhong and Xiao He, how far apart they would be! And if the loftier one practiced the Kingly Way while the lower one fell short even in military strategy, how extreme the distance between them would be! Even so, during the days when Kongming was cultivating his lofty seclusion in Longzhong 隆中, he once compared himself to Guan Zhong and Yue Yi, yet none of his contemporaries granted him that. This would mean that Kongming placed himself too high, and that the verdict of his being inferior to Yue Yi had already emerged in his own time, and not only in later ages.

You students have broadened your knowledge of antiquity in readiness for questioning, and have long been familiar with the deeds of these two men. You must cite the authors of these assessments, evaluate whether their arguments are sound or not, and weigh them to arrive at a balanced judgment in your reply. Do not merely shirk the question by saying, "How difficult it is to truly know a person!"

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
問士之所尚誠實恬退推遜清廉而已
故古人之調美風俗崇重名節有不
緩於是也厥後有戒欺誕疾奔競之
詩有黜攘奪戒貪墨之舉故當時人
皆勵行丕振士風所謂白首事上不
忍見欺十九登第不忍增年不預宴
集直陳其情私入市肆直言其故此
誠實之風著矣年方強仕請解機務
===
年未知命表求掛冠父任執政不就
廷試禮部第一不肯自陳此恬退之
風盛矣至若試大名而讓人居先薦
萊州而謙已居次以至自謂駑朽請
薦相才自謂非材久妨賢路此推遜
之風然也位宰執而無地樓臺知成
都而屏去龜鶴以至歸自南海不載
一物歸自西蜀僅有數卷此清廉之
punctuated: 問：士之所尚，誠實、恬退、推遜、清廉而已。故古人之調美風俗、崇重名節，有不緩於是也。厥後有戒欺誕、疾奔競之詩，有黜攘奪、戒貪墨之舉，故當時人皆勵行，丕振士風。所謂白首事上，不忍見欺；十九登第，不忍增年；不預宴集，直陳其情；私入市肆，直言其故：此誠實之風著矣。年方強仕，請解機務；年未知命，表求掛冠；父任執政，不就廷試；禮部第一，不肯自陳：此恬退之風盛矣。至若試大名而讓人居先，薦萊州而謙已居次，以至自謂駑朽，請薦相才，自謂非材，久妨賢路：此推遜之風然也。位宰執而無地樓臺，知成都而屏去龜鶴，以至歸自南海，不載一物，歸自西蜀，僅有數卷：此清廉之
translation_en: Question: What scholars hold in esteem are nothing more than honesty, tranquil retirement, yielding deference, and incorruptibility. Thus, when the ancients harmonized and beautified customs and revered moral integrity, they did not treat these matters lightly. In later times, there were poems warning against deceit and falsehood and detesting competitive scrambling for advancement, as well as measures dismissing those who seized and contended and admonishing against greed and venality. Consequently, people of that era all strove to cultivate their conduct, greatly revitalizing the morale of the literati. As for those spoken of who served their sovereign until white-haired and could not bear to deceive him; who passed the examinations at nineteen and could not bear to inflate their age; who did not attend a banquet gathering and frankly stated their circumstances; or who privately entered the marketplace shops and forthrightly explained their reason—in these, the ethos of honesty was made manifest. Those who, just reaching the age of forty, requested to be relieved of crucial state affairs; who, before reaching the age of fifty, submitted a memorial asking to hang up their official cap; who, because their father held office as a chief councilor, declined to sit for the Palace Examination; or who placed first in the Ministry of Rites examination yet refused to put themselves forward—in these, the ethos of tranquil retirement flourished. As for yielding first place to another when examined at Daming, or modestly placing oneself second when recommended in Laizhou, and even calling oneself worn-out and useless while begging to recommend someone of ministerial talent, or declaring oneself lacking in ability and having long blocked the path of the worthy—such was the ethos of yielding deference. Holding the rank of Grand Councilor yet having no land for storied pavilions, serving as Prefect of Chengdu and setting aside even one's tortoise and crane, and even returning from the Southern Sea without carrying a single item in one's baggage, or returning from Western Shu with only a few scrolls—such was the [ethos] of incorruptibility…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
風爾也可歷舉其人而實之歟然是
四者則又以誠實為本故議之者則
以推遜恬退清亷者有是非得失真
偽於其間亦可舉其實而言歟此皆
君子律身之要諸士子必覽之熟矣
幸為我陳之
問人臣諫諍非一端也有直諫者有諷
諫者古人有犯顏逆鱗叩頭流血其
===
名曰直宜也而或疑其激和容愉色
微言婉辭其名曰諷宜也而或疑其
佞將置之而不言歟則有愧於其職
將言之而不顧歟則不免於譏議二
者將若之何而可古人有風采壁立
雖鼎鑊不避者謂非直諫可乎有旁
入曲諭雖風雅不過者謂非諷諫得
乎之數君子者上信其心下服其誠
punctuated:
風爾也。可歷舉其人而實之歟？然是四者，則又以誠實為本。故議之者，則以推遜、恬退、清亷者，有是非、得失、真偽於其間，亦可舉其實而言歟？此皆君子律身之要，諸士子必覽之熟矣，幸為我陳之。

問：人臣諫諍非一端也，有直諫者，有諷諫者。古人有犯顏逆鱗、叩頭流血，其名曰直，宜也，而或疑其激；和容愉色、微言婉辭，其名曰諷，宜也，而或疑其佞。將置之而不言歟，則有愧於其職；將言之而不顧歟，則不免於譏議。二者將若之何而可？古人有風采壁立，雖鼎鑊不避者，謂非直諫可乎？有旁入曲諭，雖風雅不過者，謂非諷諫得乎？之數君子者，上信其心，下服其誠，
translation_en:
… custom. Can you enumerate these individuals one by one and substantiate them? Yet among these four qualities, sincerity and honesty serve as the foundation. Therefore, those who discuss them maintain that among instances of yielding to others, quiet retirement, and pure integrity, there are distinctions of right and wrong, success and failure, and genuine and false. Can you also cite the facts and speak to this? These are all essentials of how a gentleman regulates himself. You scholars must have read about them thoroughly; please set them forth for me.

Question: The ways in which a minister remonstrates with his sovereign are not limited to a single mode: there are those who remonstrate directly, and those who remonstrate by indirect allusion. Among the ancients, there were those who braved the sovereign's displeasure and brushed against his "inverted scales," knocking their heads on the ground until blood flowed; that this is called directness is fitting, yet some suspect them of being overly strident. Others maintained a gentle countenance and cheerful expression, using subtle words and tactful phrases; that this is called indirect allusion is fitting, yet some suspect them of flattery. If one sets the matter aside and does not speak, one fails in one's duty; if one speaks out without regard for the consequences, one cannot avoid criticism. Between these two courses, how should one act so that it is acceptable? Among the ancients, there were those whose demeanor stood like a sheer cliff and who did not shrink even from the executioner's cauldron—could one say this was not direct remonstrance? And there were those who approached a matter sideways and persuaded by roundabout analogy, not surpassed even by the Airs and Odes of the Book of Songs—could one say this was not indirect remonstrance? As for these several gentlemen, their superiors trusted their intentions, their subordinates submitted to their sincerity, …

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天下後世知其忠何無一人以譏議
之歟然君聖則臣直今我
聖天子在上百僚庶尹皆知無不言言無不
盡何未見信其心服其誠而知其忠
也其果言者之激與佞歟抑別有其
說歟爾諸生抱藝而来皆將有官守
言責之寄者幸為我言之以觀適用
之學
punctuated: 天下後世知其忠，何無一人以譏議之歟？然君聖則臣直。今我聖天子在上，百僚庶尹皆知無不言，言無不盡，何未見信其心、服其誠而知其忠也？其果言者之激與佞歟？抑別有其說歟？爾諸生抱藝而来，皆將有官守言責之寄者，幸為我言之，以觀適用之學。
translation_en: … and all the world and later generations knew their loyalty—why is it that not a single person criticized them? Yet when the ruler is sagely, his ministers are forthright. Now our Sagely Son of Heaven reigns above, and the hundred officials and various directors all speak of everything they know and hold nothing back in their speech—why then do we not yet see their hearts trusted, their sincerity submitted to, and their loyalty known? Is it truly that those who speak are either overly strident or sycophantic? Or is there another explanation for this? You students have come bearing your learning and arts, and all of you will soon be entrusted with official posts or the responsibility of remonstrance. Please set forth your views for me, so that I may observe your practical learning.

text:
四書義
大宰問於子貢曰夫子聖者與何其多能也子
貢曰固天縱之將聖又多能也
林會
同考試官教諭鄭批此篇場中作者多於大宰所
問聖字直以生知安行為講此卷
獨以多能為聖深合本㫖録出以
為學者式
考試官教諭陳批文簡理精初考得之
===
考試官教諭張批體認親切可取
時臣以夫子之聖專乎藝大賢言夫子之聖兼乎藝
蓋多能乃聖人餘事耳然天縱聖德豈直多藝能而
已哉宜乎大賢推言以告時臣也昔大宰問於子貢
若曰惟聖多才夫子其聖者歟不然何其才之多至
於釣弋之類亦皆無所不通也惟聖多能夫子其聖
人歟不然何其能之多至於獵較之類亦皆無所不
通也大宰之問如此蓋以多能為聖舉末而遺本矣
子貢荅之意謂思而得者若天限量之也夫子則不

四書義。

「大宰問於子貢曰：『夫子聖者與？何其多能也！』子貢曰：『固天縱之將聖，又多能也。』」

林會。

考試官教諭陳批：文簡理精，初考得之。

時臣以夫子之聖專乎藝，大賢言夫子之聖兼乎藝。蓋多能乃聖人餘事耳，然天縱聖德，豈直多藝能而已哉？宜乎大賢推言以告時臣也。昔大宰問於子貢，若曰：「惟聖多才，夫子其聖者歟？不然，何其才之多，至於釣弋之類，亦皆無所不通也？惟聖多能，夫子其聖人歟？不然，何其能之多，至於獵較之類，亦皆無所不通也？」大宰之問如此，蓋以多能為聖，舉末而遺本矣。子貢荅之意，謂思而得者，若天限量之也，夫子則不
translation_en:
Expositions on the Four Books

"A Great Officer asked Zigong, 'Is the Master a sage? How is it that he has so many abilities?' Zigong replied, 'Certainly Heaven has endowed him without limit to be a great sage, and moreover he has many abilities.'" [Analects 9.6]

By Lin Hui 林會

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Zheng 鄭: In the examination hall, most candidates writing on this topic directly explained the word "sage" in the Great Officer's question in terms of knowing by birth and practicing with ease. This paper alone treats "having many abilities" as what the Great Officer meant by "sage," which deeply accords with the original purport of the passage. It is transcribed here to serve as a model for scholars.

Comment by Examiner Instructor Chen 陳: The writing is concise and the reasoning precise; it was selected in the first session.

Comment by Examiner Instructor Zhang 張: Its personal grasp of the meaning is intimate and fitting; it is worthy of selection.

A contemporary minister took the Master's sagehood to consist exclusively in skills, whereas the great worthy stated that the Master's sagehood encompassed skills as well. Indeed, having many abilities is merely a secondary matter for a sage; yet when Heaven endows someone without limit with sagely virtue, how could it merely be a matter of having many skills and abilities? It was fitting, then, that the great worthy extended his explanation to inform the contemporary minister.

In the past, the Great Officer questioned Zigong as if to say: "Only a sage has many talents; is the Master perhaps a sage? Otherwise, why are his talents so numerous that even in matters such as angling and shooting with a corded arrow, there is nothing he does not thoroughly understand? Only a sage has many abilities; is the Master perhaps a sage? Otherwise, why are his abilities so numerous that even in matters such as competing for game in the hunt, there is nothing he does not thoroughly understand?" Such was the Great Officer's question, for he took having many abilities to constitute sagehood, citing the branches while overlooking the root.
