title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
冠本房
考試官教諭陳批文理暢達宜居前列
考試官教諭張批辭理簡當宜冠本經
制服以有親而因其屬故用理以治親有其等此人
道莫大於親親也盖服以表其親屬而已苟不用仁
義以治之其何以知親屬之重輕哉此親親為人道
之大也有以夫昔記禮者謂人之有親則有服也彼
服有重者非徒重也以親而重之爾服有輕者非徒
輕也以親而輕之爾制服以有親豈有他哉盖親有
===
聯屬也如卑者幼者則以屬於尊與長者而服之親
有繫屬也如庶者旁者則以屬於適與正者而服之
夫親者屬也如此其可不用仁義以治親耶是故仁
主恩也用夫仁之恩愛依循於親節級而上至於祖
焉仁則父母重而祖輕也如至親以期斷而父母三
年不為仁重乎義主斷也用夫義之斷割依循於祖
順而下之至於禰焉義則祖重而父母輕也如高曾
應緦麻而進以齊衰不為義重乎夫以親屬而制服
用仁義以治親何莫而非親親哉故追王祭祀皆人
punctuated:
冠本房。
考試官教諭陳批：文理暢達，宜居前列。
考試官教諭張批：辭理簡當，宜冠本經。
制服以有親而因其屬，故用理以治親有其等，此人道莫大於親親也。盖服以表其親屬而已，苟不用仁義以治之，其何以知親屬之重輕哉？此親親為人道之大，也有以夫。昔記禮者，謂人之有親則有服也。彼服有重者，非徒重也，以親而重之爾；服有輕者，非徒輕也，以親而輕之爾。制服以有親，豈有他哉？盖親有聯屬也，如卑者、幼者，則以屬於尊與長者而服之；親有繫屬也，如庶者、旁者，則以屬於適與正者而服之。夫親者屬也如此，其可不用仁義以治親耶？是故仁主恩也，用夫仁之恩愛，依循於親，節級而上至於祖焉。仁則父母重而祖輕也，如至親以期斷，而父母三年，不為仁重乎？義主斷也，用夫義之斷割，依循於祖，順而下之至於禰焉。義則祖重而父母輕也，如高曾應緦麻，而進以齊衰，不為義重乎？夫以親屬而制服，用仁義以治親，何莫而非親親哉？故追王、祭祀，皆人
translation_en:
…top this examination ward.

Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: The writing and reasoning are fluent and clear; it deserves to be placed in the front ranks.

Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: The diction and reasoning are concise and apt; it deserves to top the essays on this Classic.

Mourning garments are instituted because one has kin and in accordance with their kinship connection; therefore, when principle is applied to regulate kinship, there are gradations, and thus in the Way of Man nothing is greater than affection for kin. Indeed, mourning garments merely serve to manifest one's kinship connections; if one does not apply benevolence and righteousness to regulate them, how could one know the relative weight of kinship connections? That affection for kin is the greatest part of the Way of Man is truly with good reason!

In the past, the recorder of the rites held that because men have kin, they have mourning garments. Where those garments are heavy, they are not heavy for no reason—they are made heavy on account of kinship; where those garments are light, they are not light for no reason—they are made light on account of kinship. When mourning garments are instituted because one has kin, is there any other reason than this? It is because kin have conjoint connections: for instance, the lowly and the young wear mourning by virtue of their connection to the noble and the elder; and kin have bound connections: for instance, those of secondary and collateral lines wear mourning by virtue of their connection to the primary heir and the main line. Now, since "kinship means connection" in this way, how could one fail to apply benevolence and righteousness to regulate kin?

Therefore, benevolence presides over grace. Applying the loving grace of benevolence, one follows from one's parents step by step upward until one reaches the ancestor. By benevolence, parents are weighty and the ancestor is light: for example, mourning for the closest kin is cut off at one year, yet for parents it is three years—is this not weighty on account of benevolence? Righteousness presides over decisive distinction. Applying the decisive distinction of righteousness, one follows from the ancestor in sequence downward until one reaches the deceased father's shrine. By righteousness, the ancestor is weighty and parents are light: for example, great-great-grandparents and great-grandparents ought to receive fine-hempen three-month mourning (sima), yet they are elevated to frayed-edge mourning (zishu)—is this not weighty on account of righteousness?

Now, instituting mourning garments on the basis of kinship connections, and applying benevolence and righteousness to regulate kin—what part of this is not affection for kin? Therefore, posthumously conferring kingly titles and offering sacrifices are all…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
道也而親親則為之大治道宗法皆人道也而親親
則為之先記禮者於大傳而言此其欲人慎重於親
親也何其至哉抑觀曲禮有曰夫禮者所以定親疎
决嫌疑別同異明是非也然彼則言制服以禮此則
言制服以仁義何耶盖仁者恩也義主斷也仁有殺
義有等即禮也學者合而觀之其意實互相發也
論
聖人教人有定本
王惟節
===
同考試官訓導郁批非特議論好而舜與孔子教
人定本發明殆盡
考試官教諭陳批論得甚竒筆勢不滯誠有學之
士也
考試官教諭張批議論精研筆力蒼古傑作也
論曰聖人之心天地之心也天地之心至公而
已矣聖人體天地之心亦至公而已矣何也天
地之生人欲其無一人而不歸於至化之中然
不能諄諄然而命之也於是篤生聖人以立教
punctuated:
道也，而親親則為之大；治道、宗法，皆人道也，而親親則為之先。記禮者於《大傳》而言此，其欲人慎重於親親也，何其至哉！抑觀《曲禮》有曰：「夫禮者，所以定親疎，决嫌疑，別同異，明是非也。」然彼則言制服以禮，此則言制服以仁義，何耶？盖仁者恩也，義主斷也；仁有殺，義有等，即禮也。學者合而觀之，其意實互相發也。

論
聖人教人有定本
王惟節
同考試官訓導郁批：非特議論好，而舜與孔子教人定本，發明殆盡。
考試官教諭陳批：論得甚竒，筆勢不滯，誠有學之士也。
考試官教諭張批：議論精研，筆力蒼古，傑作也。

論曰：聖人之心，天地之心也。天地之心，至公而已矣；聖人體天地之心，亦至公而已矣。何也？天地之生人，欲其無一人而不歸於至化之中，然不能諄諄然而命之也，於是篤生聖人以立教；
translation_en:
…the human Way, and showing affection for kin is the greatest part of it; the Way of governance and the lineage system are both the human Way, and showing affection for kin takes precedence in them. When the recorder of the rites spoke of this in the Great Treatise (Dazhuan), how supreme was his desire that people be prudent in showing affection for their kin! Moreover, if we look at the Summary of the Rules of Propriety (Quli), it says: "Now ritual is that by which one determines closeness and distance of kinship, resolves doubts and suspicions, distinguishes sameness and difference, and clarifies right and wrong." Yet why does that passage speak of instituting mourning garments through ritual, whereas this one speaks of instituting mourning garments through benevolence and righteousness? This is because benevolence is kindness, while righteousness governs decisive judgment; that benevolence has gradations of diminution and righteousness has degrees of rank is precisely what constitutes ritual. When scholars examine them together, their meanings actually illuminate each other.

Discourse
"The Sages Have a Fixed Foundation in Teaching People"
Wang Weijie 王惟節
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Yu 郁 comments: Not only is the argument good, but the fixed foundation by which Shun 舜 and Confucius 孔子 taught people has been elucidated almost exhaustively.
Examiner and Instructor Chen 陳 comments: The discourse is argued most remarkably, and the momentum of the brush is uninhibited; truly he is a scholar of learning.
Examiner and Instructor Zhang 張 comments: The argument is finely researched, and the strength of the brush is vigorous and antique; it is a masterpiece.

The discourse states: The mind of the sage is the mind of Heaven and Earth. The mind of Heaven and Earth is simply supreme impartiality; the sage embodies the mind of Heaven and Earth, and so is also simply supreme impartiality. Why is this? In giving birth to human beings, Heaven and Earth desire that there be not a single person who does not return within the fold of supreme transformation, yet they cannot instruct them with repeated words; therefore, they specially bring forth sages to establish teachings…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
故聖人之教人亦欲其無一人而不囿於至教
之内自非體天地至公之心能如是乎然其所
以教者亦各因其性分所固有職分所當為而
立為定本耳豈責之以高遠難行之事哉噫天
地之愛夫吾人也亦周矣既賦之以形又畀之
以性形欲其踐也性欲其盡也如此而後人道
盡也然而氣稟不齊形焉不能踐其形性焉不
能盡其性而失其所以為人之道者衆矣天地
於是而生聖人焉聖人之生豈徒然哉聰明睿
===
知厚以質也聖神文武厚以德也作之君師厚
以位也天地之厚於聖人非私也公也非公於
一家公於天下也非公於一世公於萬世也聖
人者出膺天地付託之重任君師教養之寄以
天下之人為吾一體以宇宙内事為吾分内三
綱於我乎維持九法於我乎推布百姓不親曰
吾之責也五品不遜曰吾之責也真能體天地
之心以教人者矣然其所以教者豈有他道哉
亦惟曰有定本而已夫古之教者有六禮七教
punctuated: 故聖人之教人，亦欲其無一人而不囿於至教之内。自非體天地至公之心，能如是乎？然其所以教者，亦各因其性分所固有、職分所當為，而立為定本耳，豈責之以高遠難行之事哉！噫！天地之愛夫吾人也，亦周矣。既賦之以形，又畀之以性。形欲其踐也，性欲其盡也，如此而後人道盡也。然而氣稟不齊，形焉不能踐其形，性焉不能盡其性，而失其所以為人之道者衆矣。天地於是而生聖人焉。聖人之生，豈徒然哉？聰明睿知，厚以質也；聖神文武，厚以德也；作之君師，厚以位也。天地之厚於聖人，非私也，公也；非公於一家，公於天下也；非公於一世，公於萬世也。聖人者出，膺天地付託之重，任君師教養之寄，以天下之人為吾一體，以宇宙内事為吾分内，三綱於我乎維持，九法於我乎推布。百姓不親，曰「吾之責也」；五品不遜，曰「吾之責也」。真能體天地之心以教人者矣！然其所以教者，豈有他道哉？亦惟曰有定本而已。夫古之教者，有六禮、七教、
translation_en: Therefore, when the sages instruct humanity, they likewise wish that not a single person should fail to be encompassed within their supreme instruction. Were it not for embodying the supremely impartial mind of Heaven and Earth, how could they act thus? Yet that whereby they instruct is simply to establish a fixed foundation for each person on the basis of what is inherent in their allotted nature and what ought to be done according to their allotted duty; how could they demand of people things that are lofty, distant, and difficult to practice? Ah! The love that Heaven and Earth bear toward us humans is indeed comprehensive. Having endowed us with physical form, they have also conferred upon us an inner nature. As for our form, they wish us to fulfill it; as for our nature, they wish us to develop it to the utmost; only when this is done is the Way of humanity exhausted. Yet endowments of vital energy are not uniform: having form, people are unable to fulfill their form; having nature, they are unable to develop their nature to the utmost; and those who lose the Way of what makes them human are many. Thereupon Heaven and Earth bring forth the sages. Is the birth of the sages in vain? Clear-sighted, discerning, and wise—they are generously endowed with natural qualities; sagely, inscrutable, accomplished, and martial—they are generously endowed with virtue; made rulers and teachers—they are generously endowed with position. That Heaven and Earth are generous toward the sages is not out of partiality, but out of impartiality; it is an impartiality not for a single family, but for all under Heaven; an impartiality not for a single generation, but for ten thousand generations. When the sages emerge, they receive the heavy trust of Heaven and Earth and take up the charge of ruling, teaching, and nourishing. They regard the people of all under Heaven as one body with themselves, and the affairs within the universe as their own responsibility. Through them the Three Bonds are maintained; through them the Nine Divisions of the Grand Plan are promulgated. If the hundred surnames are not affectionate toward one another, they say, "It is my responsibility"; if the five ranks of human relations are not compliant, they say, "It is my responsibility." Truly they are able to embody the mind of Heaven and Earth in instructing humanity! Yet as for that whereby they instruct, how could there be any other way? It is simply a matter of having a fixed foundation, and nothing more. Now, in the instruction of antiquity, there were the Six Rites, the Seven Teachings, …

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
八政矣又有三物四教矣而其所謂定本果在
於是乎盖六禮節此本也七教興此本也八政
防此本也三物達此本也四教明此本也非定
本也然其所謂定本者不外乎五品之人倫與
夫視聽言動之間而已然是本也非由外鑠我
也根原於太極之初具足於性分之內賢非豐
而愚非嗇也古非有而今非無也達非加而窮
非損也柰何伐於斧斤牧於牛羊塞於蓁茅失
其本者多矣故聖人立教因其父子之情薄而
===
或至於相夷也則教之以有親君臣之位失而
或至於相陵也則教之以有敬長幼之序或失
則教之以有序夫婦之道或虧則教之以有別
於朋友也則教之以有信焉聖人之所以教者
非耳提而面命之也振舉於上而下者自化焉
爾目司乎視而或非禮也則教以勿視耳司乎
聽而或非禮也則教以勿聽言焉非禮言之私
也則教以勿言動焉非禮動之私也則教以勿
動聖人之所以教者非家至而日見之也軌範
punctuated: 八政矣，又有三物、四教矣，而其所謂定本，果在於是乎？盖六禮節此本也，七教興此本也，八政防此本也，三物達此本也，四教明此本也，非定本也。然其所謂定本者，不外乎五品之人倫與夫視聽言動之間而已。然是本也，非由外鑠我也，根原於太極之初，具足於性分之內。賢非豐而愚非嗇也，古非有而今非無也，達非加而窮非損也。柰何伐於斧斤，牧於牛羊，塞於蓁茅，失其本者多矣。故聖人立教，因其父子之情薄而或至於相夷也，則教之以有親；君臣之位失而或至於相陵也，則教之以有敬；長幼之序或失，則教之以有序；夫婦之道或虧，則教之以有別；於朋友也，則教之以有信焉。聖人之所以教者，非耳提而面命之也，振舉於上而下者自化焉爾。目司乎視，而或非禮也，則教以勿視；耳司乎聽，而或非禮也，則教以勿聽；言焉非禮，言之私也，則教以勿言；動焉非禮，動之私也，則教以勿動。聖人之所以教者，非家至而日見之也，軌範
translation_en: …and the eight regulations of government; and there were also the three things and the four teachings. Yet did what is called the "fixed foundation" truly lie in these? In fact, the six rites regulate this foundation, the seven teachings arouse this foundation, the eight regulations of government safeguard this foundation, the three things carry this foundation into practice, and the four teachings illuminate this foundation—they are not themselves the fixed foundation. Rather, what is called the fixed foundation is nothing other than the human relationships of the five classes and the realm of seeing, hearing, speaking, and acting. Moreover, this foundation is not fused onto us from outside; it originates in the beginning of the Supreme Ultimate and is fully complete within our allotted nature. It is not abundant in the worthy nor stinted in the foolish; it was not present in antiquity only to be absent today; it is neither increased by eminent station nor diminished by obscurity. How is it, then, that when hacked at by axes and bills, grazed over by cattle and sheep, and choked by overgrown weeds, there are so many who lose their foundation? Therefore, the sage establishes instruction: because the affection between father and son may grow thin and perhaps even lead to mutual injury, he teaches them to have closeness; because the positions of ruler and minister may go amiss and perhaps even lead to mutual encroachment, he teaches them to have reverence; should the order between elder and younger be lost, he teaches them to have precedence; should the way of husband and wife be impaired, he teaches them to have distinction; and with respect to friends, he teaches them to have trustworthiness. The means by which the sage instructs is not by holding people by the ear and commanding them face to face; he simply uplifts these principles from above, and those below are transformed of themselves. The eyes govern seeing, and should what they see be contrary to ritual propriety, he teaches them not to look; the ears govern hearing, and should what they hear be contrary to ritual propriety, he teaches them not to listen; when in speaking one departs from ritual propriety, that is selfish speech, so he teaches them not to speak; when in acting one departs from ritual propriety, that is selfish action, so he teaches them not to act. The means by which the sage instructs is not by visiting every household and seeing people every day; he sets the model…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
於此而遠者自效焉爾由是天下之人雖知愚
異稟賢不肖殊科而凡沐浴於吾聖人膏澤之
中者莫不熈熈然敦義以相正也鼓舞於吾聖
人聲敎之內者靡不皥皥然謹禮以相與也百
姓昭明定本明也五典克從定本從也敎化無
窮定本之無窮也人徒見四方風動民協于中
以為聖人敎之使然也而不知天地生聖人篤
倫理以敎天下後世也人徒見天道以明人極
以建以為聖人敎之使然也而不知天地生聖
===
人明天理以敎天下萬世也聖人體天地之心
以敎天下後世則聖人之敎行即天地之敎行
也大哉聖人至公之心乎其與天地之心流通
而無間者乎稽之古人其克當乎此者唯大舜
與吾孔子為然大舜使契為司徒敎以人倫父
子有親君臣有義夫婦有别長幼有序朋友有
信夫子告顏淵曰克己復禮為仁非禮勿視非
禮勿聽非禮勿言非禮勿動朱晦菴有見於此
而曰聖人敎人有定本其言不我欺也其言不
punctuated: 於此而遠者自效焉爾。由是，天下之人雖知愚異稟、賢不肖殊科，而凡沐浴於吾聖人膏澤之中者，莫不熈熈然敦義以相正也；鼓舞於吾聖人聲敎之內者，靡不皥皥然謹禮以相與也。百姓昭明，定本明也；五典克從，定本從也；敎化無窮，定本之無窮也。人徒見四方風動、民協于中，以為聖人敎之使然也，而不知天地生聖人篤倫理以敎天下後世也。人徒見天道以明、人極以建，以為聖人敎之使然也，而不知天地生聖人明天理以敎天下萬世也。聖人體天地之心以敎天下後世，則聖人之敎行，即天地之敎行也。大哉聖人至公之心乎！其與天地之心流通而無間者乎！稽之古人，其克當乎此者，唯大舜與吾孔子為然。大舜使契為司徒，敎以人倫：父子有親，君臣有義，夫婦有别，長幼有序，朋友有信。夫子告顏淵曰：「克己復禮為仁。非禮勿視，非禮勿聽，非禮勿言，非禮勿動。」朱晦菴有見於此，而曰：「聖人敎人有定本。」其言不我欺也，其言不
translation_en: …in this place, and those who are far away naturally emulate it. From this, although the people of the world have different endowments of wisdom and folly and belong to distinct categories of worthiness and unworthiness, all who bathe in the rich grace of our sages without exception harmoniously cultivate righteousness to rectify one another; all who are inspired within the renown and teaching of our sages without fail contentedly observe ritual propriety in their dealings with one another. That the hundred surnames become illustrious is because the fixed foundation is made illustrious; that the five cardinal norms are adhered to is because the fixed foundation is adhered to; that moral transformation is inexhaustible is because the fixed foundation is inexhaustible. People merely see the four quarters moved as by the wind and the common folk brought into harmony with the Mean, and suppose that the sages' teaching made it so; yet they do not know that Heaven and Earth give birth to the sages to consolidate human moral relations in order to teach the world and posterity. People merely see the Way of Heaven made clear and the supreme standard of humanity established, and suppose that the sages' teaching made it so; yet they do not know that Heaven and Earth give birth to the sages to clarify Heavenly Principle in order to teach the world and ten thousand generations. When the sages embody the mind of Heaven and Earth to teach the world and posterity, then the flourishing of the sages' teaching is none other than the flourishing of the teaching of Heaven and Earth. Great indeed is the supremely impartial mind of the sages! Does it not flow in communion with the mind of Heaven and Earth without the slightest gap? Examining the ancients, those who could truly measure up to this were only Great Shun 舜 and our Confucius 孔子. Great Shun appointed Xie 契 as Minister of Education to teach human moral relations: between father and son there is affection; between ruler and minister there is righteousness; between husband and wife there is distinction; between elder and younger there is precedence; between friends there is trustworthiness. The Master told Yan Yuan 顏淵: "To subdue oneself and return to ritual propriety is humaneness. Do not look at what is contrary to ritual propriety; do not listen to what is contrary to ritual propriety; do not speak what is contrary to ritual propriety; do not do what is contrary to ritual propriety." Zhu Huian 朱晦菴 (Zhu Xi 朱熹) perceived this and said: "In teaching people, the sages have a fixed foundation." His words do not deceive us; his words do not…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄

在下之聖人也舜達而在上故其教行於當時
孔子窮而在下故其教行於萬世舜與孔子往
矣千載而下體天地之心以教夫人者今幸有
聖天子在上

translation_en:
…do not deceive me! Now, the Great Shun was a sage who achieved high station and ruled from above; Confucius was a sage who remained in obscurity and dwelt below. Because Shun achieved high station and ruled from above, his teachings were put into practice in his own time; because Confucius remained in obscurity and dwelt below, his teachings have been put into practice for ten thousand generations. Shun and Confucius are gone, yet a thousand years later, as for one who embodies the mind of Heaven and Earth to instruct all people, today we are fortunate to have the Sage Son of Heaven reigning above.

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
諫登賢俊以盈
朝偃武脩文重詞章於
內苑購遺文而山積幸
聖駕以時臨千載奇逢一朝
盛事此誠建億萬載太平之基業者也臣草茅賤
士樗櫟凡材遽承
紫殿之恩獲
賜玉堂之篆昔知諫院殊無陳善之能今任詞林
忝預登瀛之選舊階之榮已至
===
===
新命之眷奚堪自揣疎庸深懷戰懼恩如泉注慙
非陸贄之奇才官自氷銜徒冒彭年之美譽顧
涓埃之未答何
雨露之重霑臣敢不罄竭丹衷慎居清要掌
絲綸之出入謹
制誥之精嚴伏願
聖德中天日斯明而月斯朗
皇圖永曆山與峙而川與流共沐
洪休均承
punctuated: 諫，登賢俊以盈朝；偃武脩文，重詞章於內苑。購遺文而山積，幸聖駕以時臨。千載奇逢，一朝盛事，此誠建億萬載太平之基業者也。臣草茅賤士，樗櫟凡材，遽承紫殿之恩，獲賜玉堂之篆。昔知諫院，殊無陳善之能；今任詞林，忝預登瀛之選。舊階之榮已至，新命之眷奚堪？自揣疎庸，深懷戰懼。恩如泉注，慙非陸贄之奇才；官自氷銜，徒冒彭年之美譽。顧涓埃之未答，何雨露之重霑！臣敢不罄竭丹衷，慎居清要，掌絲綸之出入，謹制誥之精嚴。伏願聖德中天，日斯明而月斯朗；皇圖永曆，山與峙而川與流。共沐洪休，均承
translation_en: … remonstrances, elevates the worthy and talented to fill the court; laying down arms to cultivate letters, He prizes literary composition in the Palace Park. Searching out lost writings until they pile up like mountains, He graces them with the Imperial Presence from time to time. A rare encounter in a thousand years, a glorious event in a single morning—this truly lays the foundation for hundreds of millions of years of Great Peace! Your servant, a lowly scholar from the rustic wilds and ordinary timber like the ailanthus and scrub oak, has suddenly received the grace of the Purple Hall and been granted the seal-script inscription of the Jade Hall. Formerly administering the Bureau of Policy Criticism, I thoroughly lacked the ability to set forth what is good; now serving in the Forest of Letters, I unworthily participate in the selection of those who ascend Yingzhou. The honor of my former rank was already the utmost; how can I bear the favor of this new appointment? Examining my own crudeness and mediocrity, I am deeply filled with trembling fear. With grace pouring forth like a spring, I am ashamed not to possess the extraordinary talent of Lu Zhi; holding an office of ice-pure title, I merely usurp the fine reputation of Peng Nian [Chen Pengnian]. Considering that I have not yet repaid a single drop or grain of dust, how is it that the rain and dew of imperial favor moisten me once again? How dare your servant not exhaust his sincere loyalty, dwell cautiously in this pure and vital post, take charge of the issuing and receiving of silken imperial words, and carefully maintain the precision and solemnity of imperial decrees and patents of appointment? I humbly pray that the Sacred Virtue may stand at the zenith of Heaven, bright as the sun and clear as the moon; that the Imperial Enterprise may endure through eternal ages, towering with the mountains and flowing with the rivers; and that all together may bathe in the vast blessings and equally receive …

聖辟明君，繼統天位，而體元參化之功，先後同一道；天葩睿藻，昭布海宇，而垂訓立教之道，先後同一心。前乎堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武所以君師天下者，此心、此道也；後乎我朝列聖所以昭示海宇者，亦此心、此道也。請因明問而畧陳之。蓋人道之要莫大於五倫，故人君立教之道亦莫先於五倫。如堯之以親九族，舜之慎徽五典，禹之敷文命，湯之脩人紀，文王之緝熈

First Question

Lin Qiu
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Hua comments: The essay is well-structured and leaves out neither name nor reality; it is a fine policy essay.

Sacred sovereigns and enlightened rulers succeed to the heavenly throne, and their achievements in embodying the primal origin and participating in cosmic transformation follow one and the same Way from first to last; their heavenly blossoms of imperial writing are brilliantly promulgated throughout the realm, and their Way of handing down instructions and establishing teachings stems from one and the same mind from first to last. In earlier times, that whereby Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu acted as rulers and teachers to All under Heaven was this mind and this Way; in later times, that whereby the successive Sacred Emperors of our Dynasty have clearly instructed the realm within the seas is likewise this mind and this Way. Allow me to outline this briefly in response to the enlightened question. Now, the essentials of the human Way are no greater than the Five Relationships; therefore, the ruler's Way of establishing teachings places nothing ahead of the Five Relationships. Take, for instance, Yao's bringing harmony to the nine branches of the clan, Shun's cautiouslybeautifying the Five Constant Virtues, Yu's spreading abroad his cultural mandate, Tang's cultivating the human bonds, King Wen's continuing and brightening…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
敬止武王之重民五教何莫不以是為先務歟
洪惟我
朝誕膺
天命
列聖繼作文教大興
太祖高皇帝御製大誥三編
太宗文皇帝御製孝順事實為善陰騭二書以頒布
中外家傳人誦所以百年之間四海之内聲教
遠暨而人倫無不明矣伏遇
===
宣宗章皇帝光昭聖謨游心典籍又於萬幾之暇采
古今之嘉言善行有關於倫理者萃以成編名
曰五倫書而
英宗睿皇帝克承先烈頒布天下以示勸其立教垂
訓之意盖與堯舜禹湯文武之心
太祖
太宗之意寔同一揆也道豈異乎哉心豈二乎哉生
嘗欽誦所載君道之目五十而始於聖德聖學
以聖德言之其仁如天其智如神就之如日望
punctuated: 敬止，武王之重民五教，何莫不以是為先務歟？洪惟我朝誕膺天命，列聖繼作，文教大興。太祖高皇帝御製《大誥》三編，太宗文皇帝御製《孝順事實》、《為善陰騭》二書，以頒布中外，家傳人誦。所以百年之間，四海之内，聲教遠暨，而人倫無不明矣。伏遇宣宗章皇帝光昭聖謨，游心典籍，又於萬幾之暇，采古今之嘉言善行有關於倫理者，萃以成編，名曰《五倫書》；而英宗睿皇帝克承先烈，頒布天下以示勸。其立教垂訓之意，盖與堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之心，太祖、太宗之意，寔同一揆也。道豈異乎哉？心豈二乎哉？生嘗欽誦所載，君道之目五十，而始於聖德、聖學。以聖德言之：其仁如天，其智如神，就之如日，望
translation_en:
… resting in reverence, and King Wu’s emphasis on the Five Teachings for the people—which of them did not take this as their foremost task?

Reflecting upon our august Dynasty, having grandly received the Mandate of Heaven, successive sacred emperors have arisen one after another, and civil教 (moral and literary education) has greatly flourished. Emperor Taizu Gao (the Hongwu Emperor) imperially composed the Three Compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao sanbian), and Emperor Taizong Wen (the Yongle Emperor) imperially composed the two books Biographical Accounts of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi) and Secret Merits of Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi), promulgating them throughout the capital and the provinces so that every household transmitted them and every person recited them. Thus, over the course of a hundred years, within the Four Seas, the imperial prestige and teachings have reached far and wide, and there is no place where human moral relations have not been made clear.

Humbly encountering Emperor Xuanzong Zhang (the Xuande Emperor), who gloriously manifested sacred plans and immersed his mind in the classical canons: in his leisure from the myriad affairs of state, he further gathered fine words and virtuous deeds from antiquity to the present that pertained to moral principles, compiling them into a work entitled Book of the Five Relationships (Wulun shu). And Emperor Yingzong Rui (the Zhengtong/Tianshun Emperor), ably carrying on the meritorious enterprise of his predecessors, promulgated it throughout the realm to serve as an encouragement to virtue. The intention behind their establishing teachings and handing down instructions truly follows the exact same principle as the minds of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu, and the intentions of Emperors Taizu and Taizong. How could the Way be any different? How could the mind be divided into two?

Your student has reverently recited what is recorded therein: the categories under the Way of the Ruler number fifty, beginning with Sacred Virtue and Sacred Learning. Speaking of Sacred Virtue: he whose benevolence was like Heaven, whose wisdom was like a spirit, whom approaching was like the sun, and whom looking…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之如雲者堯也而克寛克仁克明克忠者非成
湯乎臨下以簡御衆以寛者舜也而不泄邇不
忘遠者非武王乎是雖有性之身之之殊要之
同一聖德之盛也以聖學言之受丹書於尚父
訪洪範於箕子者武王也開文學館而銳情經
術者非唐太宗乎舊學于甘盤惟克邁乃訓者
高宗也而雖在軍旅手不釋卷者非宋太祖乎
是雖有先後小大之殊要之同一聖學之勤也
臣道之目四十有八而始於輔德經國以輔德
===
言之毋怠毋荒四夷來王伯益之告舜者至矣
而周公作無逸之書賦大明之詩以戒成王者
心豈異乎脩德脩刑動天以誠宋璟之戒玄宗
者切矣而呂夷簡陳辨佞之言進節費之疏以
告仁宗者意豈異乎以經國言之决九川弼五
服大禹之功茂矣視召穆公之經營四方告成
于王寔同一轍焉辨方正位體國經野周公之
績偉矣視仲山甫之出納王命為王喉舌皆同
一軌焉包拯擢任舘閣戒犯贓濫而刻石三十
punctuated: 之如雲者，堯也；而克寛克仁、克明克忠者，非成湯乎？臨下以簡、御衆以寛者，舜也；而不泄邇、不忘遠者，非武王乎？是雖有性之、身之之殊，要之同一聖德之盛也。以聖學言之：受《丹書》於尚父、訪《洪範》於箕子者，武王也；開文學館而銳情經術者，非唐太宗乎？舊學于甘盤、惟克邁乃訓者，高宗也；而雖在軍旅、手不釋卷者，非宋太祖乎？是雖有先後、小大之殊，要之同一聖學之勤也。臣道之目四十有八，而始於「輔德」、「經國」。以輔德言之：「毋怠毋荒，四夷來王」，伯益之告舜者至矣；而周公作《無逸》之書、賦《大明》之詩以戒成王者，心豈異乎？脩德脩刑、動天以誠，宋璟之戒玄宗者切矣；而呂夷簡陳辨佞之言、進節費之疏以告仁宗者，意豈異乎？以經國言之：决九川、弼五服，大禹之功茂矣；視召穆公之經營四方、告成于王，寔同一轍焉。辨方正位、體國經野，周公之績偉矣；視仲山甫之出納王命、為王喉舌，皆同一軌焉。包拯擢任舘閣，戒犯贓濫，而刻石三十
translation_en:
… looked upon from afar as the clouds—such was Yao; and was he who could be magnanimous and benevolent, discerning and loyal, not Tang the Completer? He who oversaw his subordinates with simplicity and governed the multitude with寬 (leniency)—such was Shun; and was he who did not treat the near with familiarity nor forget the distant not King Wu? Although there is a difference between possessing virtue by innate nature and embodying it through personal cultivation, in essence they share the same flourishing of sagely virtue.

Speaking of sagely learning: he who received the Cinnabar Writing (Danshu) from Grand Father [Lü Shang] and inquired about the Great Plan (Hongfan) from the Viscount of Ji (Jizi) was King Wu; and was he who opened the Institute for the Advancement of Literature (Wenxue guan) and devoted himself keenly to classical scholarship not Emperor Taizong of Tang? He who formerly studied under Gan Pan and was able to advance diligently in his teachings was Gaozong [of Shang]; and was he who never put down a scroll even while on military campaign not Emperor Taizu of Song? Although there are differences of earlier and later, lesser and greater, in essence they share the same diligence in sagely learning.

The headings under the Way of the Minister number forty-eight, beginning with "Assisting Virtue" and "Ordering the State." Speaking of assisting virtue: "Do not be idle, do not be dissolute, and the four surrounding peoples will come to acknowledge your kingship"—the counsel that Boyi gave to Shun was utmost indeed; and when the Duke of Zhou composed the document "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi) and presented the ode "Greater Brightness" (Daming) to admonish King Cheng, how could his heart have been any different? Cultivating virtue and regulating punishments, moving Heaven through sincerity—the admonition that Song Jing gave to Emperor Xuanzong [of Tang] was earnest indeed; and when Lü Yijian set forth words on distinguishing flatterers and submitted memorials on curtailing expenditures to advise Emperor Renzong [of Song], how could his intention have been any different?

Speaking of ordering the state: dredging the nine rivers and establishing the five domains—the achievements of Great Yu were abundant indeed; compared with Duke Mu of Shao's bringing order to the four quarters and reporting completion to the king, they truly followed the very same track. Determining orientations and fixing positions, laying out the capital and demarcating the countryside—the accomplishments of the Duke of Zhou were magnificent indeed; compared with Zhong Shanfu's issuing and receiving the royal commands and acting as the king's throat and tongue, they all followed the very same course.

Bao Zheng, promoted to office in the Institutes and Pavilions, warned against committing the crime of venality and corruption, and had engraved on stone thirty-…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
七字以詔其子李襲譽解職揚州囊無餘蓄而
惟以賜田十頃桑千株以遺其後其所遺雖不
同而教子之心則同也父道不亦善乎伯竒見
逐於其母則采檸以食援琴以歌而不敢有怨
大舜不得於其親則往畊于田號泣于天而終
身怨慕其情雖不一而慕親之心則一也子道
不亦盡乎寧忤帝旨不以貴戚易陋妻尉遲敬
德於夫道善矣彼貞姬却白璧黃金之聘辭吳
王夫人之位而守節不渝者婦道何愧焉寧違
===
父命不以寵祿傷天倫叔齊於弟道盡矣彼餘
祭夷昧知季札之賢效泰伯之讓而秉德不回
者兄道何厚焉至若朋友之倫如雷義之於陳
重則相許以膠漆申屠蟠之於王子居則相托
以死生柳宗元之於劉禹錫鮑叔牙之於管夷
吾又皆友道之善而不以利害得失易其心者
也愚生游心校庠欽服
聖訓盖已有日而於五倫之教固將書諸紳而措諸
行矣徒誦說云乎哉徒誦說云乎哉謹對
punctuated: 七字以詔其子；李襲譽解職揚州，囊無餘蓄，而惟以賜田十頃、桑千株以遺其後。其所遺雖不同，而教子之心則同也，父道不亦善乎？伯竒見逐於其母，則采檸以食，援琴以歌，而不敢有怨；大舜不得於其親，則往畊于田，號泣于天，而終身怨慕。其情雖不一，而慕親之心則一也，子道不亦盡乎？寧忤帝旨，不以貴戚易陋妻，尉遲敬德於夫道善矣；彼貞姬却白璧黃金之聘，辭吳王夫人之位，而守節不渝者，婦道何愧焉？寧違父命，不以寵祿傷天倫，叔齊於弟道盡矣；彼餘祭、夷昧知季札之賢，效泰伯之讓，而秉德不回者，兄道何厚焉？至若朋友之倫，如雷義之於陳重，則相許以膠漆；申屠蟠之於王子居，則相托以死生；柳宗元之於劉禹錫，鮑叔牙之於管夷吾，又皆友道之善，而不以利害得失易其心者也。愚生游心校庠，欽服聖訓盖已有日，而於五倫之教，固將書諸紳而措諸行矣，徒誦說云乎哉？徒誦說云乎哉？謹對。
translation_en:
…seven characters to instruct his sons; when Li Xiyu 李襲譽 left his post in Yangzhou 揚州, his purse had no surplus savings, and he left behind to his descendants only ten qing of Imperially bestowed farmland and a thousand mulberry trees. Although what they left behind differed, their intention in instructing their sons was the same; was not their way as fathers admirable? When Boqi 伯奇 was driven away by his stepmother, he gathered pear blossoms [?] (ning 檸, for Location/花 [?]) to eat and took up the zither to sing, not daring to harbor resentment; when the Great Shun 大舜 could not win the affection of his parents, he went to plow in the fields, crying out and weeping to Heaven, yearning for them with contrition all his life. Although their circumstances were not identical, their hearts in yearning for their parents were one; was not their way as sons fulfilled to the utmost? Preferring to defy an imperial decree rather than exchange his humble wife for a noble kinswoman, Yuchi Jingde 尉遲敬德 excelled in the way of a husband; as for the Chaste Lady (Zhenji 貞姬), who declined betrothal gifts of white jade disks and yellow gold, refused the position of consort to the King of Wu 吳, and maintained her chastity without wavering, what shame had she in the way of a wife? Preferring to disobey his father's command rather than harm heavenly human relationships for the sake of favor and emolument, Shuqi 叔齊 fulfilled to the utmost the way of a younger brother; as for Yuji 餘祭 and Yimei 夷昧, who recognized the worthiness of Jizha 季札, emulated the yielding of Taibo 泰伯, and held fast to virtue without turning back, how generous they were in the way of elder brothers! As for the relationship of friends: in the case of Lei Yi 雷義 and Chen Zhong 陳重, they pledged themselves to each other as closely as glue and lacquer; in the case of Shentu Pan 申屠蟠 and Wang Ziju 王子居, they entrusted life and death to each other; and Liu Zongyuan 柳宗元 with Liu Yuxi 劉禹錫, as well as Bao Shuya 鮑叔牙 with Guan Yiwu 管夷吾, all exemplified excellence in the way of friends, never changing their hearts on account of advantage or harm, gain or loss.

Your foolish student has let his mind roam in the local schools and has reverently submitted to the Sage's instructions for some time now. As for the teachings of the Five Relationships, I shall certainly inscribe them upon my sash and put them into practice. Could it be a matter of mere recitation and discussion? Could it be a matter of mere recitation and discussion? I respectfully reply.

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第二問
梁建中
同考試官訓導周批〔隨問隨答畧無疑碍非老於性理者不能歆羨歆羨〕
同考試官訓導華批〔援據經傳條答詳明蓋嘗潜心於理學者〕
考試官教諭陳批〔據理條答畧無所遺〕
考試官教諭張批〔敷對無遺必博學之士也〕
文以載道而六經四書則萬世之至文也學以
===
明道而六經四書則萬世之正學也學者因文
以窮理窮理以明道則聖賢所載之微辭奥義
一以貫之而無疑矣請承明問而畧評之夫六
經四書之行于世猶日月星辰之麗乎天照臨
萬古光景常新而不可以一日無者也其間所
載遠而天理之精微近而人道之顯著幽而鬼
神明而禮樂廣大悉備誠未可以一二究其涯
涘姑以其大者言之故法象莫大於天地而有
陰陽剛柔之妙盖立天之道曰陰與陽立地之
punctuated:
第二問
梁建中
同考試官訓導周批〔隨問隨答，畧無疑碍，非老於性理者不能。歆羨，歆羨。〕
同考試官訓導華批〔援據經傳，條答詳明，蓋嘗潜心於理學者。〕
考試官教諭陳批〔據理條答，畧無所遺。〕
考試官教諭張批〔敷對無遺，必博學之士也。〕
文以載道，而六經四書則萬世之至文也；學以明道，而六經四書則萬世之正學也。學者因文以窮理，窮理以明道，則聖賢所載之微辭奥義，一以貫之而無疑矣。請承明問而畧評之。夫六經四書之行于世，猶日月星辰之麗乎天，照臨萬古，光景常新，而不可以一日無者也。其間所載，遠而天理之精微，近而人道之顯著，幽而鬼神，明而禮樂，廣大悉備，誠未可以一二究其涯涘。姑以其大者言之：故法象莫大於天地，而有陰陽剛柔之妙。盖立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之
translation_en:
Second Question
Liang Jianzhong 梁建中
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Zhou 周 comments: [Answers each point as it is asked, without the slightest hesitation or obstruction; none but one deeply seasoned in the philosophy of human nature and principle (xingli 性理) could do this. Admirable, admirable!]
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Hua 華 comments: [Cites the Classics and commentaries as evidence, replying point by point with detail and clarity; surely one who has immersed his mind in the Study of Principle (lixue 理學).]
Examiner, Instructor Chen 陳 comments: [Replies point by point on the basis of principle, leaving almost nothing out.]
Examiner, Instructor Zhang 張 comments: [Sets forth his responses without omission; he must be a scholar of broad learning.]

Literature serves to convey the Way, and the Six Classics and Four Books are the supreme literature for ten thousand generations; learning serves to illuminate the Way, and the Six Classics and Four Books are the orthodox learning for ten thousand generations. When a scholar relies on the texts to exhaustively investigate principle, and exhaustively investigates principle to illuminate the Way, then the subtle words and profound meanings recorded by the sages and worthies arethreaded together by a single unity without a doubt. Permit me to take up your enlightened question and briefly discuss it. Now, the circulation of the Six Classics and Four Books in the world is like the sun, moon, and stars arrayed in the heavens: shining down upon ten thousand ages, their radiance ever fresh, they are things the world cannot do without for a single day. As for what is recorded in them—distant, the subtle refinement of Heavenly principle; near at hand, the manifest clarity of the human Way; in the unseen realm, ghosts and spirits; in the bright realm, rites and music—all is vast, great, and completely provided, so that one truly cannot exhaust its bounds by enumerating one or two points. Let me tentatively speak of its greatest aspects. Thus, among modeling images there is nothing greater than Heaven and Earth, and they possess the wondrous mystery of yin and yang, firmness and softness. For in establishing the Way of Heaven, it is called yin and yang; in establishing the Way of Earth…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
道曰柔與剛一陰一陽而四時行焉一剛一柔
而四維定焉非天地之至妙者歟陰陽莫妙於
鬼神而不無大小費隱之别如晅之以日月潤
之以風雨是其大也而郊則天神格廟則人鬼
饗非小歟視弗見聽弗聞是其隱也而體物如
在非費歟惟皇上帝降衷于民所謂命也而其
吉凶禍福亦皆天之所命然惟莫之致而至者
乃為正命彼桎梏者豈正命耶成之者性各一
太極所謂性也而彼聲色臭味亦皆人之所有
===
然道則責成於己養則付命於天君子豈謂性
耶天命之性率循於已非道乎而所謂道一者
盖言古今聖愚本同一性初無二理也道二者
盖言能法堯舜則為仁不法堯舜則不仁也而
五達道則自君臣以至朋友之交是焉率性之
道實得於已非德乎而所謂三德者則孝德敏
德至德是也六德則智仁聖義中和是也而九
德則自寛而栗以至強而毅是焉立人之道曰
仁與義是人道莫大於仁義矣然分而言之則
punctuated: 道曰柔與剛，一陰一陽而四時行焉，一剛一柔而四維定焉，非天地之至妙者歟？陰陽莫妙於鬼神，而不無大小費隱之别。如晅之以日月，潤之以風雨，是其大也；而郊則天神格，廟則人鬼饗，非小歟？視弗見，聽弗聞，是其隱也；而體物如在，非費歟？惟皇上帝降衷于民，所謂命也，而其吉凶禍福亦皆天之所命，然惟莫之致而至者乃為正命，彼桎梏者豈正命耶？成之者性，各一太極，所謂性也，而彼聲色臭味亦皆人之所有，然道則責成於己，養則付命於天，君子豈謂性耶？天命之性，率循於已，非道乎？而所謂「道一」者，盖言古今聖愚本同一性，初無二理也；「道二」者，盖言能法堯、舜則為仁，不法堯、舜則不仁也；而「五達道」則自君臣以至朋友之交是焉。率性之道，實得於已，非德乎？而所謂「三德」者，則孝德、敏德、至德是也；「六德」則智、仁、聖、義、中、和是也；而「九德」則自寛而栗以至強而毅是焉。立人之道曰仁與義，是人道莫大於仁義矣。然分而言之，則
translation_en: … Way is called softness and firmness. With the alternation of yin and yang, the four seasons proceed; with the alternation of firmness and softness, the four corners of the earth are fixed—is this not the supreme subtlety of Heaven and Earth? In yin and yang, nothing is more subtle than ghosts and spirits (guishen), yet they are not without distinctions of great and small, of wide-reaching (fei) and hidden (yin). For instance, warming things with the sun and moon and moistening them with wind and rain—this is their greatness; whereas at the suburban sacrifice the heavenly spirits arrive, and in the ancestral temple the human ghosts enjoy the offerings—is this not their smallness? Looking for them and not seeing them, listening for them and not hearing them—this is their hiddenness; whereas embodying all things as if visibly present—is this not their wide-reaching nature? That the August Supreme Ruler sends down the moral sense to the people is what is called destiny (ming). Good and bad fortune, calamity and blessing, are likewise all ordained by Heaven; yet only that which comes without being brought on by oneself is true destiny—how could dying in fetters and handcuffs be true destiny? That which completes it is human nature (xing), each possessing a Supreme Ultimate (Taiji)—this is what is called human nature. Sounds, colors, odors, and tastes are likewise all possessed by human beings; yet since the Way requires fulfillment within oneself while physical nourishment is left to the decree of Heaven, how could the noble man call those things human nature? When the nature conferred by Heaven is followed by oneself, is it not the Way (dao)? What is called "the Way is one" means that sages and ordinary folk of past and present originally share the same nature, there being from the beginning no dual principle. "The Ways are two" means that if one can model oneself on Yao and Shun, that is benevolence (ren), and if one does not model oneself on Yao and Shun, that is non-benevolence. And the "five universal Ways" (wu dadao) are those extending from ruler and minister down to the fellowship of friends. When the Way of following one's nature is genuinely attained within oneself, is it not virtue (de)? What are called the "three virtues" are filial virtue, earnest virtue, and supreme virtue; the "six virtues" are wisdom, benevolence, sageliness, righteousness, centrality, and harmony; and the "nine virtues" are those extending from affability combined with dignity down to strength combined with fortitude. What establishes the Way of Man is called benevolence and righteousness; thus in the Way of Man nothing is greater than benevolence and righteousness. Yet if we speak of them separately, then…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
仁為陽為健義為陰為順錯而言之則義主於
斷而亦未嘗不健仁主於愛而亦未嘗不順也
大禮與天地同節大樂與天地同和是制作莫
大於禮樂矣然以言其本則和敬是已以言其
末則玉帛鐘鼓是已故敬而將之以玉帛和而
發之以鐘鼓則本物備具情文並行可謂全矣
苟玉帛交錯而敬或不足鐘鼓鏗鏘而和或不
及不已偏耶誠乃真實無妄之謂天理之本然
也學者未能真實無妄而欲其真實無妄非人
===
道之當然乎忠恕盡己推己之謂此學者之事
動以人爾而夫子之道一以貫之非動以天者
乎至若后非賢不乂賢非后不食是君臣誠人
道之大倫也而道德功力則皇帝王伯之辨以
無為為德而其道上達知足以帥人者則公卿
大夫之辨焉要其所各當盡之道則孔子所以
告定公者至矣父兮生我母兮鞠我是父子誠
天屬之至親也而正服義服則嫡繼慈養之别
而繼别繼禰則大宗小宗之别焉論其所各當
punctuated: 仁為陽、為健，義為陰、為順；錯而言之，則義主於斷而亦未嘗不健，仁主於愛而亦未嘗不順也。大禮與天地同節，大樂與天地同和，是制作莫大於禮樂矣。然以言其本，則和、敬是已；以言其末，則玉帛、鐘鼓是已。故敬而將之以玉帛，和而發之以鐘鼓，則本物備具，情文並行，可謂全矣；苟玉帛交錯而敬或不足，鐘鼓鏗鏘而和或不及，不已偏耶？誠乃真實無妄之謂，天理之本然也。學者未能真實無妄，而欲其真實無妄，非人道之當然乎？忠恕，盡己、推己之謂，此學者之事，動以人爾；而夫子之道一以貫之，非動以天者乎？至若后非賢不乂，賢非后不食，是君臣誠人道之大倫也。而道德功力，則皇帝王伯之辨；以無為為德而其道上達、知足以帥人者，則公卿大夫之辨焉。要其所各當盡之道，則孔子所以告定公者至矣。「父兮生我，母兮鞠我」，是父子誠天屬之至親也。而正服、義服，則嫡、繼、慈、養之别；而繼别、繼禰，則大宗、小宗之别焉。論其所各當
translation_en: … benevolence is yang and represents vigor, while righteousness is yin and represents compliance; yet if we speak of them in their interplay, righteousness centers on decisiveness and is thus never lacking in vigor, while benevolence centers on love and is thus never lacking in compliance. Great ritual shares the same regulation as Heaven and Earth, and great music shares the same harmony as Heaven and Earth; thus among cultural institutions none is greater than ritual and music. Yet if we speak of their root, it is simply harmony and reverence; if we speak of their branch tips, it is simply jade and silk, bells and drums. Therefore, when reverence is conveyed through jade and silk, and harmony is expressed through bells and drums, both fundamental substance and outward material are complete, and inner feeling and outer form proceed together—this may be called perfection. If, however, jade and silk are exchanged in abundance while reverence is perhaps insufficient, or bells and drums resound clangorously while harmony falls short, is this not already one-sided? Sincerity (cheng) means being true, real, and free of falsehood; it is the original state of Heavenly Principle. When a student is not yet able to be true, real, and free of falsehood, yet strives to become so, is this not the proper duty of the human Way? Conscientiousness and reciprocity (zhongshu) mean doing one's utmost and extending oneself to others; this is the business of the learner, moving by means of the human. Yet the Master's Way binds all together with a single thread—is this not moving by means of Heaven? As for the saying that "the sovereign without the worthy cannot govern, and the worthy without the sovereign cannot be supported," this shows that ruler and minister are truly a great relationship of the human Way. Moral Way, virtue, merit, and force mark the distinctions among Augustus, Emperor, King, and Hegemon; taking non-action as virtue so that one's Way reaches upward, or having wisdom sufficient to lead others, marks the distinctions among Dukes, Ministers, and Grand Masters. To sum up the Way that each ought to fulfill, what Confucius told Duke Ding is the ultimate statement. "O father, who begot me! O mother, who nourished me!"—this shows that father and son are truly the closest of Heaven-ordained kin. Proper mourning garments and righteous mourning garments mark the distinctions among the legal wife's son, the繼 (successor/stepmother), the慈 (foster mother), and the adoptive mother; while succeeding to the ancestor of a distinct lineage (jiebieli) and succeeding to the father's temple (jini) mark the distinctions between the great lineage (dazong) and the lesser lineage (xiaozong). If we discuss the mourning garments that each ought…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
為之服則諸儒所以載於禮記者詳矣凡若此
者信皆天理人道之大端而凡學者所當講也
第愚生天與凡近問學功疎而於道猶望洋惟
不鄙夷而進教焉則幸甚
第三問
林會
同考試官教諭鄭批博以備衆言公以折羣議對策
其殆學術正識見高而毀譽
不足以動其心者歟
===
考試官教諭陳批備紛紛之議論而以義利邪
正折其衷其博而能約之士也
考試官教諭張批不規規於問目而議論淵如
文彩燁如是必陋樂毅而志
孔明者
甚矣古人之難盡知也亦甚矣載籍之難盡信
也盖載籍浩浩論議紛紛或舉其一而遺其二
或具其事而畧其心卒至是非失真而古人之
賢否邪正莫之辨矣必考其時跡其事究其心
punctuated:
為之服，則諸儒所以載於《禮記》者詳矣。凡若此者，信皆天理人道之大端，而凡學者所當講也。第愚生天與凡近，問學功疎，而於道猶望洋。惟不鄙夷而進教焉，則幸甚。

第三問
林會
同考試官、教諭鄭批：博以備衆言，公以折羣議。對策其殆學術正、識見高，而毀譽不足以動其心者歟？
考試官、教諭陳批：備紛紛之議論，而以義利邪正折其衷，其博而能約之士也。
考試官、教諭張批：不規規於問目，而議論淵如，文彩燁如，是必陋樂毅而志孔明者。

甚矣，古人之難盡知也！亦甚矣，載籍之難盡信也！盖載籍浩浩，論議紛紛，或舉其一而遺其二，或具其事而畧其心，卒至是非失真，而古人之賢否邪正莫之辨矣。必考其時，跡其事，究其心，
translation_en:
… observe as mourning for them, what the various Confucian scholars have recorded in the Record of Rites (Liji) is detailed indeed. All matters such as these are truly the great fundamentals of heavenly principle and the human way, which all scholars ought to investigate. Yet I, a foolish student, am endowed by Heaven with ordinary and shallow capacities, my efforts in study and inquiry have been lax, and before the Way I still gaze out as if bewildered at the vast ocean. If only you do not disdain me as rustic and instead advance me with your instruction, I shall be most fortunate.

Third Question
Lin Hui 
Associate Examiner and Confucian Instructor Zheng comments: Broadly learned in setting forth the words of the many, and impartial in arbitrating the arguments of the crowd. Is the author of this policy essay not perhaps one whose scholarship is orthodox, whose insight is lofty, and whose mind neither slander nor praise is sufficient to move?
Examiner and Confucian Instructor Chen comments: Setting forth the welter of varied discussions and striking a balance among them by the standards of righteousness and profit, orthodoxy and perversity—he is a scholar who is broadly learned yet able to bring it back to essentials.
Examiner and Confucian Instructor Zhang comments: Not narrowly bound by the points of the question, his arguments are profound and his literary brilliance is resplendent; this must be a man who looks down on Yue Yi and sets his ambition on Kongming [Zhuge Liang].

Extreme indeed is the difficulty of fully knowing the ancients! And extreme indeed is the difficulty of fully trusting written records! For written records are vast and boundless, and discussions and opinions are confused and manifold: some cite one aspect while omitting another, and some recount the deeds while passing over the intentions, until in the end right and wrong lose their truth, and there is no way to distinguish the worthiness or unworthiness, the perversity or rectitude of the ancients. Only if one examines their times, traces their deeds, and investigates their minds…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
然後庶幾焉使不出此則雖同時而仕同堂而
語十人而書一人之事亦各不同蓋聞見有詳
畧文辭有工拙意向有高下坐此數者已多失
真矣況於數百載之下或千餘年之後耳不聞
其言也目不睹其事也意揣心構以補其所不
足而增其所未備則所以失其真者不尤多乎
哉是故觀載籍與儒先君子之論在執事猶衆
難填胷羣疑滿腹況於迂愚之左見乎請因明
問所及而陳之燕之樂毅下齊七十餘城而即
===
墨與莒不拔夏侯太初謂其庶幾湯武蘇子瞻
謂王道不可以小用小用之則亡而以其為行
王道之過且湯武所以伐人之國者曷嘗有利
天下之心哉不忍斯民之塗炭挾大義而拯救
之是以東征西怨南征北怨皆曰奚為後我使
取一毫之非義殺一介之不辜雖奉海內之籍
而歸之湯武不肯正目而視也王道蕩蕩大用
之則大治小用之則小治猶之菽粟不可少食而
不死恒食之則充實奚可以菽粟少食之則
punctuated:
然後庶幾焉。使不出此，則雖同時而仕、同堂而語，十人而書一人之事，亦各不同。蓋聞見有詳畧，文辭有工拙，意向有高下，坐此數者，已多失真矣。況於數百載之下，或千餘年之後，耳不聞其言也，目不睹其事也，意揣心構，以補其所不足，而增其所未備，則所以失其真者，不尤多乎哉？是故觀載籍與儒先君子之論，在執事猶衆難填胷、羣疑滿腹，況於迂愚之左見乎？請因明問所及而陳之。

燕之樂毅下齊七十餘城，而即墨與莒不拔。夏侯太初謂其庶幾湯、武，蘇子瞻謂王道不可以小用，小用之則亡，而以其為行王道之過。且湯、武所以伐人之國者，曷嘗有利天下之心哉？不忍斯民之塗炭，挾大義而拯救之，是以東征西怨，南征北怨，皆曰：「奚為後我？」使取一毫之非義，殺一介之不辜，雖奉海內之籍而歸之，湯、武不肯正目而視也。王道蕩蕩，大用之則大治，小用之則小治。猶之菽粟，不可少食而不死，恒食之則充實；奚可以菽粟少食之，則…
translation_en:
…only then can one come close to the truth. If one does not proceed in this way, then even when people serve in office at the same time and converse in the same hall, if ten men write down the deeds of a single person, each account will differ. For what is heard and seen varies in detail, literary expression varies in skill, and personal intentions vary in elevation; owing to these several factors, much of the truth is already lost. How much more so several hundred or over a thousand years later, when the ears do not hear their words and the eyes do not witness their deeds! When people conjecture in their minds and fabricate in their thoughts to supply what is lacking and add what is incomplete, are not the ways in which the truth is lost even more numerous? Therefore, in examining the written records and the discussions of former Confucians and gentlemen, if even Your Excellency has a breast filled with manifold difficulties and a mind brimming with a host of doubts, how much more so a pedantic and foolish person with his skewed views? Allow me to set forth my answer by following the points raised in your brilliant question.

Yue Yi 樂毅 of Yan 燕 captured more than seventy cities of Qi 齊, yet Jimo 即墨 and Ju 莒 were not taken. Xiahou Taichu 夏侯太初 (Xiahou Xuan 夏侯玄) said that he came close to Tang 湯 and Wu 武, whereas Su Zizhan 蘇子瞻 (Su Shi 蘇軾) said that the Kingly Way cannot be applied on a small scale—for if applied on a small scale it leads to ruin—and regarded this as the fault of his practicing the Kingly Way. Moreover, in attacking the states of others, how could Tang and Wu ever have harbored a desire to profit from the world? Unable to bear the people being plunged into mire and charcoal, they upheld great righteousness to rescue them. Thus, when they campaigned in the east, the west complained, and when they campaigned in the south, the north complained, all saying, "Why does he leave us to the last?" Had it required taking a single hair unrighteously or killing a single innocent person, even if the registers of all within the seas had been presented and submitted to them, Tang and Wu would not have deigned to look straight at them. The Kingly Way is broad and level: applied on a grand scale, it brings grand order; applied on a small scale, it brings small order. It is like beans and grain: one cannot eat even a little without being kept from dying of starvation, and if one eats them constantly, one becomes full and strong; how could one say that because eating only a little of beans and grain…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
寧啖糠粃哉彼樂毅生當戰國之時為魏使燕
因燕昭王好賢遂委質為臣未幾至上將軍時
齊最收怨於諸侯而燕昭怨之特甚故毅得以
承令而約趙楚韓魏與燕之兵併護之以伐齊
下齊之國都不能施仁敷惠以慰其父兄子弟
乃遷其重器寶貨於燕齊民固已怨入骨髓矣
毅之師特報讐圖利之舉耳幸而下七十餘城
畏其兵威刀屈而服之非心服也及兵威既振
所不下者即墨與莒毅之心以為在吾腹中一
===
指顧而取之有餘矣其心肆氣怠士剉而二城
之怨方堅齊民之心方奮用堅奮之人而禦怠
肆已剉之讐雖百萬之師固不能拔二城之人
非可拔而姑存之使自服也亦非愛其民而不
以兵屠之也湯武以一國征諸國而人靡有不
服者毅以諸國征二小邑且猶叛之湯武以義
而毅以利王道以正而霸以譎事之所以不同
也遠矣不知夏侯太初何自而謂其庶幾湯武
蘇子瞻何自而謂其行王道之過也漢之孔明
punctuated:
寧啖糠粃哉？彼樂毅生當戰國之時，為魏使燕，因燕昭王好賢，遂委質為臣，未幾至上將軍。時齊最收怨於諸侯，而燕昭怨之特甚，故毅得以承令，而約趙、楚、韓、魏與燕之兵，併護之以伐齊。下齊之國都，不能施仁敷惠以慰其父兄子弟，乃遷其重器寶貨於燕，齊民固已怨入骨髓矣。毅之師，特報讐圖利之舉耳！幸而下七十餘城，畏其兵威，刀屈而服之，非心服也。及兵威既振，所不下者即墨與莒，毅之心以為在吾腹中，一指顧而取之有餘矣。其心肆氣怠士剉，而二城之怨方堅，齊民之心方奮。用堅奮之人，而禦怠肆已剉之讐，雖百萬之師，固不能拔二城之人。非可拔而姑存之使自服也，亦非愛其民而不以兵屠之也。湯、武以一國征諸國，而人靡有不服者；毅以諸國征二小邑，且猶叛之。湯、武以義而毅以利，王道以正而霸以譎，事之所以不同也遠矣！不知夏侯太初何自而謂其庶幾湯、武，蘇子瞻何自而謂其行王道之過也？
漢之孔明，
translation_en:
…would one rather eat chaff and husks? That Yue Yi 樂毅 lived during the Warring States period. Serving as an envoy from Wei 魏 to Yan 燕, because King Zhao of Yan 燕昭王 loved worthy men, he presented a pledge and became his subject, before long reaching the rank of Upper General. At that time, Qi 齊 had incurred the greatest resentment among the feudal lords, and King Zhao of Yan resented it most bitterly. Thus, Yi was able to receive the command to form a pact with the troops of Zhao 趙, Chu 楚, Han 韓, Wei 魏, and Yan, combining and commanding them to attack Qi. Upon capturing the capital of Qi, he failed to practice benevolence and spread kindness to comfort its fathers, elder brothers, and younger brothers, and instead removed its precious vessels and treasured goods to Yan; the people of Qi already felt a resentment that penetrated to their very marrow! Yi's campaign was merely an act of avenging a feud and seeking profit! By good fortune he captured more than seventy cities, yet they submitted because they feared his military might and their strength [刀, for 力?] was exhausted, not because they submitted in their hearts. Once his military might had been displayed, the only places that had not fallen were Jimo 即墨 and Ju 莒. In his mind, Yi considered them to be already in his belly, more than easy enough to take at the point of a finger or the turn of a gaze. His mind grew lax, his spirit slackened, and his soldiers were blunted, whereas the resentment of the two cities was just then firm, and the hearts of the people of Qi were just then roused. Using firm and roused men to resist a slack, lax, and already blunted enemy, even with an army of a million, he certainly could not uproot the people of the two cities. It was not that they could have been uprooted and he temporarily spared them so they would submit of their own accord, nor was it that he loved their people and refrained from slaughtering them with troops. Tang 湯 and Wu 武 used a single state to punish many states, and there was no one who did not submit; Yi used many states to attack two small towns, and even so they rebelled against him. Tang and Wu acted out of righteousness while Yi acted out of profit; the Kingly Way uses rectitude while the Hegemon's Way uses deceit—the reasons why their affairs differed are vast indeed! One knows not on what basis Xiahou Taichu 夏侯太初 (Xiahou Xuan 夏侯玄) said that he came close to Tang and Wu, or on what basis Su Zizhan 蘇子瞻 (Su Shi 蘇軾) said that his fault lay in practicing the Kingly Way!
As for Kongming 孔明 (Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮) of the Han…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
志在恢復炎祚而大業未就以卒陳壽謂其亞
匹管蕭又謂其連歲動衆未能成功盖應變將
畧非其所長且管仲相桓公覇諸侯一匡天下
民到于今稱之功亦偉矣而乃不能正身脩德
以致主于王道蕭何輔高祖成帝業發蹤指示
而匡輔之功居多養民致賢而勸君之意尤切
烈亦盛矣而亦不能積誠法古以聿興夫禮樂
若吾孔明生當三國寄跡隆中漢之昭烈三顧
草廬幡然而起未幾身都將相是時吳為最強
===
魏次之而漢獨以區區之蜀間於二雄而欲信
大義於天下以復漢祖之炎祚其時其事尤為
難也然以布衣至於為相而人不以為速以討
賊為已任而不任將帥人不以為自用斷一國
之政賞罰予奪一無所貸人不以為專彼二國
之司馬懿周魯張陸之徒皆不能及顧乃深有
資於僚佐而懇懇求忠藎之言以孔明之賢豈
待乎僚佐之益舉全蜀之士豈復有出於孔明
智慮之右乎賢人君子之用心也遠而期望也
punctuated: 志在恢復炎祚，而大業未就以卒。陳壽謂其亞匹管、蕭，又謂其連歲動衆，未能成功，盖應變將畧，非其所長。且管仲相桓公，覇諸侯，一匡天下，民到于今稱之，功亦偉矣；而乃不能正身脩德，以致主于王道。蕭何輔高祖成帝業，發蹤指示，而匡輔之功居多；養民致賢，而勸君之意尤切，烈亦盛矣；而亦不能積誠法古，以聿興夫禮樂。若吾孔明，生當三國，寄跡隆中，漢之昭烈三顧草廬，幡然而起，未幾身都將相。是時吳為最強，魏次之，而漢獨以區區之蜀，間於二雄，而欲信大義於天下，以復漢祖之炎祚，其時其事尤為難也。然以布衣至於為相，而人不以為速；以討賊為已任，而不任將帥，人不以為自用；斷一國之政，賞罰予奪，一無所貸，人不以為專。彼二國之司馬懿、周、魯、張、陸之徒皆不能及，顧乃深有資於僚佐，而懇懇求忠藎之言。以孔明之賢，豈待乎僚佐之益？舉全蜀之士，豈復有出於孔明智慮之右乎？賢人君子之用心也遠，而期望也…
translation_en: …had his heart set on restoring the fiery mandate of the Han, yet died before the great enterprise was accomplished. Chen Shou 陳壽 said that he was a close match for Guan Zhong 管仲 and Xiao He 蕭何, and also said that although he mobilized the masses year after year, he failed to achieve success, probably because flexible military strategy was not his strong suit. Now, Guan Zhong assisted Duke Huan 桓公, established hegemony over the feudal lords, and brought order and unity to the realm, so that the people praise him down to the present day—his achievements were indeed great! Yet he could not rectify his own person and cultivate virtue so as to lead his ruler to the Kingly Way. Xiao He assisted Emperor Gaozu 高祖 in accomplishing the imperial enterprise; in pointing out the quarry and giving directions, his merit in assisting and supporting was the greatest, and in nourishing the people and attracting the worthy, his earnestness in exhorting his ruler was especially keen—his accomplishments were indeed magnificent! Yet neither could he accumulate sincerity and model himself on antiquity so as to bring about the flourishing of ritual and music. As for our Kongming 孔明 [Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮], he was born in the era of the Three Kingdoms and lived in seclusion at Longzhong 隆中. When Emperor Zhaolie 昭烈 of Han [Liu Bei 劉備] thrice visited his thatched cottage, he rose up decisively, and before long held in his own person the offices of both general and chief councillor. At that time Wu 吳 was the strongest, and Wei 魏 came next,[?] while Han alone, with tiny Shu 蜀 wedged between two mighty rivals, sought to make great righteousness prevail throughout the realm and restore the fiery mandate of the Han ancestors—both the circumstances and the undertaking were especially difficult. Even so, he rose from a commoner to become chief councillor, and men did not consider it too rapid; he took the suppression of the rebels as his own personal responsibility rather than delegating it to the generals, and men did not consider him self-willed; he decided the governance of the entire state, meting out rewards and punishments, giving and taking away without the slightest leniency, and men did not consider him autocratic. None of those in the other two states—men the likes of Sima Yi 司馬懿, Zhou Yu 周瑜, Lu Su 魯肅, Zhang Zhao 張昭, and Lu Xun 陸遜—could match him. Yet he relied deeply upon his staff and subordinates, and earnestly sought out loyal and devoted counsel. Given Kongming's worthiness, how could he have stood in need of the help of his subordinates? Among all the scholars in the entirety of Shu, how could there have been anyone who surpassed Kongming in wisdom and foresight? The minds of worthy men and noble men reach far, and their aspirations are…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
大常自見其不足而不見其有餘惟不自用其
才知也故能舉用天下之才智茍露其才智與
人角錙銖分寸以求勝則凡有才智者皆吾敵
也吾安得而用之哉至於出師一表無愧乎伊
訓說命之言八陣一圖彷彿乎黃帝太公之制
魏之司馬懿用兵如神筭無遺策每與孔明交
鋒動輒敗北是以其徒有畏之如虎之譏時孔
明孤軍遠出粮餉不繼懿以銳師大衆乗氣而
扞禦之猶狼狽如許至受巾幗婦人之服而不
===
敢出氣孔明既卒而懿追之姜維令楊儀反旗
鳴鼓若向懿者懿遂斂軍以退百姓為之諺曰
死諸葛猶走生仲達及懿行孔明營壘處所嘆
曰天下奇才也况五丈原之屯恩信行於中原
威畧震乎遠邇屯田積聚軍旅散於民居而皆
相安三代之兵若時雨孔明者庶幾矣故論諸
葛之出處可比伊尹正大之出處也諸葛之人
才可亞伊周王佐之大才也而其心則一於興
漢豈有一毫譎詐圖利之意哉特時事之難不
punctuated: 大，常自見其不足，而不見其有餘。惟不自用其才知也，故能舉用天下之才智。茍露其才智，與人角錙銖分寸以求勝，則凡有才智者皆吾敵也，吾安得而用之哉？至於《出師》一表，無愧乎《伊訓》、《說命》之言；八陣一圖，彷彿乎黃帝、太公之制。魏之司馬懿用兵如神，筭無遺策，每與孔明交鋒，動輒敗北，是以其徒有「畏之如虎」之譏。時孔明孤軍遠出，粮餉不繼，懿以銳師大衆，乗氣而扞禦之，猶狼狽如許，至受巾幗婦人之服而不敢出氣。孔明既卒而懿追之，姜維令楊儀反旗鳴鼓，若向懿者，懿遂斂軍以退，百姓為之諺曰：「死諸葛猶走生仲達。」及懿行孔明營壘處所，嘆曰：「天下奇才也！」况五丈原之屯，恩信行於中原，威畧震乎遠邇，屯田積聚，軍旅散於民居而皆相安。三代之兵若時雨，孔明者，庶幾矣。故論諸葛之出處，可比伊尹正大之出處也；諸葛之人才，可亞伊、周王佐之大才也。而其心則一於興漢，豈有一毫譎詐圖利之意哉？特時事之難，不
translation_en: … grand; he constantly saw his own inadequacies and never saw himself as having a surplus. Only because he did not rely solely on his own talent and wisdom was he able to employ the talent and wisdom of the entire world. Had he flaunted his talent and wisdom, competing with others over every tiny fraction to seek victory, then all who possessed talent and wisdom would have become his enemies—how could he have employed them? As for his single Memorial on Deploying the Army (Chushi biao), it is worthy of the words of the Instructions of Yi (Yi xun) and the Charge to Yue (Yue ming); his single Diagram of the Eight Arrays (Bazhen tu) closely resembles the systems of the Yellow Emperor (Huangdi) and the Grand Duke (Taigong). Sima Yi of Wei used troops like a god and planned without a single oversight, yet whenever he crossed swords with Kongming, he suffered defeat at every turn; for this reason his own followers mocked him for "fearing him like a tiger." At the time, Kongming led an isolated army far afield with grain supplies failing to keep pace, while Yi, with elite troops and a massive host, rode the momentum to defend against him; yet Yi was still reduced to such dire straits that he even received a woman's headdress and garments without daring to utter a breath of protest. After Kongming died and Yi pursued him, Jiang Wei ordered Yang Yi to turn the banners around and beat the drums as if advancing toward Yi, whereupon Yi pulled back his army and retreated. Because of this, the common people coined the proverb: "A dead Zhuge still puts a living Zhongda to flight." When Yi inspected the site of Kongming's camp and ramparts, he sighed and said: "Truly a wondrous talent under heaven!" Moreover, during the encampment at Wuzhang Plains (Wuzhang yuan), his grace and good faith spread across the Central Plains, and his majesty and strategy shook both near and far; while establishing military agricultural colonies and stockpiling supplies, his troops were interspersed among the civilian dwellings, yet all lived in mutual peace. The armies of the Three Dynasties were like timely rain, and Kongming came close to that ideal. Therefore, if one discusses Zhuge's withdrawal and engagement in public life, it can be compared to the upright and noble course of Yi Yin; if one discusses Zhuge's personal talent, it can rank second only to the great kingly-assistant talents of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou (Zhougong). And his heart was wholly devoted to reviving the Han—how could he have harbored even a hair's breadth of deceitful cunning or desire for personal gain? It was only because of the difficulties of the times and events, and…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不幸五十四歲而卒天不祚漢可勝嘆哉使其
不死則漢室可興禮樂有望矣彼陳壽之徒以
形跡成敗論人而比之為管蕭又謂應變將畧
非其所長所言之繆不攻而自破矣若論其極
則樂毅非管蕭之匹而孔明直亞伊周豈戰國
秦漢之士可及哉噫太初曲士不足論獨惜陳
壽蘇子之易其言耳此後世之論失其真者然
也若夫孔明養高隆中之日嘗自比管仲樂毅
而時人已莫之許盖孔明特主於撥亂繼絕一
===
時自寓之言耳豈不知二人而甘附之哉然惟
豪傑然後能知豪傑當時盖少孔明之儔故雖
自比管樂而人亦莫之許無足怪焉此又當時
之論失其真者然也雖然論人失真非獨古昔
也幸執事裁而表章之以示警策云謹對
第四問
林廷璋
同考試官訓導周批士風一策正欲觀學者趨向何如
此答詳於事實未復歸重於
punctuated:
不幸五十四歲而卒，天不祚漢，可勝嘆哉！使其不死，則漢室可興，禮樂有望矣。彼陳壽之徒，以形跡成敗論人，而比之為管、蕭，又謂應變將畧非其所長，所言之繆，不攻而自破矣。若論其極，則樂毅非管、蕭之匹，而孔明直亞伊、周，豈戰國、秦、漢之士可及哉！噫！太初曲士，不足論；獨惜陳壽、蘇子之易其言耳。此後世之論失其真者然也。若夫孔明養高隆中之日，嘗自比管仲、樂毅，而時人已莫之許。盖孔明特主於撥亂繼絕，一時自寓之言耳，豈不知二人而甘附之哉？然惟豪傑然後能知豪傑，當時盖少孔明之儔，故雖自比管、樂，而人亦莫之許，無足怪焉。此又當時之論失其真者然也。雖然，論人失真，非獨古昔也，幸執事裁而表章之，以示警策云。謹對。
第四問
林廷璋
同考試官訓導周批：士風一策，正欲觀學者趨向何如。此答詳於事實，未復歸重於
translation_en:
…unfortunately he died at the age of fifty-four. Heaven did not bless the Han—how can one sigh enough over this! Had he not died, the House of Han could have been restored, and there would have been hope for rites and music. People like Chen Shou 陳壽 judge men by outward traces of success and failure, comparing him to Guan Zhong 管仲 and Xiao He 蕭何, and further claiming that flexible military strategy was not his strong suit; the absurdity of their words collapses of itself without needing to be attacked. If we speak of the highest standard, Yue Yi 樂毅 was not the peer of Guan Zhong and Xiao He, while Kongming 孔明 (Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮) was directly second only to Yi Yin 伊尹 and the Duke of Zhou 周公—how could the scholars of the Warring States, Qin, or Han ever match him! Alas! A narrow-minded scholar like Taichu 太初 (Xiahou Xuan 夏侯玄) is not worth discussing; one only regrets that Chen Shou and Master Su 蘇子 (Su Xun 蘇洵 or Su Shi 蘇軾) spoke so carelessly. Such is how the evaluations of later generations lost the truth of the matter. As for the days when Kongming was cultivating his lofty retirement at Longzhong 隆中, he once compared himself to Guan Zhong and Yue Yi, yet his contemporaries did not grant even that. In truth, Kongming was simply focused on quelling chaos and continuing an imperiled line, so these were merely words by which he expressed his aspirations for the moment—how could it be that he did not understand those two men and gladly attached himself to them? Yet only a hero is capable of recognizing a hero. At that time there were few who were Kongming's peers, so even though he merely compared himself to Guan Zhong and Yue Yi, people still did not acknowledge it, which is hardly surprising. Such, again, is how the evaluations of his own time lost the truth of the matter. Even so, failing to grasp the truth in judging men is not unique to antiquity; I hope that Your Excellency will judge and highlight this to serve as an admonition and encouragement. I respectfully reply.

Fourth Policy Question
Lin Tingzhang 林廷璋

During the Three Dynasties and earlier, discussions of literati ethos were unheard of; after the Three Dynasties, discussions of literati ethos first became prominent. Indeed, that literati ethos was unheard of was because the customs of the age were simple and generous, and everyone wore virtue at their belt, so there was nothing to criticize or discuss; that literati ethos first became prominent was because the customs of the age grew daily more frivolous, and men were not like those of antiquity, so there came to be things that could be discussed. Allow me to base myself on your discerning question and briefly set this forth. Now, when a scholar is born between heaven and earth, how could it merely be a matter of speaking like a Confucian and acting like a Confucian, wearing a Confucian cap and dressing in Confucian robes? The reason he is truly so lies simply in prizing honesty, quiet retirement, deferential modesty, and incorruptible integrity. Therefore, the ancients spoke of "beautifying customs to make scholars know how to respect themselves" and "exalting reputation and integrity to make scholars know where to keep their minds," which is why they were so urgently devoted to this without delay. Thereafter, when Emperor Taizong of the Song composed poems to warn against deceit and absurdity, and Emperor Zhenzong composed poems to denounce opportunistic competition, how could scholars fail to be honest and quietly retiring? When the younger kinsmen of Li Fang 李昉 were dismissed to punish usurpation, and the descendants of Liu Wensou 劉溫叟 were recorded for appointment to warn against贪墨 (greedy corruption), how could scholars fail to be deferential and incorruptible? Thus at that time everyone strove to cultivate their conduct, greatly revitalizing the literati ethos. For instance, when Hu Su 胡宿 was Administrator of the Judicial Control Office, there was a Tax Overseer who fell short of his quota; someone tried to stop Hu from reporting it candidly, but His Excellency said, "I have served our Sovereign until my hair is now white; I cannot bear to deceive my ruler by even a hair's breadth." 故對君者晏殊也為宫官私入市飲亦直以貧
故對上者魯宗道也諸公制行如此非誠實之
風著乎錢若水為樞密副使以母老而請解機
務韓見素為監察御史厭奔競而表求致仕至
於舉進士以父執政而不就廷試者韓持國也
登黃甲以奏名第一而不肯自陳者范景仁也

之試大名而讓同郡之張覃為第一蔡公齊之
===

之除相曰臣以駑朽請薦相才之寇準焉杜祁
公之去相曰某以非材誠恐久妨賢路焉此則
數公之推遜者然也萊公之位宰相居家隘窄
而無地以起樓臺趙抃之知成都心存廉潔而
龜鶴尚猶屏去以至余靖為廣西安撫及歸也
而不載南海之一物焉沈倫為水陸轉運及回
也而惟有圖書之數卷焉此則數公之清廉者
爾也然是四者分而言之則有彼此之殊要而

translation_en:
… shame [?]; how could I deceive my sovereign?" As for the one who, while serving in an Academician-in-Waiting post (guanzhi), did not attend banquets and gatherings, and honestly answered his sovereign that it was because of poverty—that was Yan Shu 晏殊. And the one who, while serving as a palace official, privately went into the market to drink, and likewise honestly answered the Emperor that it was because of poverty—that was Lu Zongdao 魯宗道. With these gentlemen regulating their conduct in such a manner, was not the ethos of honesty and sincerity clearly manifest?

Qian Ruoshui 錢若水, serving as Vice Military Affairs Commissioner (Shumi fushi), requested to be relieved of his confidential duties on account of his mother's old age; Han Jiansu 韓見素 [Han Hu 韓琥], serving as Investigating Censor (Jiancha yushi), grew weary of the scramble for advancement and submitted a memorial asking to retire from office. As for the one who was recommended as a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) but declined to sit for the Palace Examination because his father was a Grand Councilor—that was Han Chiguo 韓持國 [Han Wei 韓維]; and the one who ascended the Imperial Roster (huangjia), having been ranked first on the submitted list of names, yet refused to step forward and declare himself when his name was called—that was Fan Jingren 范景仁 [Fan Zhen 范鎮]. With these several gentlemen establishing their minds in such a manner, was not the ethos of calm modesty and withdrawal flourishing?

As for Master Zhang Yong 張詠, when examined at Daming 大名, he yielded first place to Zhang Tan 張覃 of the same commandery; Master Cai Qi 蔡齊, when examined at Laizhou 萊州, yielded top ranking to his fellow villager Shi Fang 史方. Coming down to Bi Wenjian 畢文簡 [Bi Shi'an 畢士安], upon being appointed Grand Councilor, he said: "As a worn-out and useless servant, I beg to recommend Kou Zhun 寇準, who possesses the talent of a Grand Councilor." And Duke Qi of Du 杜祁公 [Du Yan 杜衍], upon leaving the post of Grand Councilor, said: "Being devoid of talent, I truly feared blocking the path of worthy men for too long." Such was the deferential yielding of these several gentlemen.

When the Duke of Lai 萊公 [Kou Zhun] held the position of Grand Councilor, his private residence was cramped and narrow, without even space to build a pavilion or terrace; when Zhao Bian 趙抃 administered Chengdu 成都, he kept his heart set on incorruptibility and purity, going so far as to put away even his pet tortoise and crane. Coming down to Yu Jing 余靖, who served as Pacification Commissioner (Anfushi) of Guangxi 廣西—when he returned, he did not carry back a single item from the southern seas; and Shen Lun 沈倫, who served as Overland and Waterway Transport Commissioner (Shuilu zhuanyunshi)—when he came back, he had only a few scrolls of books and charts. Such was the incorruptibility and integrity of these several gentlemen.

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
言之則以誠實為本然非誠實則三者不可虛
行矣且司馬公之辭翰林王安石之辭館職其
推遜一也議者以温公為是而荆公為非温公
之辭歸西洛荆公欲投老鍾山其恬退一也論
者以温公為得而荆公為失温公不事生產荆
公不自奉養均之為清廉也議者以温公為真
而荆公為詐何也重厚之士其處巳以誠好名
之士其處巳以不誠温公忠厚之士而荆公好
名之士也故有彼此習尚之殊又豈不關於誠
===
與不誠也哉此誠實者所以為三者之本也愚
也棲迹螢窓潜心蠹簡素思以名節存心嘗有
考於是矣茲承明問聊槩述是以對幸執事進
而教焉
第五問
王惟節
同考試官訓導郁批策有考據有斷制篇末數語
又能窺主司之意於言外舉而
措之必有大過人者當拭目以俟
punctuated:
言之，則以誠實為本。然非誠實，則三者不可虛行矣。且司馬公之辭翰林，王安石之辭館職，其推遜一也，議者以温公為是而荆公為非；温公之辭歸西洛，荆公欲投老鍾山，其恬退一也，論者以温公為得而荆公為失；温公不事生產，荆公不自奉養，均之為清廉也，議者以温公為真而荆公為詐。何也？重厚之士，其處巳以誠；好名之士，其處巳以不誠。温公，忠厚之士，而荆公，好名之士也。故有彼此習尚之殊，又豈不關於誠與不誠也哉？此誠實者，所以為三者之本也。愚也棲迹螢窓，潜心蠹簡，素思以名節存心，嘗有考於是矣。茲承明問，聊槩述是以對，幸執事進而教焉。

第五問
王惟節
同考試官訓導郁批：策有考據，有斷制，篇末數語，又能窺主司之意於言外，舉而措之，必有大過人者，當拭目以俟。
translation_en:
… [summed] up, sincerity and truthfulness are the foundation. Without sincerity and truthfulness, the other three cannot be practiced in vain. Moreover, when Sima Guang (司馬公, Duke Wen 温公) declined the Hanlin Academy and Wang Anshi (王安石, Duke of Jing 荆公) declined a post in the Historiography Institute, their modest yielding was the same, yet commentators considered Duke Wen right and the Duke of Jing wrong. When Duke Wen asked leave to retire to Xiluo (西洛) and the Duke of Jing wished to spend his old age at Mount Zhong (鍾山), their serene retirement was the same, yet critics considered Duke Wen to have succeeded and the Duke of Jing to have failed. Duke Wen did not concern himself with family property and the Duke of Jing did not indulge in personal comfort; both alike were incorruptible, yet commentators considered Duke Wen genuine and the Duke of Jing deceitful. Why is this? A man of gravity and generosity conducts himself with sincerity; a man fond of reputation conducts himself with insincerity. Duke Wen was a man of loyalty and generosity, whereas the Duke of Jing was a man fond of reputation. Therefore, does the difference in how their habits and inclinations are judged not also hinge upon whether they were sincere or insincere? This is why sincerity and truthfulness serve as the foundation for the other three virtues. I, in my simplicity, have dwelt by a firefly-lit window and immersed my mind in worm-eaten bamboo slips; I have long aspired to keep moral integrity in my heart and have examined these matters. Now, having received your enlightened question, I briefly outline this in reply, hoping that Your Excellency will bring me forward and instruct me.

Fifth Question
Wang Weijie (王惟節)

嘗謂人臣之進諫於君也貴有其道又貴有其
時何也有其道矣而時不至焉則諫或不行不
可也有其時矣而或道已失焉則諫或不切其
可乎哉然必有其道有其時而後諫可行也今
承執事發策而以諫諍為問是盖責望以古者
執節秉義之士而不以尋常目之也其用心抑
何厚耶請因明問而條陳之甚矣諫諍之多端
===
也有直諫者有諷諫者如石介之犯顏逆鱗叩
頭流血其名曰直宜也而或疑其激如趙公槩
之和容愉色微辭婉容其名曰諷宜也而或譏
其佞直既不可諷又不可君子於此將何為哉
愚嘗聞朱晦庵有云伊川之諫其至誠惻怛防
微慮遠既發乎愛君之誠其涵養善端培殖治
本又合乎告君之道皆可以為後世法此進諫

考試官教諭張批：隨問隨答，必有學之士也。
嘗謂人臣之進諫於君也，貴有其道，又貴有其時。何也？有其道矣，而時不至焉，則諫或不行，不可也；有其時矣，而或道已失焉，則諫或不切，其可乎哉？然必有其道、有其時，而後諫可行也。今承執事發策而以諫諍為問，是盖責望以古者執節秉義之士，而不以尋常目之也。其用心抑何厚耶！請因明問而條陳之。甚矣，諫諍之多端也！有直諫者，有諷諫者。如石介之犯顏逆鱗，叩頭流血，其名曰直，宜也，而或疑其激；如趙公槩之和容愉色，微辭婉容，其名曰諷，宜也，而或譏其佞。直既不可，諷又不可，君子於此將何為哉？愚嘗聞朱晦庵有云：「伊川之諫，其至誠惻怛，防微慮遠，既發乎愛君之誠；其涵養善端，培殖治本，又合乎告君之道。皆可以為後世法。」此進諫之有其道也。又嘗聞吕東萊有云：「諫之道有三難焉：曰遠，曰疎，曰驟。遠則勢不接，疎則情不通，…

I have held that when a minister presents remonstrance to his ruler, what is valued is having the proper way, and also having the proper time. Why is this? If one has the proper way, yet the time has not arrived, then the remonstrance may not be put into practice—this will not do. If one has the proper time, yet the proper way has already been lost, then the remonstrance may not be to the point—how could that be acceptable? Thus, only when one has both the proper way and the proper time can remonstrance take effect. Now, having received Your Excellency's policy question asking about remonstrance and admonition, this is surely because you expect of us what was expected of the men of antiquity who upheld integrity and grasped righteousness, and do not regard us as ordinary men. How generous indeed is your intention! Allow me to set forth my reply item by item in response to your enlightened inquiry.

How manifold indeed are the ways of remonstrance and admonition! There are those who remonstrate directly, and those who remonstrate by indirect suasion. For instance, Shi Jie 石介 braved the ruler's countenance and brushed against the dragon's inverted scales, knocking his head on the ground until it bled; to call this "direct" is fitting, yet some suspected him of being overly confrontational. Or again, Lord Zhao Gai 趙槩 maintained a harmonious countenance and pleasant expression, using subtle words and a gentle demeanor; to call this "indirect suasion" is fitting, yet some ridiculed him as flattering. If directness will not do, and indirect suasion will not do either, what then is a gentleman to do in this situation? I have heard that Zhu Huian 朱晦庵 (Zhu Xi 朱熹) once said: "In the remonstrances of Yichuan 伊川 (Cheng Yi 程頤), his utmost sincerity and earnest solicitude in guarding against the minute and taking thought for the distant future sprang from a genuine love for his ruler; and his nurturing of the beginnings of goodness and cultivating of the foundations of governance accorded with the proper way of counseling a ruler. Both may serve as a model for later generations." This is having the proper way in presenting remonstrance. I have also heard that Lü Donglai 呂東萊 (Lü Zuqian 呂祖謙) once said: "In the way of remonstrance there are three difficulties: being distant, being estranged, and being abrupt. When distant, one's position does not bring one into contact; when estranged, feelings are not communicated; …"

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
驟則理不究其言之不行也固也此又進諫之
有其時也夫君子之進諫亦惟盡其道恤□□
時之何如爾盖嘗求之古人矣有風力愈勁者
目曰擊鶻則王素其人也有廷争不回者稱為
殿虎則劉安世其人也此其風采焠立雖鼎鑊
不避者謂非直諫可乎因詩章而含規諷歐陽
脩之辭何婉耶因身疾而喻朝政呂獻可之章
何誠耶此其旁入曲諭雖風雅不過者謂非諷
諫得乎之數君子者發乎愛君之誠合乎告君
===
之道而又皆近者親者久任者此所以上信其
心下服其誠天下後世知其忠夫何有佞與激
之譏耶然君聖則臣直洪惟我
聖天子嗣登大寶首開言路其論治體而裨國事者
多見采納真億萬載太平之
主也然其間有未信其心而行其所言者豈有他哉
其即東萊所謂遠者疎者與驟者時不至焉者
也雖然此但言其時與勢爾以理言之則
愛
punctuated: 驟則理不究，其言之不行也，固也。此又進諫之有其時也。夫君子之進諫，亦惟盡其道，恤□□時之何如爾。盖嘗求之古人矣：有風力愈勁者，目曰「擊鶻」，則王素其人也；有廷争不回者，稱為「殿虎」，則劉安世其人也。此其風采焠立，雖鼎鑊不避者，謂非直諫可乎？因詩章而含規諷，歐陽脩之辭何婉耶？因身疾而喻朝政，呂獻可之章何誠耶？此其旁入曲諭，雖《風》《雅》不過者，謂非諷諫得乎？之數君子者，發乎愛君之誠，合乎告君之道，而又皆近者、親者、久任者，此所以上信其心，下服其誠，天下後世知其忠，夫何有佞與激之譏耶？然君聖則臣直。洪惟我聖天子嗣登大寶，首開言路，其論治體而裨國事者，多見采納，真億萬載太平之主也。然其間有未信其心而行其所言者，豈有他哉？其即東萊所謂遠者、疎者與驟者，時不至焉者也。雖然，此但言其時與勢爾，以理言之，則愛……
translation_en: … and if one acts abruptly, the principles cannot be thoroughly examined; that one's words are not put into practice is only natural. This means that presenting remonstrance also has its proper timing. In presenting remonstrance, a gentleman simply fulfills the proper way and takes heed of [?] what the timing is like. Indeed, I have sought examples among the ancients: there was one whose force of character grew ever more vigorous, who was eyed as a "striking falcon"—such a man was Wang Su 王素; there was one who argued at court without yielding, who was called the "tiger of the palace hall"—such a man was Liu Anshi 劉安世. With their bearing standing tempered and firm, not shrinking even from the cauldron, could one say that this was not direct remonstrance? Incorporating admonition and satire by way of poetic verses, how tactful were the words of Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩! Drawing analogies to court administration by way of physical illness, how sincere were the memorials of Lü Xianke 呂獻可 [Lü誨]! Approaching indirectly and persuading subtly, not surpassed even by the Airs (Feng 風) and Odes (Ya 雅) of the Classic of Poetry, could one fail to call this remonstrance by oblique allusion? These several gentlemen spoke from the sincerity of loving their ruler and conformed to the proper way of advising their ruler; moreover, they were all those who were close, intimate, and long in office. This is why the ruler above trusted their hearts, subordinates below admired their sincerity, and the world and later generations knew their loyalty—how then could there be any criticism of flattery or excess? Yet when the ruler is sagely, the ministers are forthright. Humbly reflecting on how our Sagely Son of Heaven succeeded to the Great Treasure, he first opened the avenues of speech; those who discuss the principles of governance and benefit state affairs mostly see their advice adopted—truly the Lord of ten thousandmyriad years of Great Peace! Yet if among them there are some whose hearts are not yet trusted and whose words are not yet put into practice, how could there be any other reason? It is simply what Donglai 東萊 [Lü Zuqian 呂祖謙] called being distant, estranged, or abrupt—cases where the timing has not yet arrived. Even so, this speaks only of timing and circumstance; if we speak of it in terms of principle, then… [love/cherishing?]…

title: 成化四年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄後序
天道至公而已矣
聖人法天立道亦至公而已矣
天道
聖德莫罄名言而皆不外乎一公下此
而中外臣鄰所以奉若
天道祗承
聖德者亦不外夫公焉爾公以治事則
===
===
事集公以治民則民安公以求賢
則賢才進然求賢最重進士一科
而是科之制置條格既周且備一
有不公弊將不可勝言矣成化戊
子之秋適賓興賢能之期先是提
督兩廣軍務左副都御史韓雍削
平羣盜愛民養士蓋公心也繼而
巡撫右副都御史陳濂拊循瘡痍
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄後序

天道至公而已矣，聖人法天立道，亦至公而已矣。天道、聖德，莫罄名言，而皆不外乎一公。下此而中外臣鄰所以奉若天道、祗承聖德者，亦不外夫公焉爾。公以治事則事集，公以治民則民安，公以求賢則賢才進。然求賢最重進士一科，而是科之制置條格，既周且備，一有不公，弊將不可勝言矣。

成化戊子之秋，適賓興賢能之期。先是，提督兩廣軍務、左副都御史韓雍削平羣盜，愛民養士，蓋公心也。繼而巡撫右副都御史陳濂拊循瘡痍，
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

The Way of Heaven is nothing other than utmost impartiality; the sages take Heaven as their model in establishing the Way, and that too is nothing other than utmost impartiality. The Way of Heaven and the virtue of the sages cannot be exhausted by words, yet neither goes beyond this single principle of impartiality. Below them, the means by which officials inside and outside the court conform to the Way of Heaven and reverently uphold the sacred virtue likewise do not go beyond impartiality. When one governs affairs with impartiality, affairs are accomplished; when one governs the people with impartiality, the people are at peace; when one seeks the worthy with impartiality, worthy talents advance. Yet in seeking the worthy, the most important channel is the metropolitan graduate (jinshi) examination category; and the institutional regulations and rules of this category are both comprehensive and complete. Should there be a single lapse of impartiality, the abuses would be beyond description.

In the autumn of the wuzi year of the Chenghua era [1468], the time arrived for recommending the worthy and capable as guests of the state. Prior to this, the Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and Supreme Commander of Military Affairs in Guangdong and Guangxi, Han Yong 韓雍, had pacified the bands of bandits, cherished the people, and nurtured the scholars—all out of an impartial mind. Subsequently, the Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator, Chen Lian 陳濂, comforted and cared for the war-weary and wounded…
